title: [BUG] Helper with TWO mechanism writes ($8000 select + $8001 data): argumentSurvivesPrologue anchors on firstSite, killing smb3's r7=27/26 (regressed by d612bff, not 788f09b)
description:
REGRESSION shipped on main by 788f09b (grm-2dr increment 1, pass-through wrapper helpers). Found
via grm-bj6; proven by human disassembly 2026-08-09. smb3's golden is the CORRECT baseline and is
deliberately unblessed.

THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: inside an MMC3 helper that performs BOTH halves of the two-write protocol,
argument recovery attributes the register-SELECT constant written to $8000 to the BANK field
written at $8001.

    ffc2:  LDA #$47 ; STA $0721 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $0720 ; STA $8001

$8000 takes the select/mode byte ($47 -> register 7, prg_mode 1); $8001 takes the bank, which
here comes from RAM shadow $0720, NOT from a register argument. Production now reports
r7 = $47 & $3F = 7.

PROOF, from the dump's own 'known:' bit fields:
    ca23 OLD  011011 = 27 = $1B      ca23 NEW  000111 = 7
    ca2e OLD  011010 = 26 = $1A      ca2e NEW  000111 = 7   (byte-identical to ca23)
    $47 & $3F = 7

CORROBORATION:
  - Two distinct call sites collapsing to ONE value = value taken from the helper's own constant.
  - Built-in control: c5f5/c9f7 are LDA #$47 ; STA $8000 ; LDA #$1a ; STA $8001 (direct, no
    shadow update) and are reported correctly as r7=26=$1A. So $1A is a real bank here and the old
    ca2e=26 is consistent; 7 matches no call-site constant anywhere.
  - The PRE-regression recovery had a correct mechanism: 'LDA #bank ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2' is
    grm-mu7's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource save-restore model reading the shadow. It worked.

BLAST RADIUS on smb3: refs.intoOverlay 846->822, instrs.inOverlay 4263->4173 (a 90-instruction
LOSS -- wrong bank retargets into a wrong/absent overlay), c631 gains a bogus 'r7=7? via FUN_ffc2',
f894 loses a bankcomment. Any MMC3 title whose helper carries both writes is exposed; smb3 is
simply where it was caught.

WHY IT PROBABLY BIT NOW: 788f09b re-keys a helper's model onto a predecessor, and
argumentSurvivesPrologue walks LINEARLY BY ADDRESS with no reference to function boundaries. Note
ffbf (JSR $ffd1, then FALLS THROUGH into ffc2) is address-contiguous with ffc2 and is exactly the
pass-through shape that pass admits. A linear walk that now starts earlier, or a model re-keyed
onto ffbf, can reach the LDA #$47 and treat it as the argument. THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS, not the
diagnosis -- confirm in code before fixing.

WHAT A FIX MUST PRESERVE: the select byte and the bank byte are DIFFERENT operands of the same
protocol. Recovering select=7,prg_mode=1 from $47 is CORRECT and must keep working; only its leak
into the r7 field is wrong. And when the bank genuinely comes from a shadow the caller wrote, the
shadow model must win -- silence is better than a confident wrong number.

ACCEPTANCE: smb3 realrom check PASSES against the CURRENT (unblessed) golden, i.e. ca23 r7=27,
ca2e r7=26, refs 846, instrs 4263, no bogus c631 comment. Then close grm-bj6. Do NOT bless smb3 to
make this green.

REPRO: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --only smb3 H:/emulators/nes/roms

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DIRECT PROOF AT THE CALL SITE, 2026-08-09 (human, follow-up to the trace above). The two call
sites are preceded by exactly the shadow-establishing idiom:

    ca23:  LDA #$1b ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2      ->  $1B = 27
    ca2e:  LDA #$1a ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2      ->  $1A = 26

That is no longer an inference. The old golden's r7=27 and r7=26 are literally the call-site
constants, recovered through shadow $0720 exactly as grm-mu7's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource
model is designed to do. The regression replaced two CORRECT, DISTINCT, call-site-sourced values
with one wrong constant lifted from the helper's own body ($47 & $3F = 7).

This also pins the shape of a correct fix. The recovery that must be restored is:
  caller writes an immediate to the argument CELL ($0720)  ->  helper reloads that cell  ->  helper
  stores it to $8001.
The value the fix must NOT follow is the immediate feeding the OTHER mechanism write in the same
helper body (#$47 -> $8000). Both writes are mechanism writes; only one carries the bank. Whatever
change 788f09b made to how the argument-bearing load is chosen, it now prefers the $8000 chain
over the $8001 chain, and the $8001 chain is the one that terminates in the caller's constant.

A fix that restores 27/26 by disabling wrapper recognition for MMC3 would be wrong for the same
reason: the target is picking the right one of two mechanism writes, not avoiding the helper.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLAME CORRECTED BY BISECTION, 2026-08-09. The regression is d612bff (grm-mu7, 'Decline a helper
argument the helper's own prologue clobbers'), NOT 788f09b. This bead's original 'why it probably
bit now' hypothesis is REFUTED -- do not spend time on it, and do not investigate ffbf's
pass-through admission, which is also cleared.

Bisection, each commit BUILT AND INSTALLED per-worktree rather than measured against a shared
install (the shared %APPDATA% install was stale and produced false reproductions at every commit
until each was built -- worth remembering for any future bisect in this repo):
    ce1dfc9 golden blessed              PASS
    c7278ae grm-hum arg recovery        PASS
    50f2c2c grm-nju thunks              PASS
    d612bff grm-mu7 prologue decline    FAIL, r7=7   <-- introduced here
    ea2df90 / 0083b3a / 788f09b / f8cd931            FAIL, r7=7
788f09b's diff never touches findHelpers, argumentSurvivesPrologue or recoverCallArgument.
d612bff's own commit message names the exact shape it was built for -- 'A helper that reloads the
bank from RAM breaks that assumption' -- which is precisely ffc2. It declined too much.

MECHANISM, as far as it is proven: findHelpers merges ffc2's two mechanism writes into ONE
HelperModel with firstSite = the SELECT write (STA $8000, min address) and switchSite = the DATA
write (STA $8001, max address). argumentSurvivesPrologue walks entry..firstSite, so it walks
ffc2..ffc7 -- which begins with LDA #$47 and therefore clobbers A immediately, and the guard
declines. That verdict is CORRECT for the select write and WRONG for the data write: the caller's
byte does survive to $8001, via LDA $0720 reloading the shadow the caller wrote. One firstSite
anchor cannot express 'this deposit's consumption point is switchSite, not firstSite' -- a
distinction that only arises for select-data's two-write shape, since register-write and
serial-shift helpers consume at firstSite genuinely.

STILL OPEN, and a fix must explain it: a declined argument yields UNKNOWN, which should surface as
a warning, not a confident value. Production emits r7=7 with ALL SIX r7 bits marked KNOWN. So the 7
arrives by some path other than a discarded argValue -- candidates being constState (line 685
serves helper.constState() at every call site, which would explain both sites collapsing to one
number), or StoredValueScanner resolving LDA $0720 to $47 (note the helper stores $47 to $0721
immediately before, and $0721 is ADJACENT to $0720). Under investigation.

DETERMINISM CONFIRMED, so single measurements are trustworthy here: two runs of
'check --only smb3' with separate REALROM_WORK_DIRs gave byte-identical dumps (fe66a525...),
matching grm-bj6's earlier two-full-set-run observation. smb3 is NOT part of the grm-4nr/grm-g73
bistable family; do not treat a single smb3 result as suspect.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FULLY DIAGNOSED 2026-08-09. It is a TWO-COMMIT INTERACTION, and the earlier
'blame d612bff' correction is itself half the story. Neither commit is wrong for the case it was
built for; together on a two-write helper they ship a confident wrong bank.

FIRST, the branch question is settled. I had doubted that ffc2's two writes reach findHelpers'
MERGE branch (:914) rather than its DEGRADE branch (:943), since a select write and a data write
own different bits. They DO merge, because effectMask does not come from the individual write --
BoardBankAnalyzer:675 constructs every SwitchResult with matchedMechanism.effectMask(), the
MECHANISM's declared mask, which is identical for both writes. So ffc2 gets ONE HelperModel with:
    firstSite  = STA $8000  (min address, the SELECT write)
    switchSite = STA $8001  (max address, the DATA write)
    argReg     = 'A', constState = null (the two sites' results disagree, so :915 nulls it)

STEP 1 -- d612bff (grm-mu7) LOST the correct value. recoverCallArgument:1744 runs
argumentSurvivesPrologue over entry..firstSite, i.e. ffc2..ffc7. The very first instruction is
LDA #$47, which clobbers A, so the guard declines. That verdict is RIGHT for the select write and
WRONG for the data write: the caller's byte does reach $8001, through LDA $0720.

    (Note how 27/26 were originally recovered -- not by any shadow model. The idiom
    'LDA #$1b ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2' leaves A STILL HOLDING $1b at the call, and argReg is
    'A', so the plain caller-register scan read it. Correct here, but only because the idiom
    happens to leave the value in A -- which is exactly the unsound assumption d612bff set out to
    kill, and Bionic Commando's FUN_dca8 is the case where it really is wrong.)

STEP 2 -- 0083b3a (grm-cxb) turned the loss into a confident WRONG value. It added
valueSuppliedInsideHelper (:2014), so a declined argument no longer stays unknown:
    recoverCallArgument:1746   local = valueSuppliedInsideHelper(program, helper, reg, stateMask);
and that method resolves the register AT firstSite (:2016-2024). For Kid Icarus's FUN_eb07 --
its motivating case, a serial-shift chain where every site carries the same byte -- firstSite is
exactly right. For ffc2 it reads A at STA $8000, which is $47, and the deposit then happens at
switchSite via SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy's odd/data branch: setFieldFromByte(empty, r7, $47),
and r7 is 6 bits wide, so $47 & $3F = 7. That is the confident 7, with all six bits known.

    So the earlier bisect line 'd612bff FAIL, r7=7' conflates two different failure modes.
    valueSuppliedInsideHelper did not exist at d612bff, so at THAT commit the sites should warn
    with an unknown bank, not report 7. The r7=7 signature can only start at 0083b3a.

STALE JAVADOC to fix alongside: recoverCallArgument's javadoc (:1719) still says a failure
'withholds argValue (leaving it unknown)'. 0083b3a made that false and did not update it -- which
is very likely why this went unnoticed.

THE GENERAL DEFECT, stated once: valueSuppliedInsideHelper resolves at firstSite while the deposit
consumes at switchSite. For every single-value mechanism those coincide, so the bug is invisible.
select-data is the first shape where one helper carries TWO mechanism writes with DIFFERENT
values, and there firstSite's value belongs to the OTHER write.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SOUNDNESS HALF IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED 2026-08-09 (NOT committed pending a decision, see below).

THE CHANGE. valueSuppliedInsideHelper read the argument register at firstSite; which site to read
is now the STRATEGY's call, because the two multi-site shapes want OPPOSITE answers:
  BankSwitchStrategy.suppliesHelperValueAtFirstSite()  default TRUE  -- unchanged for everyone
  SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy overrides to            FALSE         -- read at switchSite
A global switch to switchSite would have been wrong: serial-shift's Kid Icarus FUN_eb07 does
LDA #$0F / STA $9FFF / LSR A / STA $9FFF / ..., so the committed byte is live at the FIRST write
and the last write's A has already been shifted away. Also fixed recoverCallArgument's javadoc,
which still claimed a prologue decline 'withholds argValue (leaving it unknown)' -- false since
0083b3a, and very likely why this defect went unnoticed.

RESULT ON smb3: the confident wrong r7=7 is GONE. But the correct 27/26 do NOT come back, and
coverage falls further than the broken build's:
                    golden(correct)   broken     with this fix
  refs.intoOverlay        846           822          807
  instrs.inOverlay       4263          4173         4088
  bankComments            104           102          102
ca23/ca2e now produce NO comment at all. That is expected and is the honest answer for THIS fix:
the value at $8001 comes from LDA $0720, a RAM read, which is unresolvable from inside the helper
(the same decline Bionic Commando's FUN_dca8 gets, by the same rule).

SO THE FIX IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Restoring 27/26 needs a capability this engine does not
have: the caller writes the bank to shadow $0720 and the helper reloads it, so the value crosses
the call boundary THROUGH MEMORY. argumentCells/argumentReloadSource already model exactly this
save/restore shape but only WITHIN one helper body (BoardBankAnalyzer:1881-1971) -- a cell enters
the set when the HELPER stores to it. Here the store is in the CALLER. The missing piece is an
INBOUND argument cell: helper reloads reg from cell C before switchSite, C is never written inside
the helper, therefore C carries the caller's value; then resolve C's stored value at the call site
(LDA #$1b / STA $0720 -> 27). That is squarely grm-mej's charter ('everything still unrecovered
is unrecovered because the bank value passes through MEMORY or the STACK first').

COLLATERAL, and it needs a human. Full realrom --all: pass=22 fail=3 skip=6.
  smb3      expected, above.
  ff1       NOT mine -- refs +33 / instrs +44, count lines only, exactly grm-4nr's documented
            signature, and ff1 is MMC1/serial-shift which this change does not touch.
  rcransom  MINE, and unresolved. Two bank comments become two warnings:
              f1d0  'select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff07'  -> warning
              f21d  'select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff29'  -> warning
            Same board (MMC3), same strategy, same 'via FUN_xxx' shape, and the values were
            produced by the SAME firstSite path that shipped smb3's wrong 7 -- so the strong prior
            is that they were wrong or accidental too. But that is a prior, not evidence. Deciding
            it needs someone to read what ff07/ff29 do with their select and data writes; it is
            the identical question smb3's trace answered, on a title whose helpers grm-8iy.4
            already flags as having zero constant-arg call sites.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
HELD, NOT COMMITTED, 2026-08-09 -- user decision: nothing lands until rcransom's f1d0/f21d are read
by a human, because that measurement decides whether this change removes two WRONG comments or two
RIGHT ones.

The soundness change is in the working tree, uncommitted, and saved to build/grm-67g-soundness.patch
(gitignored, so it survives a clean checkout of tracked files but NOT a 'git clean -x'). Three files,
67 insertions / 7 deletions. It is reconstructable from scratch from the description in the previous
comment if the patch is lost -- it is small and the design rationale matters more than the diff:

  1. BankSwitchStrategy: new default method suppliesHelperValueAtFirstSite() returning TRUE, with
     the javadoc explaining why the two multi-site shapes need opposite answers (serial-shift's Kid
     Icarus FUN_eb07 re-derives by LSR from the first write; select-data's two writes hold different
     values).
  2. SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy: overrides it to FALSE.
  3. BoardBankAnalyzer.valueSuppliedInsideHelper: reads the register at firstSite or switchSite per
     that method instead of always firstSite. Plus the stale-javadoc fix on recoverCallArgument
     (:1719 still claimed a decline leaves argValue unknown -- untrue since 0083b3a, and probably
     why this was never caught).

DO NOT land it as-is on the assumption rcransom's two comments were artifacts. That is a strong
prior -- same board, same strategy, same firstSite path -- but the whole reason smb3 got a correct
verdict is that someone read the ROM instead of reasoning from shape. Give rcransom the same.

Gate before landing, whichever way rcransom goes: full realrom --all must show exactly the expected
set. Today it is pass=22 fail=3 skip=6, where ff1 is grm-4nr jitter (refs +33 / instrs +44, count
lines only, and ff1 is MMC1 so this change cannot touch it), smb3 is intended, and rcransom is the
open question.

title: Argument-marshalling wrappers that write no mechanism are not recognized as helpers (blmaster e61b, tmnt cea5, cv2 c183/c185)
description:
A BANK-SWITCH HELPER'S ARGUMENT IS OFTEN MARSHALLED BY A FUNCTION THAT WRITES NO MECHANISM.
Such a function is not a helper by the current definition, so calls into it never count as calls
into a helper and their adjacent immediates are never considered. Two hand-confirmed instances
in two titles, reaching the real helper by two different edges.

INSTANCE 1 -- blmaster FUN_e61b, reached by TAIL JMP (grm-8iy.5 section 2).

    caller: LDA #5  --JMP-->  e61b: STA $DB  --JSR e627-->  e63c: 5x STA/LSR $FFFF

  e61b writes no mechanism. It stores the argument to the $DB shadow and calls the real helper.
  TWELVE call sites reach it; five of them by JMP rather than JSR. Consistent with the probe
  reporting TALLY.mech tailCall=0 -- the tail calls land on e61b, which is not in the mech set.

INSTANCE 2 -- tmnt FUN_cea5, reached by FALLTHROUGH INTO ANOTHER FUNCTION (2026-08-06).

    cea5:  STA $21          ; FUN_cea5, two bytes, no mechanism write
    cea7:  <serial chain>   ; FUN_cea7, the actual helper

  Ghidra creates functions at BOTH addresses (confirmed), so cea5 is a complete function whose
  entire body is one store and whose only exit is falling through into cea7. SEVEN call sites
  reach it, every one carrying a non-home constant: LDA #1 (x3), LDA #6 (x2), LDA #3, LDA #4.

THE COMMON SHAPE: a function that (i) writes no mechanism itself, (ii) reaches a mechanism-writing
function with the argument register intact, and (iii) is what callers actually call. The EDGE
varies -- tail JMP, fallthrough, and grm-nju already handles thunks and one-instruction
trampolines -- but the definition gap is the same one each time.

  grm-nju (CLOSED)   thunks, one-instruction JMP trampolines      HANDLED
  blmaster e61b      multi-instruction function, entered by JMP   NOT HANDLED
  tmnt cea5          two-byte function, entered by fallthrough    NOT HANDLED

NOTE THIS IS WHY grm-8iy.3's RULING-OUT WAS MISLEADING. It used viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and
midBodyEntry=0 to conclude grm-nju's shapes could not explain cv2/blmaster/tmnt. Both numbers
were correct. Both measure only the two edges grm-nju implemented, so neither could ever report
these.

PROPOSED DIRECTION (not decided): widen the helper definition from "function containing a
mechanism write" to "function that reaches a mechanism write with the argument register
unmodified", following call, tail-call and fallthrough edges, bounded to a small number of hops.
The argument register must be tracked across the relay -- and grm-mu7's prologue-clobber guard
already exists for exactly the question of whether it survives.

CAUTION -- EACH WRAPPER HAS ITS OWN SEMANTICS AND THEY ARE NOT THE HELPER'S. blmaster e61b
writes the $DB shadow; tmnt cea5 writes the $21 shadow; the helpers they reach (e63c, cea7)
write no shadow at all. tmnt cea7 is separately callable and three sites do call it directly.
A model that collapses wrapper and helper into one signature gets the shadow side-effect wrong.

ACCEPTANCE: blmaster reports its twelve e61b call sites and tmnt its seven cea5 sites as calls
into a bank-switch helper, with the adjacent immediates recovered. Expect nine non-home banks on
blmaster (5, 2, and the ea41 path) and seven on tmnt (1, 1, 1, 6, 6, 3, 4).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CV2 IS A THIRD TITLE AND A FOURTH+FIFTH INSTANCE -- AND IT BREAKS THIS BEAD'S DEFINITION
(2026-08-06). Ghidra creates functions at c183, c185 AND c187 (confirmed). So cv2 is a wrapper
case, not a pre-body-entry case; grm-i7v is closed with no instances.

    FUN_c183:  STA $1C        ; forwards caller's A, writes the shadow   -> falls through
    FUN_c185:  LDA $1C        ; ESTABLISHES A from the shadow            -> falls through
    FUN_c187:  <serial chain> ; the real helper

TWO WRAPPERS STACKED, each a complete two-byte function, each reaching the helper by falling
through into the next function.

DEFINITION GAP THIS EXPOSES. This bead currently proposes "a function that reaches a mechanism
write with the ARGUMENT REGISTER UNMODIFIED". c185 fails that by construction -- it overwrites A
from $1C, which is its entire purpose. So a wrapper does one of TWO things and both must be
modelled:

  FORWARDING wrapper   passes the caller's argument through, possibly with a side effect
                       (blmaster e61b writes $DB; tmnt cea5 writes $21; cv2 c183 writes $1C)
  ESTABLISHING wrapper supplies the argument itself from memory, ignoring the caller
                       (cv2 c185 loads $1C; compare tmnt ced0/cf0b, which do the same as
                       separate non-fallthrough functions)

The recurring semantic triple across all three titles is set-and-remember / set-transient /
restore. Only the first two are forwarding; restore is always establishing.

INTERACTION WITH grm-mu7 -- CHECK THIS BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. grm-mu7's prologue-clobber guard
declines a helper argument when the helper's own prologue clobbers the argument register. c185
clobbers A by design, so the guard fires -- correctly by its own rule, wrongly in effect, since
the shadow load IS the value. grm-cxb ("fall back to the helper's own value when the caller's
cannot reach") is presumably what should take over. Confirm it does, or an establishing wrapper
will be silently declined rather than resolved.

UPDATED INSTANCE TABLE:
  blmaster e61b   forwarding, entered by TAIL JMP        12 call sites
  tmnt     cea5   forwarding, entered by FALLTHROUGH      7 call sites, all non-home constants
  cv2      c183   forwarding, entered by FALLTHROUGH     10 call sites (9x LDA #4, 1x LDA #0)
  cv2      c185   ESTABLISHING, entered by FALLTHROUGH    3 call sites (restores)
  tmnt     ced0   establishing, ordinary function         restores from $21
  tmnt     cf0b   establishing, ordinary function         restores from $59 (a read-back value)

THIRTY-TWO CALL SITES ACROSS THREE TITLES, all three of which currently resolve ZERO
instructions into overlay space. This is the largest single gap identified in the grm-8iy
cluster, which is why the priority is being raised.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE: blmaster reports 12 e61b sites, tmnt 7 cea5 sites, cv2 10 c183 sites, with
adjacent immediates recovered -- expecting non-home banks 5/2 on blmaster, 1/1/1/6/6/3/4 on
tmnt, and 4 (x9) on cv2. The establishing wrappers (cv2 c185, tmnt ced0/cf0b) additionally need
their shadow read (grm-mej.2) and are not required for a first increment.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WIZWARR IS THE FOURTH TITLE WITH THE FALLTHROUGH-WRAPPER STACK, ON A DIFFERENT BOARD FAMILY
(2026-08-06, from the wizwarr def-use pass on grm-8iy.5).

  ce8b  sets the AxROM register from A on entry, then clears VRAM at $2000   <- mechanism writer
  ce89  sets A to zero, then FALLS THROUGH to ce8b                            <- establishing
  ce84  sets A to #$10, CALLS ce8b, then FALLS THROUGH to ce89                <- forwarding

Structurally identical to cv2's c183/c185/c187. The PAYOFF here is nil -- the values carried are
VRAM page bits at bank 0, not bank selections -- so wizwarr does not add call sites to this
bead's count.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING ANYWAY: wizwarr is AxROM, not MMC1. The first three instances
(blmaster, cv2, tmnt) are all MMC1 serial-shift boards, which left open whether the wrapper stack
was an artifact of that mechanism -- a five-write chain is bulky enough that sharing a tail is
worth the trouble. ce8b is a SINGLE-WRITE latch and the idiom appears anyway. So this is a
general 6502 code-organisation habit, not an MMC1 consequence, and a fix should not be scoped to
serial-shift boards.

Also note ce84 is currently reached only from RESET. Other callers may exist behind grm-k5m (the
undisassembled RAM-resident routines) or grm-pfp (the entry point hidden inside a BIT operand),
so wizwarr's contribution here should be re-counted once those land.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 1 LANDED 2026-08-08 -- pass-through (fallthrough) wrappers only. Bead stays OPEN for
increment 2 (the blmaster call edge); see the end.

=== WHAT SHIPPED ===

BoardBankAnalyzer only, NO existing method body changed:
  - findPassThroughWrappers(program, helpers, switchResults), run AFTER composeTailCalls, so a
    wrapper inherits the composed model. Rounds over a List.copyOf snapshot (determinism),
    capped by MAX_WRAPPER_CHAIN = 3; termination is structural, the cap is policy.
  - isPassThroughInto(...), package-private static so JUnit can pin it. Six conditions: single
    contiguous body starting at the entry; every instruction disassembled, zero flows (which
    excludes JSR and therefore blmaster BY CONSTRUCTION), not terminal, and its fallthrough
    equal to getMaxAddress().next() (the OVERRIDE check); no switchResults key in the body; and
    the walk lands exactly on the target.
  - HelperModel.atFallThroughWrapper(wrapper) -- function is the WRAPPER (helperLabel :1212
    compares entry against function.getEntryPoint(), so keeping the helper there would have
    rendered a false "mid-body entry in ..."), constState INHERITED as an identity: the
    admission predicate proves the wrapper body changes no tracked bank bit.

WHY IT NEEDED NO OTHER CHANGES: argumentSurvivesPrologue walks LINEARLY BY ADDRESS with no
reference to function boundaries, so re-keying entry onto a contiguous wrapper makes that one
existing walk cover the wrapper body plus the helper prologue. cv2's STA $1C / LDA $1C pair is
load-bearing rather than incidental -- without grm-mu7 increment 2's memory save/restore model
the LDA reads as a plain clobber and nothing resolves.

A SOUNDNESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING (verified against the Ghidra source, now in the javadoc): Ghidra
function bodies CANNOT OVERLAP -- createFunction and setFunctionBody both convert an
OverlappingNamespaceException into an OverlappingFunctionException. Body assignment is
first-come-claims-it, so a wrapper's body is guaranteed clipped at or before the target and
bounding the walk by getBody() is safe. The same rule is why grm-78b is this bead's mirror
image: whether a fallthrough chain surfaces as ONE function or as WRAPPER PLUS HELPER is decided
purely by what got created first. Separately: the DECOMPILER is not bounded by function bodies
at all (Funcdata::startProcessing calls followFlow over the whole address space), so decompiler
output is not evidence about where a body ends.

=== TESTS ===

Tier 2: new HelperWrapperProgramTest (9 cases -- 2 admit, 7 reject: JSR in body, conditional
branch, RTS-terminal, disassembly gap, overshoot, fragmented body, fallthrough override). The
last two carry explicit anti-vacuity assertions that the fixture really is in the intended state
first. Plus one HelperPrologueProgramTest case over cv2's exact byte sequence. 30/30 pass.

Tier 3: new neswrappertest fixture (W1-W13), deliberately SEPARATE from nesmmc1test so that
golden stays byte-identical and readable as a pure regression signal. Includes both negative
controls -- a JSR-bodied predecessor and an RTS-terminal predecessor, each adjacent to a real
helper -- and direct calls to every helper proving the negatives fail on their own shape rather
than because their neighbour is broken. Full gate: SUITE OK, and ALL 45 pre-existing goldens
unchanged. That is itself the finding this fixture exists to fix: the synthetic tier structurally
cannot see this class of change, which is how grm-mu7 regressed three real ROMs while green.

=== REAL-ROM RESULTS (19 GME titles) ===

  title      refs.intoOverlay  instrs.inOverlay  bankComments  warnings
  tmnt            0 ->   44        0 ->  103       10 -> 18      31 (=)
  ultimaav      175 ->  225      678 ->  867        1 ->  8      27 -> 33
  cv2             0 ->    1        0 ->    8        2 ->  4      24 -> 26
  rcransom        0 (=)            0 (=)           38 -> 40       5 ->  3
  wizwarr         0 (=)            0 (=)           15 (=)         5 ->  7
  zelda2          =                =                =            27 -> 31
  lifeforce       =                =                =             3 ->  6
  blmaster, kicarus, dodge, megaman, and the rest: BYTE-IDENTICAL

NOTHING DECREASED ANYWHERE. Seven goldens blessed.

TMNT IS THE HEADLINE and matches the hand prediction: +8 bank comments against 7 predicted
non-home sites at cea5, and the title goes from zero to 103 instructions in overlay space.

ULTIMAAV WAS NOT PREDICTED and is the better news: two wrappers nobody had traced by hand,
FUN_f331 (5 new comments) and FUN_f313 (2), worth +189 overlay instructions. The rule
generalising past the four hand-traced titles is the point.

WIZWARR BEHAVED EXACTLY AS PREDICTED, including the non-result: ce89 admitted (2 honest
declines, payoff nil because its values are VRAM page bits at bank 0), ce84 NOT admitted because
its body contains a JSR. wizwarr is AxROM, so this is the cross-board-family check that the rule
is not an MMC1 artifact. It passed.

ZELDA2 / LIFEFORCE / WIZWARR warning rises are all the same shape and all honest: newly-admitted
wrappers (FUN_ffc9; FUN_e618/FUN_e619; FUN_ce89) whose arguments do not resolve, so a previously
SILENT miss became a conservative one. Nothing was lost -- bankComments, refs and instrs are
unchanged on all three. Same side effect grm-nju documented.

FF1 IS THE KNOWN FLAKE, NOT A REGRESSION, and this was demonstrated rather than assumed. Its
diff was refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14 with ZERO sample-line changes, which is grm-4nr's
recorded signature exactly. Two further runs of the same code on the same input:
    run 1: refs 1847 / instrs 7382 / warnings 604   FAIL
    run 2: PASS (matched the golden exactly)
ff1's golden was deliberately NOT blessed.

=== SHORTFALL, FILED SEPARATELY ===

cv2 delivered +2 bank comments against +10 predicted. The mechanism works -- c4de recovers
prg_bank=4 via FUN_c183 and retargets to W8000_M3_B4::8326 -- but eight of the ten hand-found
c183 call sites emit neither a comment nor a warning. Filed as grm-093 (P4) with the two
candidate explanations and the cheap check that distinguishes them; also mirrored into
docs/human-research-todo.md. Note one branch of that question (calls reaching a helper by plain
JMP never passing runDataflow's isCall() gate) would ALSO cost blmaster, so grm-093 may end up
raising increment 2's ceiling.

=== INCREMENT 2, STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD ===

blmaster FUN_e61b: twelve call sites, reached by an internal JSR from a wrapper that is NOT
address-contiguous with its helper. Its dump is byte-identical after increment 1, which is the
intended scope check -- isPassThroughInto's zero-flows condition excludes it by construction.
Increment 2 needs interprocedural argument propagation (a wrapper effectively acquiring a bank
parameter sourced from its own callers), which is a different feature from wrapper admission and
was deliberately not attempted here. Check grm-093's outcome first: if the answer is the JMP
gating, that is a cheaper and broader fix than interprocedural propagation and should come first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 LANDED 2026-08-09 (d147ea3) -- CALL-EDGE WRAPPERS. blmaster measured; corpus sweep
still running at time of writing.

=== THE RECLASSIFICATION, NOW EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED ===

grm-093 and docs/human-research-todo.md both recorded that blmaster was BLOCKED UPSTREAM on
grm-mej.2, because e61b was "a shadow-ESTABLISHING wrapper of exactly the class cv2's c185 belongs
to". That was wrong, and the fix required no grm-mej work at all:

  cv2 c185      loads $1C, which a DIFFERENT FUNCTION (c183) wrote   -> establishing
  blmaster e61b stores AND reloads $DB inside ONE CONTIGUOUS BODY    -> forwarding

e61b is cv2's c183+c185 pair FUSED INTO ONE FUNCTION, not c185 alone. The span is exactly what
grm-mu7 increment 2's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource save-restore model already covers. What
actually blocked it was the CALL EDGE, which is this bead's own remaining scope. Per the ruling at
plan time the correction was held until measured; it is measured, so both records are now updated.

=== WHAT SHIPPED ===

  HelperModel gains a nullable Relay(callSite, calleeEntry) + atCallEdgeWrapper. The prologue
  becomes a LIST of spans: PrologueSegment, an argumentSurvivesPrologue overload that is a literal
  AND, and prologueSegments deriving [entry, callSite) and [calleeEntry, firstSite).

  THE PREDICATE ITSELF NEEDED ZERO CHANGES. Its loop bound is `cursor < to`, so passing the relay
  JSR's address as segment 1's end stops the walk BEFORE inspecting it -- the isCall() early-return
  never fires on the boundary instruction. Segment 2 is empty for e63c, whose STA $FFFF IS its
  entry, and an empty segment is trivially true.

  findCallEdgeWrappers, wired LAST so relays resolve through increment 1's wrappers. ONE ROUND,
  counted against the immutable input map: the exactly-one-helper-call rule is NON-MONOTONE in the
  helper set, so with rounds the answer would depend on candidate iteration order. Counting against
  the input makes the pass a pure, order-independent function -- a STRONGER property than increment
  1's snapshot, which would not have fixed this.

TWO GATES, AND NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER -- the least obvious thing in the increment, and the
plan's first draft got it wrong. A BRANCH DOES NOT MAKE argumentSurvivesPrologue DECLINE: a nonzero
getFlows() only clears straightLine/argumentCells and the walk CONTINUES. So a prefix that branches
around the relay but never writes argReg passes the VALUE gate, and admitting it would rest every
claim about the wrapper's effect on a call that might not run. The STRUCTURAL gate is
isPassThroughInto REUSED with target = the relay call site -- an exact reuse, not opportunistic:
the prefix of a call-edge wrapper up to its relay IS a pass-through into that call site.

THREE CONSUMER FIXES, all found by walking the checklist rather than by a failing test:
  - valueSuppliedInsideHelper and callSiteRegisters stop addresses must be the WRAPPED helper's
    entry. The wrapper's would let a backward scan run off the helper's entry into the wrapper's
    tail and read it as prologue -- the exact hazard valueSuppliedInsideHelper's own javadoc warns
    about.
  - midBodyEntryHelper now declines a relay model OUTRIGHT. A relay model's firstSite lives in a
    different function and so exceeds every address in the wrapper's body, meaning the existing
    entry>firstSite test admitted EVERY mid-body address -- including ones past the relay call,
    where no bank switch happens on that path at all.

=== BLMASTER: THE TARGET, MEASURED ===

  count bankComments      5 -> 9    (+4)
  count warnings         24 -> 32   (+8)
  count refs.intoOverlay  0 (=)
  count instrs.inOverlay  0 (=)

  new: c55f  prg_bank=0 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #0)
       c57a  prg_bank=0 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #0)
       e2c3  prg_bank=2 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #2)  <- non-home, as predicted
       df07  prg_bank=5 via FUN_e61b      (JMP, LDA #5)  <- non-home, and see below
  new warnings: cc6a, df0c, e304 -- "call to helper FUN_e61b whose bank argument could not be
       recovered". All LDA $D3 restore sites: a previously SILENT miss became a conservative one.

  EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR PLAIN-IMMEDIATE CALL SITES RESOLVED. The bead predicted the three JSR ones
  and hedged df07 on whether shared-return retyped it; it did. Nothing decreased anywhere.

  THE JMP FINDING IS A BONUS DELIVERABLE AND IT REFUTES grm-093's HYPOTHESIS (b). That bead closed
  saying the isCall() gate (BoardBankAnalyzer:676) was unmeasurable corpus-wide and that blmaster
  would be the probe once its helper stopped being rejected. It is now the probe, and there is NO
  REACH ASYMMETRY: resolved sites split 3 JSR / 1 JMP, declined sites split 1 JSR / 2 JMP. Recorded
  in full on grm-093; do not file an isCall() bead.

  HONEST LIMIT WORTH NAMING: instrs.inOverlay stayed 0. The banks are now recovered but nothing
  retargets against them yet on this title -- no nearby windowed access resolves under the
  recovered state. So this is a real annotation gain, not yet an overlay-coverage gain.

=== TESTS ===

  Tier 2: new HelperCallEdgeWrapperProgramTest (12 cases). Pins BOTH gates separately -- including
  a case asserting the value gate ACCEPTS the branching prefix, so a future change that made it
  reject branches would not silently render the structural gate's point moot. Also pins the two
  cross-segment reset properties (stack and memory), which would silently become true if the reset
  were removed, and the empty-list guard against a vacuous true. Increment 1's 9 cases still pass.

  Tier 3: new nesrelaytest fixture (R1-R11 + R2b/R3b/R7b, 15 criteria), deliberately a SEPARATE ROM
  so neswrappertest.dump staying byte-identical remains the proof increment 2 left increment 1
  alone. Four negative controls -- two-helper-call, non-helper-call, branching, argument-clobbering
  -- each with its OWN helper so a rejection cannot be confused with a broken helper, plus R7b as
  the anti-vacuity check that the helper behind the value-gate control still resolves.

  FULL GATE: SUITE OK. Exactly one golden ADDED, ZERO existing goldens modified.

=== FILED / STILL OPEN ===

  grm-k90 (P3): wrapper models hand the caller's X/Y to depositHelperArgument without proving they
  survive the wrapper body. NOT new to increment 2 -- increment 1 carries it identically -- and
  forcing X/Y unknown could only DECREASE annotations, which acceptance forbids. contra is the
  title to read.

  NOT A TEST GAP BUT WORTH KNOWING: the midBodyEntryHelper relay decline is not directly pinned.
  Constructing a stable mid-body entry into a wrapper synthetically is unreliable, because a JSR
  target normally gets a Function created and so stops being mid-body. The guard is blunt
  (relay != null) precisely so it cannot be wrong.

title: realrom bless served a stale cached candidate after an id rename
description:
REPORTED: 'realrom-test.sh bless --gme <romdir>' re-blessed the curated titles as well as the GME ones, and undid the wizwarr->ironsword rename -- expected/ironsword.dump came back saying 'REALROM program wizwarr.nes'.

ROOT CAUSE (two independent cache-key omissions, both fixed):
1. realrom_cache_key() hashed rom_sha + opts + RealRomDump.java + ext_id but NOT the row id. The id IS part of the output: import_and_dump names the ROM copy after it, so it reaches the dump as 'REALROM program <id>.nes'. Renaming a row therefore left the key identical and bless served the pre-rename candidate straight into the golden. It went unnoticed because the only other changes in that commit were Java COMMENTS, which do not alter bytecode, so the CRC-based ext_identity() was unchanged too.
2. ext_identity() fingerprinted only '*.jar' under Extensions -- but the compiled board descriptors ship LOOSE as data/machines/*.map next to the jar (only the two charset maps are inside it). So editing machines/nes-*.yaml, the single most common change in this repo and the one that directly determines the block/overlay layout the dump records, ALSO left the key unchanged. Worse instance of the same bug than the reported one; found while diagnosing it.

FIXES: id added to the key; ext_identity() now also sha256s the loose non-jar Extensions files; and on a cache HIT, bless asserts the candidate's 'REALROM program' == <id>.nes and 'REALROM sha256' == the manifest row before accepting it, discarding and re-importing otherwise -- so the NEXT key omission fails loudly rather than silently blessing a stale dump.

ALSO FIXED (the reported surprise): --gme was additive. It now SELECTS: no flag = curated manifest.tsv, --gme = manifest-gme.tsv only, --all = both. Every run announces the set. Additive was chosen from a design preview and was wrong in practice -- 'bless --gme' re-blessing twelve untouched goldens costs real work to undo.

VERIFIED against the real ROM (/h/emulators/nes/ROMs): 'bless --only ironsword' re-imports instead of reusing the stale entry and reproduces the committed golden BYTE-IDENTICALLY (which also proves the git-checkout restore was correct, not merely plausible); planting a wrong-program-name dump at the NEW key is rejected with 'stale cache entry ignored ... re-importing' and still yields the correct golden. Set selection gives 12/19/31 rows for none/--gme/--all.

NOTE: the 149 pre-existing build/realrom-cache entries are now unreachable (keys changed). Harmless -- the dir is gitignored and regenerates.
close_reason: Fixed and verified against real ROMs. Cache key now includes the row id; ext_identity() now hashes the loose data/machines/*.map descriptors as well as jars; bless asserts a reused candidate names this row and this ROM; check audits every existing golden at startup (no ROMs needed). --gme now selects rather than adds, with --all for both. Committed ece0722.

title: Bank-switch helper argument recovery: memory-latch sites resolve to unknown, poisoning discrete-mapper state
description:
Follow-up to grm-3x1 (2026-07-31), which closed the memory-latch REACHABILITY gap and
proved that reachability was never the whole problem. All five moved real-ROM titles now
SEE their latch stores and recover NOTHING from them.

MEASURED (all 12 hash-pinned titles, before -> after grm-3x1):
  title         overlay refs   bank comments   warnings
  contra          0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  dragonpower     0 ->    0       0 ->   0      3 ->  6
  shenlong        0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  wizwarr        17 ->   17      11 ->  11      4 ->  8
  megaman      1781 -> 1703     153 -> 151      3 -> 37

TWO DISTINCT SYMPTOMS, one root cause.

(1) NO NEW ANNOTATIONS. Contras board-level "no mechanism write was observed" warning is
gone -- replaced by a per-site warning at c142 ("mechanism write with a genuinely
undeterminable value") plus five "call to bank-switch helper FUN_c13f whose bank argument
could not be recovered at this call site". So the helper IS identified; the ARGUMENT is
not recoverable at any call site. Same shape on dragonpower/shenlong (FUN_ffbe, FUN_8eeb)
-- both GxROM Dragon Ball titles, so likely one shared engine.

(2) MEGAMAN REGRESSED -78 overlay refs / -2 bank comments / +34 warnings. Mechanism:
StoredValueScanner aborts a backward scan when it steps over a mechanism write (class
javadoc: "a base value read further back would predate that write, so falling back to the
in-state would be unsound"). Making more writes visible therefore makes more scans abort.
Watch FUN_c39c: it appears in 11 of the 34 new warnings as an unrecoverable helper.
Site 9067 specifically degraded from "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" to a warning.

WHY IT MATTERS BOTH WAYS. The optimistic reading is that megamans 1781 refs came from a
model blind to 7 of its 25 switch sites, so shrinking them is a correctness gain. The
pessimistic reading is that we traded correct annotations for warnings. NOBODY HAS
CHECKED WHICH -- that determination is the first task here, and it decides whether
megaman ever gets blessed (it is measurement-only per grm-g73).

LIKELY DIRECTION: the helper-evaluation path already works for megamans absolute sites
("via FUN_d131" etc), so the machinery exists; what is missing is recovering the bank
argument at the CALL SITE when the value arrives via a register the callers set from a
table/variable rather than an immediate. grm-hb6.4 (per-game site hints as dataflow
seeds) is a plausible lever for the genuinely unrecoverable remainder.

DO NOT "fix" this by relaxing the mid-scan abort without an argument -- the abort is
sound and the grm-3x1 javadoc records why.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROM GROUND TRUTH (2026-08-01). All 5 ROMs located and SHA-256 verified against
tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv BEFORE disassembly, so this is pinned to exactly the
dumps the goldens describe. ROM dirs: H:/emulators/nes/roms and Z:/nes/db.

CONTRA helper is 3 instructions; the bug is visible in them:
  C13F: B9 D0 FF  LDA $FFD0,Y   <- helper entry; bank argument arrives in Y
  C142: 99 D0 FF  STA $FFD0,Y   <- the "genuinely undeterminable" warning
  C145: 60        RTS
Bank table $FFD0 = 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 (fixed $C000 window). findHelpers sets
argReg = storeRegister(STA) = 'A'; the argument is really in Y. Call sites:
  C0C9 LDY #$01 / C0CB JSR      -> bank 1   RECOVERABLE
  C0D1 PLA / C0D2 TAY / C0D3 JSR-> CPU stack (NMI save/restore)
  C146 LDY $07EC / C149 JMP     -> RAM save slot (JMP tail call; Ghidra CALL_TERMINATOR)
  C155 LDY #$01 / C157 JSR      -> bank 1   RECOVERABLE
  C161 LDY $07ED / C164 JSR     -> RAM save slot
The 3 unrecoverable sites are ONE idiom: save current bank / switch / restore. NMI does
C0C1 LDA $8000 / PHA ... PLA / TAY / JSR $C13F -- it does not know what bank it interrupted,
so it reads the bank number back out of the cartridge. C139/C14F do the same into $07EC/$07ED;
C146/C15E restore from them.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT: Contra's $8000 is a BANK-IDENTIFYING byte -- byte 0 of bank N equals N
for all 8 banks (00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07). So LDA $8000 IS a read of live bank state.
Megaman does NOT use this trick (its per-bank byte-0 values are 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 00).
Per user: the identifier is not common but not rare, and its LOCATION VARIES game to game --
prefer a per-game hint over content deduction, for documentary value.

MEGAMAN: bank table at $C000 = 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07. ZP $42 is a write-through
"current bank" shadow (every mechanism write is immediately preceded by STA $42 of the same
register). ZP $31 is a partial address encoding banks as 0-6 / 7-$C (not investigated).
  D131: LDA #$06 / STA $42 / STA $C006     ; works today
  C3B3: LDA #$05 / STA $42 / STA $C005     ; works today
  C39C: LDA $31 / CMP #$06 / BCC / SBC #$06 / TAX / STA $42 / STA $C000,X
                                           ; bank from RAM $31 -- its 11 warnings are HONEST
  FUN_d846:
    D846: LDA #$06 / STA $42 / STA $C006   ; switch #1 -> bank 6
    D855: LDA #$00 / STA $0C / ASL A
    D85A: TAX                              ; X = 0, statically known
    D85B: LDA $D81E,X                      ; $D81E = 00 02 00 02 00 02 00 01 ... -> A = $00
    D85E: TAY / D85F: STA $42
    D861: STA $C000,Y                      ; switch #2, newly visible after grm-3x1

VERDICT ON THIS BEAD'S HEADLINE QUESTION: megaman's 1781->1703 shrink is a CORRECTNESS GAIN.
JSR $D846 leaves the board in bank 0, NOT bank 6 -- switch #2 overwrites switch #1 before the
RTS. The pre-grm-3x1 golden's "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" at site 9067 was WRONG, and the
78 overlay refs retargeted into PRG_LO_B6 on the strength of it were wrong with it. grm-3x1
correctly stopped believing a falsehood. This bead replaces the wrong 6 with a right 0 --
so do NOT expect 1781 back: bank 0 is PRG_LO's home bank, realized in BASE space, so refs
resolved under a known bank=0 are base-space refs and are not counted by refs.intoOverlay.

DRAGON POWER / SHEN LONG (GxROM 66), byte-identical engine, deferred:
  FFBE: LDA $F2 / ASL A / ASL A / ORA $F9 / TAY / LDA $FFCC,Y / STA $FFCC,Y / RTS
  FFDC: PLA/CLC/ADC #1/STA $17 / PLA/ADC #0/STA $18 / PLA / STA $F2 / FFEA: JSR $FFBE
        / JMP ($0017)
$F2 = current-bank shadow. $FFDC is an INLINE FAR-CALL: LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC pops the
return address, increments it, switches bank, and jumps -- execution resumes at the NEXT
instruction in a DIFFERENT bank.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT: the cross-bank invariant region is real and holds the whole switch engine.
Measured per-offset across all four 32 KiB banks:
  dragonpower  $FF68-$FFF9 (146 bytes)   contains $FFBE helper, $FFCC table, $FFDC trampoline
  shenlong     $FEE0-$FFF9 (282 bytes)   same
TRAP FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: this MUST be computed per-offset, NOT as a common suffix. $FFFA-$FFFF
genuinely differ per bank (each bank has its own NMI and IRQ handler; only RESET is common,
$FF88 in every bank of both games), so a suffix test reports ZERO invariant bytes. I got this
wrong on the first pass and nearly reported the opposite conclusion.

STRUCTURAL BLOCKER for GxROM/AxROM, independent of dataflow: both descriptors declare a single
PRG_ALL $8000-$FFFF window with no fixed bank (machines/nes-gxrom.yaml:52-57,
nes-axrom.yaml:33-37), so every cart offset is overlay-covered and
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte returns null for EVERY address those
programs can name. The $FFCC table is unreadable to the engine even with a perfect index.
That is a third gap beyond the stack and the ZP shadow.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-01, same day): MY EARLIER VERDICT IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. The prior
comment claimed "JSR $D846 leaves the board in bank 0, not bank 6" and concluded megaman's
1781->1703 shrink was a CORRECTNESS GAIN. Both claims are FALSE. Corrected below; the rest of
that comment (Contra, GxROM, the content measurements) still stands.

WHAT I MISSED: I read FUN_d846 as straight-line code. It is a LOOP. $D887 is BNE $D859, so
$D859 is the loop head:

  D855: LDA #$00 / D857: STA $0C          ; chunk counter = 0
  D859: ASL A                             <<< LOOP HEAD (BNE $D887 targets here)
  D85A: TAX                               ; X = 2 * counter
  D85B: LDA $D81E,X                       ; per-chunk BANK number from the table
  D85E: TAY / D85F: STA $42
  D861: STA $C000,Y                       ; switch to THIS CHUNK's bank -- varies per iteration
  D864..D87F:                             ; copy a CHR chunk through ($04) to $2007 (PPU)
  D881: INC $0C / D883: LDA $0C / D885: CMP #$0A / D887: BNE $D859   ; 10 chunks
  D889: LDA #$06 / D88B: STA $42
  D88D: STA $C006                         ; RESTORE bank 6 after the loop
  D890: JSR $BFF6 / D893: JMP $C3B3
  index table $D81E.. = 00 02 00 02 00 02 00 01 00 01 00 03 00 03 02 01 02 01 00 08
  (even entries are banks, odd entries are chunk counts)

So FUN_d846 is a CHR upload loop that hops among banks 0/2 while copying, and ends on bank 6.

CONSEQUENCES, all the opposite of what I said before:
1. The warning at $D861 is HONEST. The bank genuinely differs per iteration and no static
   value exists. The analyzer declines because isControlFlowJoin fires at $D859 -- the
   join guard doing exactly its job. (NOT the mid-scan mechanism-write abort; that never
   fires on this chain.)
2. FUN_d846's post-call state IS bank 6, set at $D88D immediately before the exit path.
   The pre-grm-3x1 golden's "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" at site 9067 was CORRECT.
3. Therefore megaman's 1781 -> 1703 is a REGRESSION, not a gain. The 78 refs into PRG_LO_B6
   were right, and this bead needs to restore them.
4. GAP 1 (known-index resolution) does NOT fix megaman and was never going to -- verified
   empirically: Increment 1 landed green and left megaman byte-identical at 1703/151/37.
   $D861 stays unresolvable, correctly.
5. THE FIX IS GAP 2 (increment 2). findHelpers keeps switchSite = MAX address = $D88D and
   drops constState to null because the three sites disagree (6 / unknown / 6). The
   mini-inline then evaluates $D88D under the call site's registers: LDA #$06 / STA $42 /
   STA $C006 -> bank 6, caller-independent. That restores the annotation and the 78 refs
   FOR THE RIGHT REASON -- derived from the site that actually executes last, instead of
   from a constState coincidence that happened to read the first site before grm-3x1 made
   the other two visible.
   This also makes findHelpers' max-address switchSite rule (BoardBankAnalyzer:864-871)
   load-bearing on a real cartridge for the first time, not just on serial-shift chains.
REVISED PREDICTION for megaman after increment 2: refs.intoOverlay back to ~1781 (not
"do not expect 1781 back" as I wrote before), bankComments ~153, warnings 37 minus the
FUN_d846 call sites. The 11 FUN_c39c warnings stay -- those really are RAM-sourced.

METHOD NOTE, worth keeping: the abstracted unit test passed while the real ROM did not move
at all. A verbatim reproduction of the bytes at their real addresses ALSO passed, because
ProgramBuilder had no back edge -- the abstraction and the transcription were both wrong in
the same direction. What settled it was raising RealRomDump's SAMPLE cap to see the actual
bookmark at $D861, then byte-scanning the ROM for branches targeting $D84A-$D862. Also note
tools/banktest/BankReachProbe.java is STALE: its writesInRange is a verbatim copy of the
PRE-grm-3x1 tier-1-only version (its javadoc still cites :193-203), so its today= column
reports NO for every indexed site that production actually does see via tier 2. It sent me
down a blind alley; file a fix.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND CORRECTION + NEW DEFECT CLASS (2026-08-01): a helper's effect must follow TAIL CALLS.
Reported by the user and confirmed against the ROM.

FUN_d846 does not end at $D88D. It ends:
  D890: JSR $BFF6
  D893: JMP $C3B3        <- TAIL CALL out of the function
and FUN_c3b3 is a "set bank 5" routine:
  C3B3: PHP / PHA / LDA #$05 / STA $42 / C3B9: STA $C005 / PLA / PLP / RTS
So on return from JSR $D846 the live bank is 5 -- not 6, and not 0. My previous correction
got the loop right and the exit wrong.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. Scanning every megaman function that contains a mechanism write, for
its exit terminator:
  FUN_c55d   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $C573   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_d131   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D159   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_d846   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D893   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_c05a   TAIL JMP $C079,  FUN_c219 TAIL JMP $907E,  FUN_c3bf TAIL JMP $BFF3
  FUN_f105   TAIL JMP $F105  (self -- a CYCLE GUARD is mandatory, this is not hypothetical)
  the rest end RTS/RTI.

CONSEQUENCE -- a pre-existing wrong-answer class, independent of grm-3x1 and grm-hum:
HelperModel summarizes a helper by the max-address recognized write in ITS OWN BODY
(BoardBankAnalyzer:864-871). For any helper that tail-jumps to another bank-setting routine,
that is the wrong site. FUN_d131 is the clearest case: its only own site is $D135 STA $C006,
so constState = bank 6 and EVERY call to it currently folds bank 6 -- while the real
post-call state is bank 5. That annotation is shipping today and is wrong.

So "restore megaman to 1781 refs" is NOT the goal. The 1781 number was wrong in two
independent ways: bank 6 for FUN_d846 (should be 5), and the same error at FUN_d131 and
FUN_c55d call sites. Increment 2 as briefed would faithfully REINTRODUCE bank 6 -- a
confident falsehood. It must not be blessed in that state.

REQUIRED MODEL FIX (increment 2b): a helper's effect is the bank state at its EXIT, following
tail calls -- not the highest-address write inside its own body. Minimal tractable form:
when a helper's function terminates in a JMP/CALL_TERMINATOR to another recognized helper,
COMPOSE the two effects (callee wins on the bits it owns). Bounded depth, and a cycle guard
is required -- FUN_f105 tail-jumps to itself.
The principled statement to put in findHelpers' javadoc: switchSite means "the last recognized
write on the path to the helper's RETURN", and the max-address rule is only a valid proxy for
that while control cannot leave the function body. A tail call is exactly when it can.
Note the engine ALREADY has the ingredients: runDataflow treats a CALL_TERMINATOR jump as a
call and folds the callee helper's effect, so the state at the end of FUN_d846 is already
computed correctly -- it is only the HelperModel SUMMARY that ignores it.

The honest fallback, if composition is deferred: decline (warn) when a helper tail-calls
another helper, rather than assert the body-local answer. Losing 78 refs beats shipping a
wrong bank.

comments.text:
REGRESSION FOUND, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT (2026-08-02).

WIZWARR IS REGRESSED, AND INCREMENT 2 DID IT -- not 2b. Isolated by stashing the 2b/3 working
changes and re-running wizwarr at commit 918a70e (increments 1+2 only): identical numbers, so
2b is exonerated.

  wizwarr    golden        inc2 and inc2+2b+3
  refs         17    ->      0
  bankComments 11    ->      4
  warnings      8    ->     11
  lost: bank -> 7 / 3 / 1 / 1 / 4 / 6 / 4 via FUN_ffc0 at 80c2/d56e/d691/e5b1/e924/e92b/e942
  lost refs incl. 80ca -> PRG_ALL_B7::8c4b and 80cd -> PRG_ALL_B7::8b8b, i.e. DOWNSTREAM of
  the 80c2 call -- the annotation was load-bearing, not cosmetic.

MY EARLIER CLAIM WAS WRONG. The increments-1+2 commit message and my report to the user both
say every real-ROM golden except megaman/contra stayed byte-identical. That was based on an
INCOMPLETE run: after increment 2 I only ran `--only megaman,contra`. The last FULL real-ROM
run predated increment 2. Lesson: run the full realrom set before claiming a blast radius,
or say explicitly which titles were actually measured.

ROOT CAUSE -- same family as the megaman tail call, different mechanism:
  FUN_ffc0 (AxROM, bank arg in A) is a CALL-INTO-ANOTHER-BANK-AND-RETURN trampoline:
    FFC0: STY $C1 / STA $C3          ; save target-pointer low byte and the bank arg
    FFC4: LDA $C5 / PHA              ; save the CURRENT bank shadow on the stack
    FFC7: AND #$18 / ORA $C3         ; splice the requested bank into the shadow
    FFCB: STA $C5
    FFCD: STA $8000                  ; <<< THE COMMIT -- switch to the target bank
    FFD0: JSR $FFDA                  ; -> JMP ($00C1), call the routine in that bank
    FFD3: PLA / STA $C5
    FFD6: STA $8000                  ; <<< THE RESTORE -- value came from PLA, unrecoverable
    FFD9: RTS
  findHelpers picks switchSite = MAX ADDRESS = $FFD6, the RESTORE. Increment 2 mini-inlines
  that site, scans back, hits PLA (an A-modifier) and gets UNKNOWN -- so every call site
  declines. The PRE-increment-2 convention (recover argReg at the CALL SITE and deposit it
  verbatim) was RIGHT for this helper, because the argument in A is exactly what $FFCD commits.

So max-address switchSite is wrong in BOTH directions:
  megaman FUN_d846 -- too EARLY (the real effect is past the body, via a tail call)
  wizwarr FUN_ffc0 -- too LATE  (the real commit is the FIRST write; the last is a restore)
The unifying statement is the one 2b already put in the javadoc -- "the last recognized write on
the path to the helper's RETURN" -- but neither max-address NOR min-address implements it. A
switch/call/restore pair nets to NO CHANGE on return, which is a third answer again.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (not yet implemented, needs a decision):
  Prefer the mini-inline only when it RESOLVES; fall back to the legacy argReg-at-call-site
  recovery when it yields unknown. That restores wizwarr (legacy path resolves A) and keeps
  contra (mini-inline resolves Y, legacy would not) and megaman (2b's composition resolves).
  It is a strict improvement over both conventions taken alone. Downside: it is a heuristic
  union of two models, so it wants a comment saying WHY rather than looking like a hack.
  The principled alternative -- model save/restore pairs so the helper's net effect is
  "unchanged" -- is more correct but bigger, and would ALSO drop wizwarr's 17 refs unless
  callers genuinely observe the switched bank downstream (the B7 refs above suggest they do,
  which needs checking before committing to that model).

STATUS: 2b and 3 are otherwise GOOD -- unit 145/145, full headless gate 368/368 criteria PASS,
nesuxhelpertest U1-U10 all PASS, megaman's bank-6 falsehood is gone. Only wizwarr blocks.
DO NOT bless any real-ROM golden until wizwarr is resolved.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RESOLVED (2026-08-02). wizwarr PASSES; only contra and megaman differ, which is the intended
blast radius. Full realrom: pass=9 fail=2 skip=1.

TWO THINGS WENT WRONG AND BOTH ARE WORTH RECORDING.

1. THE FIX. The user spotted that my proposed "use the FIRST write instead of the last" repair
   could not work: at $FFCD, A = ($C5 & $18) | $C3, and `ORA $C3` is NON-IMMEDIATE, so
   StoredValueScanner stops there (:233). Neither of FUN_ffc0's switch sites mini-inlines --
   $FFCD needs $C3, $FFD6 needs a PLA. Confirmed by inspection; they were right.
   Note bits 0-2 (AxROM's whole tracked field, `bits: 3`) come ENTIRELY from $C3, which
   $FFC2 stored from the caller's A. So the legacy convention "the argument register holds
   the field value" is not merely lucky on this helper -- it is exactly what the code computes.
   The engine cannot DERIVE it only because it lacks zero-page store-to-load propagation
   (bead A territory).
   Implemented: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument prefers the evaluated
   answer and falls back to the conventional argValue when the evaluation pins down nothing.
   A fallback can only fill in where evaluation was silent, so it can never overwrite a derived
   answer with a weaker assumed one. Contra is recovered only by evaluation (argument in Y,
   invisible to the convention); wizwarr only by the convention (argument laundered through ZP,
   invisible to evaluation). Neither model dominates -- that is why it is a union, and the
   javadoc says so.

2. A MEASUREMENT TRAP THAT COST TWO WRONG CONCLUSIONS. `build-and-test.sh check unit`
   DELIBERATELY SKIPS the extension build/install (documented in CLAUDE.md). realrom-test.sh
   runs against the INSTALLED extension. So `check unit && realrom-test.sh check` measures the
   PREVIOUS build. I did exactly that, saw wizwarr unchanged, and concluded the fix had failed
   -- it had actually worked. Re-running after `check nes-banking` (which does build+install)
   showed the pass.
   RULE: before any realrom run, build+install via a HEADLESS chunk (`check nes-banking`) or the
   full gate. Never trust a realrom measurement that follows only `check unit`.
   This ALSO retroactively explains nothing about the earlier wizwarr regression -- that one was
   real and is now fixed -- but it is the same shape as the grm-8cq stale-probe trap: the tool
   answered a question about a different build than the one under test.

FINAL REAL-ROM STATE (all measured against a freshly installed extension):
  contra   0 -> 257 refs, 0 -> 849 instrs, 0 -> 2 comments, warnings 6 -> 6
           (c0cb/c157 -> bank 1 via FUN_c13f; c0d3 stack, c149/c164 RAM, c142 helper-interior
           still honestly warned; 2 new warnings in bank-1 code that only became analyzable
           because of the new refs)
  megaman  1781 -> 1704 refs, 7437 -> 7429 instrs, 153 -> 156 comments, 3 -> 32 warnings
           9067 bank -> 5 via FUN_d846   (was the pre-grm-3x1 golden's WRONG bank 6)
           91bf/949e/a044/a082 bank -> 5 via FUN_d131   (was wrongly bank 6, shipping for ages)

           The 11 FUN_c39c warnings remain -- bank from RAM $31, genuinely unrecoverable.
           refs do NOT return to 1781 and should not: 77 of those were retargets into
           PRG_LO_B6 justified by the wrong bank-6 claim at FUN_d846/FUN_d131/FUN_c55d call
           sites. They are gone because they were wrong.
  wizwarr, dragonpower, shenlong, db3, dbz2, dbz_datach, dbz_saiyan, zelda, smb3: byte-identical
  smb: SKIP (ROM not present in the supplied dirs)

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THE MEGAMAN DETERMINATION IS ANSWERED (hand RE + current goldens, 2026-08-06). This bead said
"NOBODY HAS CHECKED WHICH -- that determination is the first task here, and it decides whether
megaman ever gets blessed." Checked. The answer is the OPTIMISTIC reading, and by a wider margin
than this bead allowed for.

=== 1. CURRENT COUNTS vs THE TWO HISTORICAL POINTS ===

                        pre-grm-3x1    post-grm-3x1    current 2026-08-06
  refs.intoOverlay          1781           1703              1704
  instrs.inOverlay           --             --               7429
  bankComments               153            151                156
  warnings                     3             37                 32

  NOTE the 1703 -> 1704 move is NOT a gain: grm-g73 measures megaman as bistable run-to-run at
  exactly refs -1 / instrs +2, so 1703 and 1704 are the same result seen twice. Do not read a
  one-ref delta on this title as signal until grm-g73 closes.

  THE HEADLINE: bankComments 156 now EXCEEDS the pre-regression baseline of 153. The annotation
  channel is RICHER than before grm-3x1, not poorer. warnings are also down 37 -> 32 since the
  low point (grm-4kc, grm-nju, grm-mu7 all landed in between). Only refs.intoOverlay remains
  below its old peak, at -77.

=== 2. SITE 9067, THE NAMED DECISIVE CASE: THE OLD ANNOTATION WAS WRONG ===

This bead recorded 9067 degrading from "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" to a warning. Current
state: NO bookmark, and the generated comment reads "bank -> 5 (bank=5) via FUN_d846".

HAND TRACE OF FUN_d846 shows 5 is correct and 6 never was:
  - sets PRG bank and $42 to #6 at entry (redundant -- the chunk loop overrides immediately)
  - sends 10 chunks to the PPU, setting PRG bank from a stride-2 table at d81e per chunk
  - sets PRG bank and $42 to #6 again, then calls b53f via the thunk at bff6
  - finally JMPs to c3b3, which sets PRG bank and $42 to #5 and returns

So d846's EXIT state is bank 5. The old "bank=6" came from the last write inside d846's own
body -- the #6 before the b53f call -- because nothing followed the tail JMP into c3b3. The
sequence at this site is therefore:

    1781-refs era     bank -> 6     WRONG
    after grm-3x1     warning       honest but unhelpful
    current           bank -> 5     CORRECT

THIS IS A THIRD OUTCOME THIS BEAD DID NOT CONSIDER. The framing was "correctness gain" vs
"correct annotations traded for warnings". At the decisive site it was neither: a WRONG
annotation was replaced by an honest warning and then by the RIGHT value. The old 1781 refs
did not merely come from a blind model -- at least one of them was a wrong bank.

=== 3. FUN_c39c'S 11 WARNINGS ARE HONEST DECLINES, NOT LOST INFORMATION ===

c39c appears in 11 of the 34 warnings this bead flagged. Hand trace: it saves P, A and X, then
sets PRG bank and $42 from ZP $31, subtracting 6 first when $31 > 6. $31 is INC'd, DEC'd, zeroed
at several sites, and elsewhere loaded from tables or by more exotic routes.

That makes $31 a STATEFUL COUNTER with a wrap-adjust (7->1 ... 12->6). Its value at a given site
depends on execution history rather than on any dominating definition, so no constant-
propagation model recovers it, and no amount of helper-argument work will. The analyzer is
correctly declining. Recovering these would need value-range or path-sensitive tracking of $31,
which is a different and much larger project -- do not file it against helper-arg recovery.

=== 4. VERDICT ===

Both halves point the same way. The surviving annotations got BETTER (156 > 153, with at least
one previously-wrong value now correct), and the new warnings are HONEST (c39c's argument is
genuinely unrecoverable). The pessimistic reading -- correct annotations traded for warnings --
is not supported at the one site this bead nominated to decide it.

MEGAMAN SHOULD BE BLESSABLE ON THE MERITS. It is still blocked from actual blessing by grm-g73
(run-to-run bistability), which is an independent problem and unaffected by this finding.

HONEST LIMIT OF THIS EVIDENCE: 9067 is one site out of a 77-ref delta. It was THIS BEAD'S named
decisive case and it resolves cleanly, but it does not prove every lost ref was wrong. If a
stronger guarantee is wanted, the remaining work is to sample a handful more of the lost refs --
not to re-open the framing.

=== 5. WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWNS ===

The megaman determination was only its FIRST task. The bead's main body -- contra,
dragonpower and shenlong at 0 refs / 0 bank comments, with the helper identified but the
ARGUMENT unrecoverable at every call site (FUN_c13f, FUN_ffbe, FUN_8eeb) -- is untouched by
this and remains open. dragonpower and shenlong are both GxROM Dragon Ball titles and likely
share one engine, so treat them as one investigation.

=== 6. SPUN OUT OF THIS TRACE ===
  - $42 is hand-confirmed as megaman's write-through bank shadow (noted on grm-mej.2).
  - d846's 10-chunk loop takes its bank from a stride-2 table at d81e -- grm-m95's shape, ten
    switch sites in one loop (noted on grm-m95).
  - d846 is a real-ROM case where tail-call composition changes the answer (noted on grm-432).

title: Backward value scan lacks single-predecessor check; over-confident value at CFG join
description: StoredValueScanner.java:114. resolveStoredValue only validates the prev->cur fall-through edge, never that cur has a single predecessor, so at a control-flow join it attributes the fall-through path value to the store with full confidence. Failure: LDA #$05 / BEQ t / LDA #$0A / t: STA $8000 returns fullyKnown 0x0A, ignoring A=$05 on the BEQ path. The immediate-fold and AND/ORA-fold paths bypass the engine merge (resolveLoad path is safe as it uses merged inStateAtStore). Fix: require block-leader / single-predecessor before folding a local immediate. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): resolveStoredValue now aborts to unknown() at a control-flow join, detected via isControlFlowJoin (incoming flow Reference to cur from an addr other than prev). RESIDUAL: unresolved computed/indirect jumps leave no reference, so a join reached only by a jump table is not detected -- conservative in the safe direction (worst case a fold we'd otherwise make), not a wrong-value risk.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: recoverCallArgument guesses bank register (A-first), recording wrong bank
description: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:558. recoverCallArgument tries A then X then Y and returns the first that resolves to any immediate, not the register the helper actually reads. Failure: LDX #3 / LDA #$80 / JSR SelectBank (helper takes bank in X, its store not locally resolvable) -> A-first scan returns $80, engine records bank 0x80 instead of 3; downstream refs retargeted to wrong overlay, EOL comment lies. Fix pattern: propagate unknown() when the convention is ambiguous rather than a confident guess. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): recoverCallArgument now scans the register the helper actually stores into its mechanism (HelperModel.argReg from StoredValueScanner.storeRegister on the switch site) instead of the A-first guess. Strictly dominates old behavior: the STX-helper failure now records the correct bank; transform helpers degrade to prior behavior, never worse. RESIDUAL follow-up: a helper that stores a DIFFERENT register than the caller loads (e.g. TXA / STA mechanism) still mis-attributes, needing recursive convention inference inside the helper body. Not filing separately unless it bites.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2
