=== 5. c9a4/c9ba IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE SITE AND NEEDS FOUR THINGS AT ONCE ===

Non-home banks inventoried: 2 (e2c3), 5 (df07, ec53, dec2), 4 and 6 (c9ba). The first three are
single sites worth a few hundred bytes. c9ba is different in KIND: it selects a bank, then reads
POINTERS FROM $8000 and dispatches through an indirect jump -- the classic banked-dispatch
idiom, where one recovered bank yields as many entry points as the table has entries. It is the
only thing found in blmaster with the shape to move instrs.inOverlay meaningfully.

  FUN_c9a4:
      LDX #$40
      LDA $14
      AND #$08
      BEQ c9ae        ; skips ONLY the next instruction
      LDX #$60
    c9ae:
      TXA
      PHA
      JSR ea3a        ; body does 4x LSR at ea41, then JSR e61b -> bank 4 or 6
      PLA
      LSR A x4
      AND #$0F
      STA $D3         ; = c9ba; records the same bank ea3a just selected
      ; ... pointer resolution from $8000, indirect jump

  NOTE the $40/$60 values are NOT an attempt to set bank $40/$60 (which would mask to 0):
  ea3a unpacks them with 4x LSR before switching, and the post-PLA 4x LSR/AND #$0F is the same
  unpack applied to the saved copy. The two agree. Nothing sets bank 0 here.

  FOUR SEPARATE UNIMPLEMENTED THINGS, ALL REQUIRED:
    (i)   SET-VALUED BANK STATE. The BEQ skips only 'LDX #$60'; both paths MERGE at c9ae, so X
          is {$40,$60} at the merge and single-valued dataflow must call it unknown. Filed
          separately -- this is not blmaster-specific.
    (ii)  PHA/PLA STACK PAIRING across the JSR ea3a -- grm-mej.3's first half, exactly.
    (iii) 4x LSR + AND #$0F mask algebra on the recovered value.
    (iv)  The $D3 shadow with the section-4 second discovery route.
  Any one missing and c9ba recovers nothing. This is why blmaster's best site is also its hardest.

=== 6. RULED OUT / CORRECTED, DO NOT RE-DERIVE ===

  - ea41's OTHER callers (cc74, d97c) load A from tables that are CHR DATA copied to the PPU,
    not code bank selectors. Deprioritised as a disassembly source. c9a4 is a third caller of
    ea3a and is the one that matters.
  - PRG MODE 3 holds throughout: nothing writes MMC1 CONTROL except the fff4 INC reset and
    f25f's e678 call with A=#$1E (4K CHR, PRG mode 3, vertical mirror). So $8000-BFFF is the
    switchable 16K window and $C000-FFFF is fixed to the last bank.
  - HOME BANK for $8000-BFFF is 0: the RESET routine at f23b JMPs to c24f, which immediately
    sets $D3 to 0. Consequence: the three 'LDA #0' call sites (c55f, c57a, e694) resolve
    CORRECTLY to home and retarget nothing. Do not read them as failures.
  - grm-mu7 ruled out: constArgRegMatch=2, constArgRegMismatch=0, constArgRegMixed=0.

=== 7. FILED SEPARATELY FROM THIS PASS ===
  - Function-boundary over-extension merging the RESET routine into FUN_f1ca.
  - No-argument helpers (e68c) reporting helperArgReg=A and a spurious unrecoverable-arg warning.
  - Set-valued bank state at a pre-switch merge.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BEAD IDS for section 7 of the def-use pass, now filed:
  grm-78b (P3, bug)  function body over-extends past f237, merging RESET f23b into FUN_f1ca
  grm-xym (P3, bug)  no-argument helpers report helperArgReg and warn about an argument that
                     does not exist (e68c)
  grm-wul (P2)       set-valued bank state: the {4,6} merge at c9ae collapses to unknown
All three are discovered-from this bead.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CV2 DEF-USE PASS, HAND-DERIVED 2026-08-06 (Chris). Second title after blmaster. Conclusion up
front: CV2 IS NOW THE MOST TRACTABLE OF THIS BEAD'S FOUR, and its headline "20 of 20" figure
measures the wrong thing.

=== 1. THE 20/20 FIGURE IS 75% CHR AND CTRL, NOT PRG ===

This bead headline for cv2 is "20 of 20 direct stores recover not one bit". Those 20 decompose:

  FUN_c140 routine    MMC1 CTRL from $100     5 writes
                      CHR0 bank  from $101     5 writes
                      CHR1 bank  from $102     5 writes
  c187 chain          PRG bank   from A        5 writes
                                              ----
                                               20

FIFTEEN OF THE TWENTY ARE CHR AND CTRL. cv2 has exactly ONE PRG chain. This is grm-8iy.4's
rcransom lesson on a second title -- there, 32 of 35 sites were CHR selects that deliberately
no-op for PRG, and the bead concluded "bankComments is not a health metric". The same correction
applies to the SITE COUNT: 20/20 is not 20 failed PRG recoveries, it is 1 PRG chain plus 15
PRG-irrelevant writes. Worth re-deriving this bead's title figures as PRG-only for all four
titles; tmnt (24/30) and wizwarr (4/13) may carry the same inflation.

$100 IS A WRITE-ONCE RAM CONSTANT: set to #$1E at reset, no other writers found. So cv2's CTRL
value is statically determinable rather than undeterminable, and #$1E is the same value blmaster
writes at f25f -- 4K CHR banks, PRG MODE 3, vertical mirror. cv2 is therefore $8000-BFFF
switchable over a fixed $C000-FFFF, same geometry as blmaster.

=== 2. THE HELPER IS ONE ROUTINE WITH THREE STAGGERED ENTRY POINTS ===

    c183:  STA $1C          ; set bank to A AND remember it
    c185:  LDA $1C          ; entry: restore bank from the shadow
    c187:  5x STA/LSR $FFFF ; entry: set bank to A, WITHOUT remembering

Byte arithmetic confirms the fallthrough: STA $1C zero-page is 2 bytes (85 1C) landing exactly
on c185; LDA $1C is 2 bytes (A5 1C) landing exactly on c187. c183 falls through c185's load,
which harmlessly reloads what it just stored -- the trick that lets three semantics share one
tail.

This is a complete little bank API: set-and-remember (c183), restore (c185), set-transient
(c187). c187 deliberately does NOT touch $1C, so temporarily forcing bank 0 leaves the shadow
intact for a later c185 to restore. Recognisable idiom; expect it elsewhere.

$1C IS CV2'S BANK SHADOW -- the third title in a row with one (blmaster $DB/$D3, megaman $42,
cv2 $1C). See section 5.

=== 3. ALL 16 CALL SITES ===

  entry  count  arg                    bank      notes
  c183     9    LDA #4 immediately     4         NON-HOME -- the prize
  c183     1    LDA #0 immediately     0         home
  c187     3    LDA #0 immediately     0         home; transient force
  c185     3    (reads $1C)            restore   later in the SAME functions as the c187 calls
                                                 ----
                                        16 total, 13 with an adjacent immediate

  Pattern for the c187/c185 pairs: force bank 0, do work, restore the remembered bank. Since
  c183's 9 dominant calls set bank 4, those restores return to bank 4.

AGAINST WHAT THE ANALYZER SEES TODAY: reachableCallSites 5, constArg 2, both resolving to HOME,
nonHomeBanks 0, instrs.inOverlay 0. So 16 real sites are seen as 5; 13 adjacent immediates are
recovered as 2; and NINE non-home bank-4 switches are recovered as zero.

=== 4. ROOT CAUSE: PRE-BODY ENTRY, WHICH NO EXISTING DETECTOR CAN SEE ===

Ghidra's function starts at c187 -- this bead own text describes cv2's chains as "around
FUN_c187". But the routine's real entry points are c183 and c185, which lie BELOW that boundary.
Thirteen of sixteen call sites therefore target addresses that are not a helper function entry
as far as findHelpers is concerned, and their adjacent immediates are never considered.

grm-nju measured cv2 at midBodyEntry=0 and viaThunkOrTrampoline=0, and grm-8iy.3 used those
numbers to rule grm-nju's shapes out for cv2. Both measurements are CORRECT and both are
MISLEADING: the problem is not a call landing inside a function body, it is a call landing
BEFORE the function starts. Pre-body entry is a distinct shape that the mid-body detector cannot
see by construction. Filed separately.

NOTE THIS IS THE SECOND FUNCTION-BOUNDARY DEFECT FOUND BY HAND IN TWO TITLES -- grm-78b is
blmaster's, where a body over-extends and swallows an unrelated routine. This one is the
opposite error: a body starts too late and orphans its own entry points. Both corrupt anything
keyed on "which function contains this".

=== 5. WHY CV2 IS THE CHEAPEST REMAINING UNLOCK ===

blmaster's best site (c9a4) needs FOUR unimplemented things simultaneously -- set-valued state,
PHA/PLA pairing, mask algebra, and a shadow with a new discovery route. cv2 needs TWO, and one
of them is easy:

  (a) Recognise c183/c185 as helper entries (the pre-body-entry fix). This alone exposes 13
      adjacent immediates, of which NINE are a non-home bank 4.
  (b) The $1C shadow for the 3 c185 restores -- and $1C is an EASY case for grm-mej.2's rule as
      written, because the STA $1C at c183 sits two bytes before the mechanism chain, in the
      same block, storing the same register. No second discovery route needed, unlike blmaster
      $D3.

Step (a) on its own should take cv2 from 0 non-home banks to 9. Given cv2 currently resolves
zero instructions into overlay space, that is the whole title.

SHADOW GRADATION ACROSS THE THREE TITLES TRACED SO FAR, useful for grm-mej.2 sequencing:
  megaman $42   written alongside every mechanism write     FOUND by the rule as written
  cv2     $1C   STA two bytes before the chain, same block  FOUND by the rule as written
  blmaster $D3  written in five functions with no mechanism write   NEEDS the second route
Three of four titles traced have a bank shadow. This is not a per-game quirk; it is how 6502
bank switching is written.

=== 6. STILL OPEN ON CV2 ===
  - Are there callers of c183/c185/c187 beyond the 16 found? "known calls" was a manual survey.
  - Does bank 4 actually hold code, and does anything reference into it once retargeted?
  - The 3 c185 restore sites: confirm each is dominated by a c183 call so the restore value is
    statically 4 rather than genuinely dynamic.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TMNT DEF-USE PASS, HAND-DERIVED 2026-08-06 (Chris). Third title after blmaster and cv2.

=== 1. GEOMETRY AND HOME BANK -- A DISCREPANCY WITH THIS BEAD'S OWN NUMBERS ===

Startup sets MMC1 control to $1F (PRG MODE 3, 4K CHR, horizontal mirroring), then PRG bank 7.
Same geometry as blmaster ($1E) and cv2 ($1E, from $100) -- all three differ only in mirroring
bits. $8000-BFFF switchable, $C000-FFFF fixed to the last bank.

So HOME for $8000-BFFF is BANK 7, not 0. That contradicts this bead's own table, which lists
tmnt's three "fully-known NON-HOME banks" as c003 (prg_bank=2), c340 (=7) and c354 (=7). Under
the startup reading, c340 and c354 are HOME and only c003 is a genuine non-home switch.

RESOLVE BEFORE ACTING ON tmnt: how does the analyzer derive home for this title? If it defaults
to bank 0, tmnt's retargeting is pointed the wrong way at two of its three recovered sites, and
"3 non-home banks" is really 1. This also changes what a fix should be measured against.

=== 2. THE BANK-IDENTIFYING ROM OFFSET IS PRESENT *AND THE GAME USES IT AS AN API* ===

The first byte of every ROM bank (at $8000 and $C000) is that bank's own number. That is exactly
grm-mej.2's content-derived bank-identifying offset, which Contra also passes.

But tmnt goes further than passing a content test -- it READS the value at runtime:

  cec0: LDA $8000        ; ask "which bank am I in?"
        STA $59          ; stash it
        ... set bank 0, JSR 9016 ...
        JSR cf0b         ; restore PRG bank from $59

So LDA $8000 is a genuine BANK READ-BACK, the literal subject of grm-mej.2's title, observed in
the wild rather than derived. Consequence: recovering this save/restore pair requires the
analyzer to answer LDA $8000 with the live bank number from tracked in-state. Deriving the
offset is not merely an optimisation here; without it the pair is opaque.

=== 3. FIVE HELPERS, ONE WITH A STAGGERED ENTRY (grm-i7v INSTANCE #2) ===

  ce56  sets MMC1 CONTROL from A
  ce6f  sets CHR0 bank from A
  ce8a  sets CHR1 bank from A
  cea5  saves A to $21, then FALLS THROUGH to cea7        <-- set-and-remember
  cea7  sets PRG bank from A                              <-- set-transient
  ced0  restores PRG bank from $21
  cf0b  restores PRG bank from $59

  STA $21 zero-page is 2 bytes (85 21), landing exactly on cea7 -- the same staggered-entry
  construction as cv2's c183/c185/c187. This bead records tmnt's fifth chain as ceaa..ceba, i.e.
  inside cea7's body, so Ghidra's function almost certainly starts at cea7 and cea5 lies BELOW
  it. That makes tmnt a second instance of grm-i7v, and a costly one -- see section 4.

  CONFIRM: does Ghidra's function start at cea7 or cea5? The whole section-4 payoff depends on it.

  NOTE the same set-and-remember / set-transient / restore split as cv2, but with the restores
  as SEPARATE FUNCTIONS (ced0, cf0b) rather than a third fallthrough entry. Two restores because
  there are two shadows.

=== 4. CALL SITES: ELEVEN CONSTANTS, SEVEN OF THEM BEHIND THE INVISIBLE ENTRY ===

  entry  arg context                       count   bank      note
  cea5   LDA #1                              3      1        NON-HOME
  cea5   LDA #6                              2      6        NON-HOME
  cea5   LDA #3                              1      3        NON-HOME
  cea5   LDA #4                              1      4        NON-HOME
  cea7   LDA #0                              3      0        NON-HOME (home is 7)
  cea7   LDA #2                              1      2        NON-HOME
  cea7   LDA $8000; PHA; ...; PLA            1      read-back see section 2 and grm-mej.3

  Twelve known call sites, ELEVEN with a recoverable constant, and under the section-1 reading
  ALL ELEVEN select a non-home bank. Against today's measurement of 13 callSites / 6 constArg
  and (at most) one genuine non-home recovery.

  ALL SEVEN cea5 SITES ARE NON-HOME AND ALL ARE GATED BY grm-i7v. That is the single highest
  concentration of recoverable non-home banks found in any title traced so far.

  INCOMPLETE COVERAGE: several further calls appear NOT to be reached by automated disassembly
  at all, so 12 is a floor, not a total. Worth a separate look -- a disassembly-reach gap is a
  different problem from a value-recovery gap and would not be fixed by either.

=== 5. THE $F0 LOCK BIT: A RE-ENTRANCY GUARD WOVEN INTO THE SERIAL CHAIN ===

All four A-taking helpers (ce56, ce6f, ce8a, cea7) share a guard idiom: the first LSR of the
MMC1 serial sequence is replaced by SEC followed by ROR $F0, with an ASL $F0 just before return.
Bit 7 of $F0 is thereby set for the duration of the switch and cleared at the end. The NMI
handler tests it and returns early, so an interrupt cannot land in the middle of a five-write
serial sequence and corrupt the shift register.

ANALYZER CONSEQUENCE, INDEPENDENT OF THE EXACT ENCODING: tmnt's mechanism chains contain
INTERLEAVED NON-SHIFT INSTRUCTIONS. A strict 5x(STA/LSR) pattern match will either reject these
chains or mis-parse their shift sequence. That is a plausible direct cause of this bead's "24 of
30 stores recover nothing" for tmnt, and it is a different failure from cv2's (which was a
boundary problem, not a pattern problem).

OPEN, NOT YET DETERMINED -- two readings, different fixes:
  (a) The value stays in A and $F0 is purely a flag. The chain is then a normal 5x(STA/LSR A)
      sequence with two extra instructions bracketing it; recognition needs only tolerance for
      interleaved unrelated writes.
  (b) $F0 HOLDS THE VALUE BEING SHIFTED, so SEC/ROR $F0 both sets the lock bit and performs the
      first shift, and the chain is STA reg / LSR $F0 rather than STA reg / LSR A. The serial
      shift then runs on MEMORY, not the accumulator -- a genuinely different mechanism shape
      that a register-based strategy will not match at all.
  Determine which before designing anything. (b) is the more consequential and would also
  explain why the stored VALUES recover nothing even where the sites are found.

=== 6. TWO SHADOWS AGAIN, WITH DIFFERENT PROVENANCE ===

  $21  primary bank shadow. Written at cea5 immediately before the mechanism chain, same block,
       same register -- so grm-mej.2's discovery rule as WRITTEN finds it, like cv2 $1C and
       megaman $42. Read back at ced0.
  $59  save slot for a READ-BACK value, not for a stored one: cec0 fills it from LDA $8000, not
       from the register being stored. Read back at cf0b. A rule that only looks for stores of
       the mechanism register will not find this one, and should not try to -- it is the
       read-back path of section 2, not a write-through shadow.

  FOUR OF FOUR TITLES TRACED NOW HAVE AT LEAST ONE BANK SHADOW: blmaster $DB/$D3, megaman $42,
  cv2 $1C, tmnt $21/$59.

=== 7. WHAT TMNT NEEDS, IN ORDER ===
  1. grm-i7v (pre-body entry) -- exposes 7 non-home constant sites at cea5. Biggest single win.
  2. Section 5's chain-recognition question -- may be why the direct stores recover nothing.
  3. Home-bank resolution (section 1) -- decides what "non-home" even means here.
  4. grm-mej.2 for $21 (easy case) and the $8000 read-back for the cec0/cf0b pair.
  5. grm-mej.3 for the PHA/PLA around the read-back call site.
Note the previously-flagged grm-v60 angle on FUN_c310 (endsWith=JMP, trampolineShape=YES,
holding 7 of tmnt's switch sites) is NOT addressed by this pass and remains open.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE TMNT PASS (2026-08-06), all confirmed by hand after the fact.

(1) TMNT IS NOT A PRE-BODY-ENTRY CASE. Ghidra creates functions at BOTH cea5 and cea7. Section 3
of the tmnt writeup inferred otherwise from this bead's own record of the fifth chain as
ceaa..ceba; that inference was circumstantial and wrong. cea5 is a complete two-byte function.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: an ARGUMENT-MARSHALLING WRAPPER reaching its helper by FALLING THROUGH into
the next function -- the same class as blmaster's e61b (tail JMP), now filed as grm-2dr with
both instances. The seven non-home call sites at cea5 (LDA #1 x3, #6 x2, #3, #4) are still real
and still unrecovered; they are gated by grm-2dr, not grm-i7v.

CV2'S CLAIM RESTS ON THE SAME UNVERIFIED INFERENCE and now needs checking: does Ghidra have
functions at c183 and c185? If it does, cv2 is a wrapper case too and grm-i7v has no instances.

(2) THE $F0 GUARD DOES NOT INTERLEAVE. Verbatim: SEC / ROR $F0 / STA $xFFFF / 4x (LSR A, STA
$xFFFF) / ASL $F0. The chain is contiguous and standard; the value rides in A; $F0 is only a
lock flag. So the guard is NOT the explanation for tmnt's 24-of-30 unrecovered stores, and
grm-oiu has been corrected, retitled and dropped to P3 -- retained only to test whether the
backward value scan trips over the ROR $F0 RMW.

(3) HOME BANK -- WITHDRAWING THE DISCREPANCY I RAISED. Section 1 of the tmnt writeup questioned
this bead's listing of c340 and c354 (prg_bank=7) as non-home, on the grounds that startup sets
bank 7. Hand check finds NO resolved LDA #7 feeding the PRG bank anywhere except the reset
routine at c32e, so bank 7 is a post-reset PLACEHOLDER rather than a persistent home for the
$8000 window. This bead's original count of three fully-known non-home banks STANDS. Disregard
section 1's "resolve before acting" note.

NET EFFECT ON THE TMNT DIAGNOSIS: the title is gated by grm-2dr (seven wrapper-hidden non-home
sites), with the direct-store failures still unexplained and grm-oiu reduced to one narrow test.
The bank-identifying-offset finding in section 2 -- cec0 reading LDA $8000 as a live bank query
-- is unaffected and remains the strongest evidence for grm-mej.2's read-back half.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WIZWARR DEF-USE PASS, HAND-DERIVED 2026-08-06 (Chris). Fourth and last of this bead's titles.
It is the least like the other three: wizwarr is NOT primarily a value-recovery problem.

=== 1. GEOMETRY, AND THE FIGURE THAT MISLEADS ===

AxROM: one register at $8000 packing PRG bank in bits 0-2 and VRAM page in bit 4. Confirmed by
the masks the game itself uses -- ff69 does AND #$18 to KEEP the non-bank bits, ce38 does
AND #$F8 to CLEAR the bank bits. Reset sets bank 0 explicitly at 894b, so HOME IS BANK 0.
The game is 4x32K, so only bits 0-1 are live.

THE 13 DIRECT STORES ARE MOSTLY NOT BANK SWITCHES. Contexts:

  LDA #0                              3x (one via LDX/STX)   bank 0
  LDA #0 with intervening stores      3x                      bank 0
  LDA $00; AND #$18                   1x   masks the bank OFF -> bank 0, VRAM bits preserved
  LDA $00                             1x   restore from shadow
  LDA #$10                            1x   VRAM PAGE 1, BANK 0
  LDA #$10; STA $00                   1x   same, also updating the shadow
  FUN_ff69 special                    1x   see section 3
                                     ---
                                      13

So the dominant activity at these sites is VRAM PAGE MANIPULATION AT BANK 0. This bead records
wizwarr as "9 of 13 stores DO recover, but every recovered value is bank 0, so retargeting
nothing is correct GIVEN THOSE VALUES" -- that reading is right, and the reason is now concrete:
those sites genuinely do not switch banks. The 4/13 figure is inflated the same way cv2's 20/20
and rcransom's 35 were, by counting mechanism writes that are not PRG selects. For AxROM the
confounder is the VRAM page bit sharing a register with the bank.

=== 2. WHERE THE REAL SWITCHING LIVES -- ALL OF IT INVISIBLE ===

Three separate reasons, none of them value recovery:

  (a) ff69's masked merge (section 3) -- needs mask algebra plus a composite shadow.
  (b) THREE BANK-SWITCH ROUTINES THAT ARE NEVER DISASSEMBLED (section 4).
  (c) A CALL SITE THAT DOES NOT EXIST as far as Ghidra is concerned (section 5).

=== 3. ff69 IS A FAR-CALL TRAMPOLINE WITH A COMPOSITE SHADOW ===

    ff69: STA $1D          ; stash the requested bank
          LDA $00          ; the shadow: the WHOLE AxROM register
          PHA              ; save it
          AND #$18         ; keep the VRAM/page bits, drop the bank
          ORA $1D          ; merge in the requested bank
          STA $00          ; update shadow
          STA $8000        ; SWITCH
          ... JSR (indirect) ...
          PLA              ; restore the saved register byte
          STA $00
          STA $8000        ; SWITCH BACK

  $00 IS A SHADOW OF THE ENTIRE REGISTER, not of the bank field. That is new -- megaman $42,
  cv2 $1C, tmnt $21 and blmaster $DB all shadow a bank number directly. Modelling $00 requires
  knowing which BITS of it are the bank, and the stored value is ($00 & $18) | $1D, so recovery
  needs mask algebra over a shadow rather than a plain read-back. Noted on grm-mej.2.

  THE STRUCTURE IS A FAR CALL: switch, JSR through an indirect vector, switch back. That is
  grm-v60's subject matter, on a title where it is the primary switching mechanism rather than
  an edge case. Noted there.

  The PHA/PLA pair around the call is grm-mej.3's stack save/restore, over the register byte
  rather than over a bank number.

=== 4. THREE BANK-SWITCH ROUTINES LIVE IN RAM AND ARE NEVER DISASSEMBLED ===

FUN_cdaf initialises RAM and copies a number of routines from the ceXX region to 03xx.
CopyLoopAnalyzer NOTICES these loops and declines them for lack of jump refs. Three of the
copied blocks are code, and ALL THREE WRITE THE AxROM REGISTER:

  ce38 -> 033d   LDA $00; PHA; AND #$F8; ORA #2; STA $8000; LDA ($9D),Y; TAY; PLA; STA $8000; RTS
                 A FAR READ: switch to BANK 2 (constant), fetch one byte through ($9D),Y,
                 restore the previous register byte. Same save/merge/restore idiom as ff69.

  ce4b -> 032d   STA $8000; <send PPU data>; ... ; STX $8000 with X=0; RTS
                 switch to A, do PPU work, return to BANK 0.

  ce5b -> 0300   STA $00; STA $8000; <send PPU data>; LDA #3; STA $00; STA $8000; RTS
                 switch to A, do PPU work, EXIT ON BANK 3 (constant) -- note it does NOT
                 restore, it leaves bank 3 live.

  The remaining copied blocks appear to be data.

  THE ROM IMAGES ARE PRESENT AND READABLE at ce38/ce4b/ce5b -- unlike DB3 (grm-azv), where the
  stub's ROM image is never disassembled either but the situation is otherwise the same. Here
  the bytes are right there; nothing seeds disassembly at them because the only "references"
  are a copy loop the analyzer declined. Filed separately.

  CONSEQUENCE: two constant non-home banks (2 at ce38, 3 at ce5b) and a pass-through at ce4b are
  invisible, on a title where ONE recovered non-home value cascades across the whole
  8000-ffff window.

=== 5. bc08 DOES NOT EXIST: AN ENTRY POINT INSIDE ANOTHER INSTRUCTION'S OPERAND ===

    bc05: LDA #2
          BIT $03A9        ; assembles as 2C A9 03
          JMP $FF69
    bc08:  LDA #3          ; <-- these are the A9 03 operand bytes of the BIT above
          JMP $FF69

The classic 6502 BIT-skip idiom: enter at bc05 and the BIT consumes the LDA #3; enter at bc08
and it executes. Two entry points, one tail JMP, overlapping instruction streams.

bc05 was disassembled first, so bc08's bytes are already claimed as BIT's operand and NO
FUNCTION CAN BE CREATED THERE. A call site carrying LDA #3 -- a non-home bank -- simply is not
in the program. Filed separately; same class as grm-o59 (vectors pointing into the middle of an
instruction), which currently has only a synthetic fixture and now has a real-ROM instance.

=== 6. ce84/ce89/ce8b: THE FALLTHROUGH-WRAPPER STACK, FOURTH TITLE ===

  ce8b  sets the register from A on entry, then clears VRAM at $2000   <- the mechanism writer
  ce89  sets A to zero, then FALLS THROUGH to ce8b                      <- establishing wrapper
  ce84  sets A to #$10, CALLS ce8b, then FALLS THROUGH to ce89          <- forwarding + fallthrough

ce84 therefore clears VRAM page 1 then page 0. Structurally this is cv2's c183/c185/c187 stack
again -- grm-2dr -- although here the values carried are VRAM page bits at bank 0, so the payoff
is nil. Recorded because it makes wizwarr the FOURTH OF FOUR titles exhibiting the shape, and
because ce84 is currently reached only from RESET, which may mean other callers exist behind
section 4 or 5.

=== 7. WHAT WIZWARR NEEDS, IN ORDER ===
  1. Seed disassembly of the three RAM-resident routines (section 4). Two constant non-home
     banks, and the biggest single win here.
  2. The bc08 overlapping-entry problem (section 5). One more non-home bank.
  3. ff69's masked merge over the composite $00 shadow (section 3) -- grm-mej.2 + mask algebra.
  4. grm-v60 for the far-call structure, if the destination bank's code is to be reached.
  Note NONE of these is "the stored value could not be recovered". wizwarr's values are mostly
  recoverable and mostly bank 0; the problem is that its real switch sites are not in the
  program at all.

=== 8. CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S FRAMING FOR WIZWARR ===
This bead's title says switching is "dominated by DIRECT stores whose value recovers no bits".
For wizwarr that is wrong on both halves: its direct stores mostly DO recover, and they are not
where switching happens. The 4/13 figure should be re-derived as PRG-only, and wizwarr's entry
in the title figures is misleading as written.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
METRIC REFRAME (from grm-oiu, closed not-a-bug 2026-08-08).

The headline counts on this bead -- "switching is dominated by DIRECT stores whose value recovers
no bits (20/20, 24/30, 4/13, 20/21)" -- are substantially a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT of MMC1's serial
write protocol, not a finding about these titles.

MMC1 takes a bank number one bit at a time: five unrolled STA/LSR pairs inside a helper. Every one
of those five stores is a distinct "direct store" to the mechanism address, and inside the helper
the value is a runtime PARAMETER, so all five are undeterminable BY CONSTRUCTION. This is not a
recovery failure -- there is nothing there to recover. The pattern is identical across titles:

  cv2      c18e..c19e (FUN_c187), c143..c17f  -- 5 per helper, stride 4
  tmnt     ceaa..ceba (FUN_cea7), ce59..ce9f  -- 5 per helper, stride 4
  blmaster e63c..e688                          -- same

The recovery that actually matters happens at the CALL SITES, where a constant may be in flight,
and that is what the "via FUN_xxx" bank comments record. Measured that way tmnt is at 18 bank
comments and 103 instrs.inOverlay, against 0 overlay instructions when grm-oiu was filed off this
bead.

FOR FUTURE DEF-USE PASSES: count call-site chains, not mechanism stores. This is the same class of
correction already captured as check #1 in docs/human-research-todo.md section 2 ("Are the 'sites'
actually PRG?" -- cv2's 20 stores were 15 CHR/CTRL + 5 PRG). Both corrections say the raw store
count is the wrong denominator.

Not reopening or restating this bead's numbers -- recording the interpretation so the next pass
does not re-derive it.

title: MMC3 (smb2, rcransom): only 3 reachable call sites each and ZERO with a constant arg -- the PRG bank never becomes known
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-03 across three probes (build/reach-wave2, build/helper-wave3,
build/consume-wave1). Both MMC3 titles in the GME set resolve zero instructions into overlay
space, and both for the same reason -- but NOT the reason this bead's parent originally guessed.

NOT A SITE-DISCOVERY GAP. BankReachProbe (extended to select-data by grm-8iy.2) reports:
  smb2      sites.total  6   orphan 0   invisible-reachable 0   todayComment 4  todayWarn 2
  rcransom  sites.total 35   orphan 0   invisible-reachable 0   todayComment 32 todayWarn 3
Every MMC3 register write in disassembled code is seen, in a function, reachable, and annotated.
smb2's sites.todayComment 4 matches its golden bankComments 4 exactly.

NOT A CONSUMER GAP. BankConsumerProbe finds smb2 with 307 consumers of 8000-9fff, 33 of them
DIRECT flow references from the fixed bank -- comparable to the working control ff1's 44.
rcransom has 69 consumers, 19 direct flow. If a non-home bank were ever known, these would light up.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE -- TWO PARTS.

(1) THE HELPER ARGUMENT IS NEVER CONSTANT. HelperShapeProbe section 5:
      smb2      reachableCallSites 3   constArg 0   viaThunkOrTrampoline 0   midBodyEntry 0
      rcransom  reachableCallSites 3   constArg 0   viaThunkOrTrampoline 0   midBodyEntry 0
    against working controls ff1 587/178 and megaman2 395/85. Not one call site in either ROM
    passes a recoverable immediate. This is grm-m95's shape exactly -- bank number from a
    variable or table rather than an immediate -- on a board family grm-m95's title does not
    name (it says Bandai FCG / GxROM). File the fix against whichever bead ends up owning
    helper-argument recovery; do NOT silently widen grm-m95's scope without retitling it.

(2) rcransom's 38 COMMENTS ARE WORTH NOTHING, which is why this title looked healthier than smb2.
    All 32 of its store-site comments are CHR selects: select=0..5, while nes-mmc3.map declares
    targets {"6": "r6", "7": "r7"}. Selects 0-5 address CHR registers and deliberately no-op for
    PRG, so r6/r7 never leave initial_state 1024 (= select 0, prg_mode 0, r6 0, r7 1) and every
    comment reads r6=0,r7=1. Its real PRG switching is FUN_ff07 / FUN_ff29, whose arguments do not
    recover (warnings at f1d0, f21d), plus three undeterminable writes at ff21/ff25/ff4b.
    LESSON FOR ANY FUTURE TRIAGE: bankComments is not a health metric. Count fully-known NON-HOME
    banks instead -- BankConsumerProbe's walk.sites, which is 0 for both these titles and 58/59
    for the working controls.

SECONDARY, SMALLER FINDING worth a look while here: smb2's fixed window WC000 (c000-dfff) is 100%
undisassembled -- 8192 undefined bytes, 0 instructions -- while W8000/WA000/WE000 hold
1501/559/2053. A whole fixed 8K bank that nothing ever reaches is suspicious on its own terms and
may be suppressing call sites that would otherwise exist.

RE-MEASURE:
  REALROM_WORK_DIR=$PWD/build/x REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT=HelperShapeProbe.java \
    bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme --only smb2,rcransom \
      Z:/git/game-music-extraction/nes/mario2 Z:/git/game-music-extraction/nes/rcransom
  (note: smb2's ROM directory is named 'mario2')

title: blmaster: 13 constant-arg call sites into bank helpers, but only 4 resolved comments and 1 non-home bank
description:
THE MOST TRACTABLE OF grm-8iy's SIX. Unlike the others, blmaster HAS the shape that works
elsewhere and still produces almost nothing -- so this is a gap, not a limitation.

MEASURED 2026-08-03 (HelperShapeProbe section 5, build/helper-wave3):

  title      reachableCallSites  constArg   resolved call comments   fully-known NON-HOME
  ff1  *            587            178              74                      58
  megaman2 *        395             85              64                      59
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  blmaster           71             13               4                       1
  tmnt               13              6               4                       3
  cv2                 5              2               2                       0
  wizwarr             8              7               6                       0 (all home bank)
  rcransom            3              0               0                       0
  smb2                3              0               0                       0
  (* = working control)

blmaster is the outlier: 71 reachable call sites into bank-switch helpers and 13 of them with a
CONSTANT argument -- the exact shape grm-nju exploited to take ff1 from 0 to 7426 instrs.inOverlay
-- yet production annotates only 4 call sites and recovers a fully-known NON-HOME bank at exactly
ONE (ec53, prg_bank=5). Roughly nine constant-arg sites go missing between the probe's count and
production's annotation. Every other failing title's constant-arg count is fully accounted for by
its comment count (cv2 2->2, tmnt 6->4, wizwarr 7->6), so blmaster's 13->4 is anomalous.

RULED OUT ALREADY, DO NOT RE-DERIVE:
  - Not grm-nju's shape: viaThunkOrTrampoline=0, midBodyEntry=0.
  - Not site discovery: BankReachProbe (extended, grm-8iy.2) reports sites.total 21, orphan 0,
    invisible-reachable 0. Every mechanism store is seen. 20 of 21 recover nothing (todayWarn 20,
    todayComment 1).
  - Not a consumer-side gate: BankConsumerProbe finds 18 consumers of 8000-bfff, 3 of them direct
    flow refs from the fixed bank, and control.fixedToFixed.flow 963 proves the fixed bank is real
    disassembled code.
  - Not a missing overlay space.

FIRST SUSPECT: grm-mu7 (helper argReg is wrong when the helper's prologue clobbers it before the
first switch site). That bead was filed from bionic's FUN_dca8 'LDA $65' shape and notes the
hazard is silent today because recovery declines for other reasons. blmaster is MMC1
(serial-shift), whose depositHelperArgument CONSUMES argValue, so it is exactly the strategy
grm-mu7 says needs the guard. Worth checking whether blmaster's helpers (FUN_e63c, FUN_e678,
FUN_e68c, FUN_eb98, FUN_f1ca) have prologues that write the recorded argReg.

SECOND DATUM: the one non-home bank that IS recovered dies almost immediately --
'BANKCONSUME walk ec53 steps=2 stop=UNKNOWN', i.e. two instructions after the switch a
'Bank state becomes unknown here' bookmark wipes it. Even fixing recovery may need that looked at.

REPRO / RE-MEASURE:
  REALROM_WORK_DIR=$PWD/build/x REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT=HelperShapeProbe.java \
    bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme --only blmaster \
      Z:/git/game-music-extraction/nes/blmaster
Then compare 'HELPERSHAPE TALLY constArg=' against the golden's bankComments.
close_reason: NOT A BUG -- measurement artifact. The 13 constant-arg call sites this bead was built on were a flawed warning-derived helper population (any function holding any Warning bookmark). The production-aligned mechanism-derived count is 2, against 5 bank comments in the golden, so nothing is going missing and there is no gap to explain. grm-mu7, the named FIRST SUSPECT, is separately ruled out (constArgRegMatch=2, mismatch=0). Full measurement in this bead's 2026-08-04 comment. blmaster's real symptom -- instrs.inOverlay 0 -- is untouched by this and moves to grm-8iy.5, whose shape it actually has.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS LIKELY STALE -- RE-MEASURE BEFORE INVESTIGATING (recorded 2026-08-04; finding not yet verified in production).

Two things changed since this bead was filed, both pointing the same way.

(1) grm-mu7 LANDED (d612bff 'Decline a helper argument the helper's own prologue clobbers',
    ea2df90 'Model save/restore in the prologue guard', 0083b3a 'Fall back to the helper's own
    value when the caller's cannot reach'). grm-mu7 is this bead's named FIRST SUSPECT, and
    blmaster is MMC1/serial-shift -- the depositHelperArgument-CONSUMES-argValue strategy the
    guard was built for. Its effect on blmaster has not been measured.

(2) THE 13 MAY BE A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT. The in-progress HelperShapeProbe.java rewrite
    (uncommitted, working tree, +727/-93) states in its own header that the ORIGINAL
    warning-derived helper population -- every function containing ANY 'Warning' bookmark, no
    text filter, no mechanism check -- was flawed, and names this bead as where it showed up:

      'On blmaster that inflated 5 real helpers into 36 site functions and a constant argument
       count from 2 to 13. It also UNDER-counts: a real helper production resolves cleanly
       (FUN_e68c on blmaster) carries no Warning bookmark and was never enumerated by this
       population at all.'

    If the true constArg count is 2 rather than 13, then blmaster is 2 constArg -> 4 comments,
    which is NOT anomalous, and the '13 -> 4, roughly nine sites go missing' framing that
    justifies this bead dissolves. blmaster would then be an ordinary member of grm-8iy.5
    (direct stores whose values do not recover), not 'THE MOST TRACTABLE OF grm-8iy's SIX'.

    The rewrite's response is to report TWO separately-derived populations side by side --
    mechanism-derived (mech) keyed on a real STA/STX/STY into a descriptor-declared mechanism
    range, and the old warning-derived one (warn), kept deliberately rather than deleted and
    classified by bookmark-text prefix -- tagging each function BOTH / MECH-ONLY / WARN-ONLY,
    with TALLY.mech, TALLY.warn and TALLY.delta. The DISAGREEMENT is the finding, not either
    number alone.

FIRST ACTION HERE, before any further diagnosis:

  REALROM_WORK_DIR=$PWD/build/x REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT=HelperShapeProbe.java     bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme --only blmaster H:/emulators/nes/roms

Compare TALLY.mech vs TALLY.warn vs TALLY.delta against the golden's bankComments. If mech
constArg is ~2 and matches the comment count, CLOSE this bead as a measurement artifact and
fold blmaster into grm-8iy.5. If a real gap survives grm-mu7, the existing diagnosis stands
and the ec53 'BANKCONSUME walk steps=2 stop=UNKNOWN' second datum is still worth pursuing.

CAVEAT ON THE PROBE ITSELF: the mech population is a fresh, unaudited re-derivation, and the
script deliberately does NOT call BoardBankAnalyzer/findHelpers/StoredValueScanner. So a
mech/warn disagreement is evidence about which population is wrong on a given title -- it is
not proof that mech is right. Treat both numbers as claims until production agrees.

MEASURED 2026-08-04 (grm-mu7 landed; two-population HelperShapeProbe). THE PREMISE IS AN ARTIFACT -- RECOMMEND CLOSE.

  HELPERSHAPE TALLY.mech  helperFuncs=5  reachableCallSites=7  callInstrs=7  constArg=2
                          constArgRegMatch=2 constArgRegMismatch=0 constArgRegMixed=0
                          viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 midBodyEntry=0 tailCall=0
  HELPERSHAPE TALLY.warn  helperFuncs=36 reachableCallSites=71 callInstrs=71 constArg=13
                          viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 midBodyEntry=0 tailCall=8
  HELPERSHAPE TALLY.delta helperFuncs.both=4 mechOnly=1 warnOnly=32
                          constArg.mechOnly=0 constArg.warnOnly=11
  HELPERSHAPE TALLY.bookmarks warnTotal=90 switchUnknown=22 violation=66 other=2 noFunction=0

  golden tools/banktest/realrom/expected/blmaster.dump: bankComments 5, warnings 90,
  instrs.inOverlay 0, refs.intoOverlay 0

(1) THE INFLATION IS CONFIRMED TO THE DIGIT, exactly as the probe rewrite's header predicted:
    5 real helpers reported as 36; constArg 2 reported as 13; constArg.warnOnly=11 closes the
    arithmetic (2 + 11 = 13). The UNDER-count half is confirmed too -- helperFuncs.mechOnly=1
    is a genuine mechanism-writing helper carrying no Warning bookmark, which the old
    warning-derived population could never enumerate.

(2) THE ANOMALY DOES NOT SHRINK, IT INVERTS. This bead's case was '13 constant-arg sites but
    only 4 resolved comments, so roughly nine go missing between probe and production'. The
    real figures are 2 constant-arg call sites against 5 bank comments. There is no shortfall
    -- comments EXCEED constant-arg call sites, because direct store sites also produce them
    and grm-4kc's INC/RMW reset seed already took blmaster 3 -> 5. Nothing is going missing,
    so there is no gap to explain. blmaster is in line with its siblings (cv2 2->2, tmnt 6->4,
    wizwarr 7->6), not an outlier, and is NOT 'THE MOST TRACTABLE OF grm-8iy's SIX'.

(3) CROSS-CHECK: the probe's warnTotal=90 equals the golden's warnings=90, derived separately.
    The probe is seeing the same bookmark population production emits, so the mech/warn split
    is a classification difference, not a different sample.

(4) grm-mu7 IS NOW POSITIVELY RULED OUT, not merely untested. constArgRegMatch=2 with
    constArgRegMismatch=0 and constArgRegMixed=0: both constant args match the helper's own
    store register, so no prologue-clobber mismatch exists at blmaster's call sites.

(5) ROOT CAUSE OF THE BAD MEASUREMENT, AND WHY grm-lwu IS NOT COSMETIC. The warn population
    counted any function holding any Warning bookmark. TALLY.bookmarks splits blmaster's 90
    into switchUnknown=22, violation=66, other=2 -- i.e. bank-state VIOLATION bookmarks are the
    dominant bucket, and they sit on 32 functions (helperFuncs.warnOnly) that write no
    mechanism at all. grm-lwu records that ~80 of these 90 are 'requires mirroring known on
    entry', a PRG-irrelevant field. So grm-lwu's noise channel did not merely clutter the log:
    it manufactured 31 phantom helpers and 11 phantom constant-arg sites, and this bead was
    filed on the result. Raising grm-lwu's value accordingly.

DISPOSITION. Recommend closing this bead as a measurement artifact and folding blmaster into
grm-8iy.5, whose shape it actually has: few call sites (7 reachable, 2 constant), everything
else direct stores that recover nothing, instrs.inOverlay still 0. The one datum worth
carrying over is the second one in the original description -- ec53 prg_bank=5 dies two
instructions later ('BANKCONSUME walk ec53 steps=2 stop=UNKNOWN') -- which is a
state-lifetime question, not a helper-argument one.

STILL TRUE AND STILL UNEXPLAINED: blmaster resolves 0 instructions into overlay space. This
bead's diagnosis was wrong; the symptom is not.

title: [BUG] ff1 real-ROM golden is bistable too (refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14), a second and much larger instance of grm-g73
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-03 while using ff1 as a CONTROL for grm-8iy's root-cause pass. Five consecutive
plain 'check --gme --only ff1' runs, same build (clean tree at 290e97c), same ROM, no probe
attached, fresh project each time (-deleteProject):

  run 1  refs.intoOverlay 1880  instrs.inOverlay 7426  warnings 618   <- blessed value
  run 2  refs.intoOverlay 1847  instrs.inOverlay 7382  warnings 604
  run 3  1880 / 7426 / 618
  run 4  1880 / 7426 / 618
  run 5  1847 / 7382 / 604

EXACTLY TWO STATES, 3:2. Not drift, not a slow walk -- the same bistability class as grm-g73.
bankComments is 75 in BOTH states, so VALUE RECOVERY is deterministic; only the placement and
disassembly cascade downstream of it varies. That matches grm-g73's megaman signature.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD RATHER THAN A COMMENT ON grm-g73:
  1. Different board. grm-g73 is megaman/UxROM/mapper 2; this is ff1/MMC1/mapper 1.
  2. Different magnitude, by more than an order. megaman flaps refs +1 / instrs -2 with warnings
     UNCHANGED. ff1 flaps refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14 -- the warning count moving at all
     is a shape megaman never showed.
  3. Different direction. megaman's counts move in OPPOSITE directions (grm-g73's own "smells
     like an analysis-order race" datum); ff1's all move the SAME way, which reads more like a
     whole subtree of disassembly being reached or not reached.
  4. grm-g73 is blocked on grm-b3m/grm-eyn, which are specifically about megaman's a737 jump
     table over-read. Those cannot explain an MMC1 title.

OPERATIONAL IMPACT, ACT ON THIS BEFORE THE NEXT BLESS: ff1's golden was blessed by grm-nju
(2026-08-02 21:41) at 1880/7426/618, which is one of two values the harness produces. So ff1 now
FAILS 'check' roughly 40% of the time on an unchanged build. Same trap grm-g73 documents for
megaman, now on a second row. The megaman rule in the nes-rom-library memory ("if those two count
lines are the ONLY diff it is grm-g73") must NOT be generalized to ff1 by eye -- ff1's diff also
moves warnings, so it looks more like a real regression than megaman's does.

ALSO NOTE FOR grm-8iy: this makes ff1 a WEAK control. Its BankConsumerProbe numbers
(refs.intoOverlay.retargeted 41, walk.sites 58, walk.sitesWithConsumer 30) were taken in a single
run and may correspond to either state. megaman2 (MMC1, PASSed, retargeted 29 / walk.sites 59 /
withConsumer 23) corroborates the same shape independently, so grm-8iy's conclusion does not rest
on ff1 alone.

NEXT STEP: DeterminismProbe.java (tools/banktest) is the instrument grm-g73 built for exactly
this -- run it on ff1 in both states and localize the divergence, as was done for megaman's
PRG_LO_B5 a527..a925.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CONTEXT FROM THE FULL-CORPUS RUN (2026-08-03): ff1 is not the only extra flaky row, but it IS qualitatively different from the others, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for keeping it separate from grm-g73.

A 31-row 'check --all' gave pass=27 fail=4 skip=0, all four count-line-only: megaman, ff1, dodge, rcproam. Detail and per-run data recorded on grm-g73.

WHAT SEPARATES ff1: instrs.inOverlay MOVES here (7426 <-> 7382) and does NOT move on any of the other three. dodge holds instrs=10692 across six runs while its refs takes three distinct values; rcproam holds 4810; megaman holds its instrs too. So the corpus has a common small REFERENCE-ONLY jitter -- same code disassembled, different number of overlay refs recorded -- and ff1 alone shows a genuinely different amount of CODE being reached (delta 33 refs / 44 instrs / 14 warnings versus 1-3 elsewhere).

That is consistent with two different bugs, and ff1 is the one that actually changes what the user sees in the listing.

Also note dodge disproves the word 'bistable' for the family generally: three distinct refs values and four distinct (refs,warnings) combinations in six runs, with the two counters varying independently. ff1, by contrast, has shown exactly two states in five runs (1880/7426/618 three times, 1847/7382/604 twice), so the bistable description is still accurate for THIS title.

title: blmaster: ~80 of 90 warnings are 'requires mirroring known on entry' -- a PRG-irrelevant field dominates the warning channel
description:
MEASURED from tools/banktest/realrom/expected/blmaster.dump (MMC1). 90 warnings total, of which
roughly 80 are the same shape from annotateBankRequirementViolations
(BoardBankAnalyzer.java:1818):

  c253 [NesBankingAnalyzer] Bank state requirement violated: call to FUN_dec2 requires
       mirroring known on entry, but it is unknown here

Sampled call sites: c253, c2a1, c2b4, c2c0, c2c3, c2db, c32e, c39b, c39e, c3a7, c3db, c519,
c51c, c52a, c540, c545, c554, c55f, c562, c56d, c57a, c767, cc3b ... The named callees vary
widely (FUN_dec2, FUN_cdba, FUN_f5d9, FUN_e692, FUN_cc35, FUN_dcfc, FUN_c742, FUN_d883,
FUN_f6a7, FUN_f71c, FUN_e61b, FUN_f833, FUN_e9b8, FUN_cc6d), so this is not one bad helper --
it is the requirement machinery firing across the whole call graph.

WHY IT MATTERS. mirroring is MMC1's nametable-mirroring control. It has NOTHING to do with PRG
bank placement: it is not a bank field of any window, so it can never change which overlay a
reference retargets to. Yet it dominates blmaster's warning channel ~9:1 and buries the four
warnings that ARE about PRG. cv2 shows the same shape at lower volume (c036, c0ed, ffd5).

Contrast the honest signal on the same title: exactly one site (ec53) recovers a fully-known
non-home prg_bank=5, and that is the one worth a human's attention.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE (do not assume the answer -- an unknown mirroring may be a legitimate
finding for a mirroring-typed annotation, just not for a bank-placement one):
  1. Should the requirement check be scoped to fields that actually participate in window
     placement, with non-placement fields reported at a lower severity or not at all?
  2. Is one warning per CALL SITE the right granularity, or should it be one per callee with a
     count?
  3. Does grm-3ou's stop-reason classification subsume this? If so, close as a duplicate rather
     than fixing twice.

NOT A BLOCKER for grm-8iy's zero-resolver work -- filed so the noise is not re-derived. Anyone
reading blmaster's warnings will hit this first and it is a decoy.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THIS IS A CORRECTNESS PROBLEM, NOT A NOISE PROBLEM -- evidence from the blmaster pass
(grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-04/05). Recommend re-rating from P3 accordingly.

This bead records that ~80 of blmaster 90 warnings are "requires mirroring known on entry", a
PRG-irrelevant field. HelperShapeProbe splits the same 90 as switchUnknown=22, violation=66,
other=2, and those violation bookmarks sit on 32 functions that write no mechanism at all.

What that noise did. The probe original helper population counted any function holding any
Warning bookmark as a bank-switch helper. On blmaster that turned 5 real helpers into 36 and a
constant-argument count of 2 into 13. grm-8iy.3 was then FILED on the inflated numbers, spent a
bead worth of analysis on a nine-site shortfall that did not exist, and named two phantom
helpers (eb98, f1ca) while missing two real ones (e650, e664). It has since been closed as a
measurement artifact.

So the mirroring-warning channel did not merely make the log hard to read: it manufactured a
false population that a P2 bug report was built on. Any measurement keyed on warnings inherits
this. That is a different and stronger argument for fixing it than the ergonomic one this bead
currently makes.

RELATED, SAME FAMILY FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: grm-xym (a helper that takes no argument is
asked for one and warns when it is not found). Both are cases of an inapplicable question
generating warning traffic. Worth treating as one class -- suppress questions that do not apply
to a site, rather than filtering their output downstream.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RAISED P3 -> P2 and MARKED BLOCKED BY grm-izu (2026-08-05).

grm-izu is the likely root cause of this bead symptom, not a neighbour of it. It describes
annotateBankRequirementViolations concluding that a FULL-OVERWRITE caller-supplied helper
requires on entry the very bits it overwrites. blmaster four helpers (e63c, e650, e664, e678)
are all 5x STA/LSR serial-shift chains of exactly that shape, so the "requires mirroring known
on entry" warnings this bead counts are the predicted output of that rule on this board.

If that holds, the ownRequires exclusion proposed in grm-izu drops most of the 66 violation
bookmarks in one change and this bead becomes its acceptance measurement rather than separate
work. CONFIRM FIRST: check whether blmaster violation bookmarks name bits its own serial chains
overwrite. Unlink the dependency if not.

Priority raised for the reason in the previous comment -- the noise manufactured the phantom
helper population that grm-8iy.3 was filed on, so this is measurement integrity rather than
ergonomics.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DEPENDENCY ON grm-izu CONFIRMED -- keep the link. The check the previous comment asked for
("check whether blmaster violation bookmarks name bits its own serial chains overwrite") has
been answered by a human RE pass on c2a1; full reasoning is recorded on grm-izu, summary here:

  c2a1 -> dec2 -> df05 -> e61b -> e63c. e61b round-trips A through $DB (STA $DB ... LDA $DB)
  before e63c's 5x STA/LSR PRG chain, so the stored byte -- and therefore its bit 7 -- is
  unresolvable. SerialShift's bit-7-unknown POISON branch poisons every field any target or
  the reset could touch, mirroring included. That is the only path by which mirroring can
  reach e61b's ownRequires: e63c's normal commit is target 3 (prg_bank only) and "never
  poisons unrelated targets", and e678, the sole mirroring writer, is not in this call chain.

So the answer to this bead's own question 1 is NO: scoping the requirement check to
placement-relevant fields would not fix the problem, it would only relabel the same 66 false
warnings "requires prg_bank known on entry". The defect is upstream, in the ownRequires
inference itself (grm-izu), not in which field it names. mirroring is merely the bit that
survives the caller-side narrowing, because mirroring.1 is never established board-wide
(see the ec53/e68e bankcomments: always "assumed from initial").

THIS BEAD IS NOW THE ACCEPTANCE MEASUREMENT for grm-izu rather than independent work.
Expected on fix: the 66 violation bookmarks leave blmaster's dump; the 22 switchUnknown
warnings and the ec53 prg_bank=5 recovery must remain untouched. Question 2 (per-site vs
per-callee granularity) survives as a separate ergonomic question only if any violations
remain after the fix.

acceptance measurement, and it is the ONE remaining step -- it needs a realrom run against a

  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir>

Question 2 of this bead's original list (one warning per call site vs. one per callee with a

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED ON THE REAL-ROM CORPUS 2026-08-08, with grm-izu's fix (f8cd931) in place.
Command: realrom-test.sh check --all H:/emulators/nes/roms Z:/nes/db (31 rows).

BLMASTER: THE PREDICTION HELD EXACTLY. warnings 90 -> 24. This bead predicted ~66 requirement
bookmarks would drop; 90 - 66 = 24. Everything predicted to survive did:

The poison-branch diagnosis recorded on grm-izu is therefore confirmed on the real ROM, not just
argued from the strategy source.

WHOLE-CORPUS SPLIT. 16 rows differ from golden. FOURTEEN of them are mapper 1 / nes_mmc1 --
exactly and only the mechanism whose strategy changed -- and in every one of the fourteen the

  blmaster 90->24, dodge 299->41, ff1 618->33, drmario 34->21, kicarus 21->9, ultimaav, megaman2,
  rcproam, zelda, zelda2, tetris, tmnt, bionic, cv2 26->23.
The '+' lines in those diffs are not new warnings: they are pre-existing later warnings scrolling
into the fixed-size sample window as earlier ones are removed.
No mapper 2 / 4 / 7 title changed for any reason attributable to this fix.

NOT YET BLESSED. Two rows need a decision first, and neither is caused by this fix:

  smb3 (MMC3). FAILS ON A CLEAN BASELINE WORKTREE BUILT AT 8a913d1, i.e. WITHOUT the fix --
  so this drift predates it. Its golden was last blessed at 71959b1, and 788f09b (grm-2dr

  contra (UxROM). SCOPE-DEPENDENT, and NOT explainable by this fix -- contra is MemoryLatch,
  and the helper-call warning pass (BoardBankAnalyzer:309-326) runs strictly BEFORE the
  requirement scan, which only ever READS alreadyWarned. Observed:
     old build/ghidra-home + --only contra          -> FAIL (4 runs, identical)
     fresh build/ghidra-home + --only contra        -> PASS (2 runs)
     baseline worktree + the fix applied + --only   -> PASS   <-- same source, opposite result
     after build-and-test.sh reinstall + FULL set   -> FAIL
  The diff is always the same 4 added lines: helper-call warnings at c094/c0a2/c21b/c9c0 naming
  FUN_c139, a helper the golden does not know about. A/B'ing the SOURCE in one environment

REPRODUCIBILITY NOTE: two independent full-set runs produced BYTE-IDENTICAL dumps for all 16

STILL TO DO: bless the fourteen mapper-1 rows, EXCLUDING the four the realrom-steady-state
