TSV retained deliberately -- the sole consumer is a pure-bash harness parsing it with one 'IFS=$'\t' read' line, and YAML would have removed the rendered table (GitHub shows .yaml as highlighted source) while adding a parser dependency to a script whose job is launching the JVM. Also added '*.tsv text eol=lf' to .gitattributes, which retired the six-line per-field CR strip in favour of one 'tr -d \r' on the loop's input -- kept as process substitution, since a pipe would run the loop in a subshell and silently discard every ROW_* result while still exiting 0. Four line-pinned 'manifest.tsv:10/:12' refs in docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md became row-id refs so they cannot rot again. Verified: all 12 data rows byte-for-byte unchanged; empty-ROM-dir run yields exactly 12 SKIPs with correct ids/titles and exit 0; --only bogus lists exactly the 12 real ids (no 'id', no '#...'); --only id rejected; --only zelda,contra gives skip=2 filtered=10; no expected/*.dump touched; build-and-test.sh check = SUITE OK.

title: Helper switchSite selection is wrong for a switch/call/restore trampoline: max-address picks the RESTORE
description:
MEASURED THIS SESSION against the pinned wizwarr ROM (Ironsword - Wizards & Warriors 2 (U),
sha256 ee026cae..), by instrumenting depositHelperArgument and StoredValueScanner and running
analyzeHeadless directly against the isolated build/ghidra-home install.

FINDING. For FUN_ffc0, depositHelperArgument evaluates $FFD6 -- the RESTORE -- at all 20 of its
call sites, and the convention fallback fires every single time. It NEVER evaluates $FFCD, the
commit. Probe output (deduplicated):
    GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6 argValue=7/1
    GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6 argValue=7/3
    GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6 argValue=7/4
    GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6 argValue=7/6
    GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6 argValue=7/7
    GRMPROBE fallback at PRG_ALL_B4::ffd6 argValue=7/6
    GRMPROBE fallback at PRG_ALL_B6::ffd6 argValue=7/4
    GRMPROBE fallback at 8bea argValue=0/0
'derived' never appeared. So every wizwarr bank comment in the golden today rests on the
convention, not on any evaluation.

WHY. findHelpers summarizes a helper by the MAX-ADDRESS recognized write in its body
(BoardBankAnalyzer:917-918). FUN_ffc0 has two: $FFCD (commit) and $FFD6 (restore). max picks the
restore, whose chain starts with a PLA, so no backward scan can ever resolve it. This is exactly
grm-hum's recorded 'max-address switchSite is wrong in BOTH directions' -- megaman FUN_d846 too
EARLY (fixed by composeTailCalls), wizwarr FUN_ffc0 too LATE (never fixed; the evaluation/
convention union was shipped as a workaround instead).

CONSEQUENCE FOR grm-mej.1, and why that bead did NOT move wizwarr's golden. Store-to-load
forwarding landed and works -- verified firing on the real ROM at exactly the predicted place:
    GRMPROBE forward use=ffc9 cell=00c3 store=ffc2 -> 0/0
i.e. ORA $C3 at $FFC9 forwards to STA $C3 at $FFC2. It resolves to unknown there only because
that call is computeSwitch (env = RegisterEnv.NONE, no caller), which is CORRECT. Under a caller's
env the same chain derives the bank -- pinned by
StoreForwardingProgramTest.ironswordCommitSiteDerivesArgumentLaunderedThroughRam, which passes
argValue = unknown so ONLY a derivation can satisfy it, and which fails if the forwarding is
removed (negative control run: exactly the 4 positive tests fail, all 7 decline tests still pass).
The forwarding is simply never reached on wizwarr because the wrong site is evaluated.

*** DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY SWITCHING TO MIN-ADDRESS OR TO THE COMMIT SITE WITHOUT SETTLING THE
SEMANTICS FIRST. *** grm-hum already worked out that a switch/call/restore pair NETS TO NO CHANGE
on return, which is a THIRD answer again -- neither the commit's bank nor the restore's
unrecoverable one:
    FFC0: STY $C1 / STA $C3         ; save target-pointer low byte and the bank arg
    FFC4: LDA $C5 / PHA              ; save the CURRENT bank shadow on the stack
    FFC7: AND #$18 / ORA $C3        ; splice the requested bank in
    FFCB: STA $C5
    FFCD: STA $8000                  ; COMMIT -- switch to the target bank
    FFD0: JSR $FFDA                  ; -> JMP ($00C1), call the routine in THAT bank
    FFD3: PLA / STA $C5
    FFD6: STA $8000                  ; RESTORE -- value came from PLA
    FFD9: RTS
So on return from JSR $FFC0 the live bank is the CALLER'S, unchanged. If that is right, wizwarr's
11 bank comments and 17 overlay refs are asserting a bank that is no longer live by the time the
caller resumes -- and grm-hum flagged exactly this as unverified: 'would ALSO drop wizwarr's 17
refs unless callers genuinely observe the switched bank downstream (the B7 refs above suggest they
do, which needs checking before committing to that model).'

THE INVESTIGATION THIS BEAD OWES, IN ORDER:
1. Read wizwarr's $80C2 call site and what follows it. Do 80ca/80cd genuinely reference
   PRG_ALL_B7 code, i.e. does the caller observe the switched bank AFTER the JSR returns? If yes,
   the trampoline is not a pure save/restore and the current annotation is right for a reason
   nobody has written down. If no, the annotations are wrong and have been shipping.
2. Only then choose a model. Candidates: (a) recognize the save/restore pair and model the net
   effect as 'unchanged'; (b) make switchSite mean 'the last recognized write on the path to the
   RETURN' for real, via terminal-site analysis rather than an address max(); (c) keep the union
   but evaluate EVERY recognized site in the helper and require agreement.
3. Whatever lands, nesbanktest2 and nesuxhelpertest must not move -- their trampolines end in RTS,
   where max-address is correct. If they move, the rule was replaced rather than narrowed.

RELATED: grm-mej.3 (stack PHA/PLA pairing) would make $FFD6 itself resolvable, which is a
different repair of the same site and may make (a) unnecessary. Sequence them together.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RESOLVED (2026-08-02). THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD'S TITLE AND BODY WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL CAUSE
IS NARROWER. switchSite selection is FINE: max-address picks $FFD6, which by the stated principle
('the last recognized write on the path to the helper's RETURN') is the CORRECT site. The bug was
the CONVENTION FALLBACK being applied to it.

The convention -- 'the argument register holds the field value verbatim' -- is a claim about the
site that COMMITS the argument ($FFCD). depositHelperArgument is handed the RETURN-path site
($FFD6). In a switch/call/restore trampoline those are different instructions, so the convention
described neither the right value nor the right point in time. Retitling would be reasonable.

EVIDENCE (all measured this session against the pinned dump via analyzeHeadless on the isolated
build/ghidra-home, plus raw ROM bytes):
1. The trampoline restores. Disassembly is byte-exact to grm-hum's transcription; $FFD3 PLA /
   STA $C5 / $FFD6 STA $8000 / RTS puts the old bank back before the caller resumes.
2. Callers do NOT pre-set the shadow to match. Every writer of $C5 in the image was enumerated;
   the relevant ones are $80AB LDA #$00 / STA $C5 (then LDA #$07 / JSR $FFC0) and
   $D680 LDA #$00 / STA $C5 (then LDA #$01 / JSR $FFC0). So the restore returns bank 0.
   This was the hypothesis that could have saved the annotation, and it is false.
3. The retarget targets are DATA, not code:
     $8C4B bank 0: a5 00 29 7f 8d 00 20 = LDA $00 / AND #$7F / STA $2000   -- code
     $8C4B bank 7: 82 30 82 00 52 30 52                                      -- graphics (82 is
                                                                                 not an opcode)
     $8B8B bank 0: a9 00 85 01 8d 01 20 = LDA #$00 / STA $01 / STA $2001   -- code
     $8B8B bank 7: 11 c0 61 c0 71 c0 81                                      -- graphics
     $E530 bank 0: ad 02 20 a9 10 8d 00 20 = LDA $2002 / LDA #$10 / STA $2000 -- code
     $E530 bank 3: aa 10 65 5a b5 02 33                                      -- graphics
4. The engine contradicted ITSELF: $E91D JSR $E530 resolved in base space while $D571 JSR $E530
   was retargeted into PRG_ALL_B3 -- one routine placed in two banks, one of them data. Also
   $E92B JSR $FFC0 was retargeted to PRG_ALL_B4::ffc0, i.e. the engine believed the caller's own
   straight-line code had moved banks mid-function.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD: grm-hum's 2026-08-02 05:53 comment called wizwarr's 17->0 refs /
11->4 comments a REGRESSION and added the convention fallback to undo it. That measurement was
CORRECT BEHAVIOR and the 'fix' reintroduced a falsehood. Same shape as the megaman bank-6 story
earlier in the same bead family -- an annotation disappearing is not automatically a regression.

FIX SHIPPED: removed the fallback. Evaluation-only; when it pins nothing down, decline (deposit
unknown -> warn -> references resolve against initial_state, which is bank 0 and therefore right).
This is grm-hum's own prescription, 'losing 78 refs beats shipping a wrong bank'.

MEASURED, every line accounted for:
  refs.intoOverlay   17 -> 0    all 17 rested on the false claims
  instrs.inOverlay   55 -> 0    55 instructions had been disassembled out of graphics data
  bankComments       11 -> 4    the 7 'via FUN_ffc0' were wrong; the 4 direct ones stay
  warnings            8 -> 11   +7 honest call-site warnings; -4 duplicate ffcd/ffd6 warnings
                                from the PRG_ALL_B4/B6 overlay COPIES of the trampoline, which
                                existed only because of the false claims
Blessed. contra, megaman and every other pinned title byte-identical -- so nothing else depended
on the fallback. Full headless gate unmoved, nesbanktest2 and nesuxhelpertest U1-U10 included, so
the rule was narrowed rather than replaced.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: unknown is HONEST but not OPTIMAL. The true post-call effect is
'unchanged', expressible today as HelperDeposit ownedMask = 0. Claiming it requires VERIFYING the
save/restore pair -- pairing the PHA at $FFC6 with the PLA at $FFD3 -- which is grm-mej.3. When
that lands, wizwarr's 7 call sites should go from warning to a verified no-op, and the inner
routine reached via JMP ($00C1) is what actually runs in the requested bank (grm-v60 territory).

GUARD: StoreForwardingProgramTest.restoreSiteOfASaveRestoreTrampolineDepositsUnknownNotTheArgument
builds the full trampoline including the restore and passes a FULLY KNOWN argValue, so any
reintroduced fallback fails it. Verified by negative control: temporarily reinstating the fallback
fails exactly that test and nothing else.

title: Bank-mirror read-back: ROM identifying offset + RAM write-through shadow resolve from tracked in-state
description:
Increment 2 of grm-mej. Parts 1 and 2 of the parent bead are ONE rule: an address that MIRRORS THE
LIVE BANK resolves from the tracked in-state. One mirror lives in ROM (the bank-identifying window
offset), one in RAM (the write-through shadow). Both answer inStateAtStore; both make computeSwitch
state-dependent. They are not worth building separately.

2a. DERIVE THE TWO MIRROR SETS -- new code in BoardBankAnalyzer, slotted between the two existing
dataflow passes (:260-270), where findHelpers already sits, because shadow discovery needs
flow.switchResults() for exactly the same reason.

  BANK-IDENTIFYING ROM OFFSET (content-derived). For each switchable window and each offset K,
  test that the byte at K in bank N's overlay block equals N for EVERY realized bank. Reuse the
  existing realizedBanks/bankUniverse derivation (:1396-1441). Require >= 3 realized banks so a
  two-bank coincidence cannot qualify. Contra passes at $8000 (00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 at byte 0
  of banks 0..7); Mega Man correctly FAILS (00 00 00 00 00 00 06 00). Early-exit on bank 1 makes
  this cheap despite the nominal window x banks cost.
  USER RULING THIS SESSION: derive by content NOW; a grm-hb6.11 bank_identifying_offset: hint
  overrides later, with provenance distinguishing hinted from derived. The per-game hint tier does
  not exist yet (GAME_DESCRIPTOR_PROPERTY is declared but never written; no machines/games/;
  grm-hb6.2/.4/.11 all open), so blocking on it would strand this. Deriving also satisfies
  vision-doc section 10 item 9 -- Contra looked like a hint candidate twice and was an analyzer
  bug both times.

  WRITE-THROUGH RAM SHADOW (derived, discovery route (a)). For each recognized mechanism-write
  site, scan its own basic block backward for a ST<r> S where r is the same register the mechanism
  write stores, with no intervening modification of r. S qualifies if it is a statically-certain
  target in WRITABLE memory outside the latch range -- ANYWHERE IN RAM, NOT JUST THE ZERO PAGE
  (same ruling as grm-mej.1; Contra's $07EC/$07ED are RAM but not zp). Require the same S at
  >= 2 DISTINCT switch sites before believing it: one site is a coincidence. Mega Man $42 and
  Ironsword $C5 both qualify; Contra has no shadow and correctly yields none.

2b. DELIVER THE MIRRORS TO THE STRATEGY. There is no post-configure injection channel today
(strategies are constructed once per mechanism at configureStrategies:453-455, and discovery
necessarily happens after pass 1). Add a small lifecycle method on BankSwitchStrategy:
    default void observeMirrors(Set<Address> mirrors) {}
Call it once per configured mechanism between the passes, and make the SECOND runDataflow run when
mirrors are non-empty as well as when helpers are (:264 gates on helpers alone today).

2c. MAKE THE LATCH READ-BACK REAL, in MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy:
  - resolveLoad (:176-185): after bankInvariantRomByte declines, if resolvedTarget is in the mirror
    set, answer inStateAtStore. RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy:88-94 is the precedent, verbatim in
    shape.
  - Thread the real in-state through computeSwitch:189 -> evaluateLatch:216 -> resolveStoredValue's
    inStateAtStore (hardcoded BankState.unknown() at :221-222 today).
  - cacheable() -> FALSE, and rewrite the tripwire javadoc at :121-143, which already names this
    exact change as its trigger.
  - Leave constantRegisterValue's BankState.unknown() in-state (:472-474) AS-IS. Its javadoc
    justifies it by cacheability, which no longer applies, but an effective address is
    all-or-nothing and widening it is a separate, separately-measurable change.
  TERMINATION IS UNAFFECTED: stateIn[addr] only ever loses known bits (BankState.merge is a
  monotone agree-join), so a mirror-derived effect can only degrade across dequeues and downstream
  state with it -- the same argument register-write has always relied on.

2d. *** THE requiresOnEntry HAZARD -- THE REAL RISK, DO NOT SKIP. *** cacheable() is read in TWO
places, not one:
  - BoardBankAnalyzer:640 -- matchCache memoization. Flipping to false costs re-probing per dequeue
    and nothing else.
  - BoardBankAnalyzer:1678 -- the requiresOnEntry derivation, which counts a switch site as
    imposing a bank-known-on-entry requirement ONLY WHEN ITS STRATEGY IS NOT CACHEABLE.
Flipping memory-latch naively would make EVERY unresolved latch site on EVERY NES board declare an
entry requirement, propagate it up the call graph, and emit fresh violation WARNING bookmarks
across all twelve real-ROM goldens and the synthetic NES fixtures. That is not a real finding --
Mega Man's FUN_c39c fails because it reads $31, not because it needed the bank on entry.
FIX: make it a PER-SITE question instead of a per-strategy one.
    default boolean consultsInState(Program program, Instruction site) { return !cacheable(); }
register-write, select-data and serial-shift keep today's behavior exactly. memory-latch overrides
it to re-run evaluateLatch with an instrumented hook recording whether a MIRROR load was actually
resolved -- true only for sites that genuinely read the bank back. Called once per site in phase 3,
never in the fixpoint. Switch :1678 to this predicate. Land it in the same change as the
cacheable() flip; without it this increment cannot be blessed.

EXPECTED BLAST RADIUS: ZERO real-ROM golden movement. Traced against the measured disassembly,
every mirror read on the pinned titles is blocked by something else that is NOT in this scope:
  contra c0d3            LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA/TAY/JSR   -> the stack (grm-mej.3)
  contra c149/c164       LDA $8000 / STA $07EC .. LDY $07EC -> cross-block forwarding (grm-mej.3)
  megaman FUN_c39c x11   LDA $31                          -> $31 is a partial address encoding,
                                                             not the $42 shadow; unrecoverable
  dragonpower/shenlong   LDA $F2 / ORA $F9               -> $FFCC unreadable on a fully-overlaid
                                                             GxROM window (grm-e7v)
  wizwarr FUN_ffc0       LDA $C5 (a real, discoverable shadow) -> nothing, but AND #$18 masks it
                                                             out of the tracked field
So the DELIVERABLE is the mechanism plus the two derived facts, which grm-mej.3 and .4 consume.
PROVE IT WITH SYNTHETIC FIXTURES, not by moving a real-ROM number. If a real-ROM golden DOES move,
stop and account for every changed line before blessing.

TESTS
Tier 2: identifying-offset detection positive (synthetic image, offset 0 of bank N holds N),
negative on Mega Man's measured byte-0 values, negative with only 2 banks; shadow discovery
positive on two adjacent STA $42 / STA $C000 sites, negative when A is modified between, negative
with a single site; consultsInState true for a mirror-reading site and false for a site that failed
for an unrelated reason (the guard on 2d).
Tier 3: new synthetic fixture nesmirrortest in tools/banktest/mknesbanktest.py with CRITERION
assertions in VerifyBankTest.java, added to the nes-banking chunk. Follow nesuxhelpertest's
discipline -- CREATE THE GOLDEN ONLY ONCE EVERY CRITERION IS GREEN, or it pins the wrong behavior
as expected. Include an anti-overreach criterion in the shape of nesuxhelpertest's U3: a
RAM-sourced helper argument with no shadow and no in-block store must stay UNRESOLVED.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DESIGN INPUT FROM A HAND PASS ON BLMASTER (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05): this bead's write-through
shadow DISCOVERY RULE is too local to find one of the two shadows that actually matter.

The rule as specified scans THE MECHANISM-WRITE SITE OWN BASIC BLOCK backward for a ST<r> S
where r is the register the mechanism write stores, requiring the same S at >= 2 distinct switch
sites. blmaster has two shadows and the rule finds only one:

  $DB  FOUND. FUN_e61b stores A to $DB immediately before reaching e63c, which performs the
       5x STA/LSR into $FFFF. Same block, same register. Qualifies as written.

  $D3  MISSED ENTIRELY. It is written at c251, e692, c9ba, e9bb and e9d5 -- five sites in five
       different functions, NONE of which contains a mechanism write. No backward scan from any
       mechanism write reaches them. Yet $D3 feeds six of the twelve call sites into e61b
       (cc6a, df0c, e304, e9cb, e9ff, f026), so it is the more consequential of the two.

PROPOSED SECOND DISCOVERY ROUTE: a variable loaded into the argument register immediately before
a call to a bank-switch WRAPPER -- a function that is not itself a mechanism writer but reaches
one with the argument intact. That is the same widened notion of helper that blmaster needs for
relay-following anyway (see grm-8iy.5 section 2), so the two changes share a definition.

ALSO NOTE $D3 CARRIES TWO ROLES AT ONE ADDRESS, which a shadow model that assumes a single
direction of information flow will get wrong:
  as INPUT, a requested bank written before the switch (c251, e692, c9ba);
  as SAVE SLOT, a copy of $DB stashed across a region and written back at the end (e9bb, e9d5).
The save-slot use is grm-mej.3 territory (cross-block memory forwarding), not this bead, but the
DISCOVERY pass has to tell the two apart or it will treat a save slot as a bank request.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RAISED P3 -> P2 (2026-08-05). Consequence shifted on two counts from the blmaster pass.

DEMAND. This bead now has concrete real-ROM customers beyond the Mega Man $42 / Ironsword $C5
cases in its description. blmaster routes SIX of its twelve bank-switch call sites through a RAM
shadow ($D3 at cc6a, df0c, e304, e9cb, e9ff, f026) and a seventh through $DB at ec5b. Those
seven recover nothing today and cannot be reached by any other mechanism under discussion. It
also sits under a P2 (grm-8iy.5) and blocks three further beads (grm-mej.3, grm-mej.4,
grm-v60), so it is the gating increment of the whole shadow family.

SCOPE. It is also now known to be incomplete as specified -- see the discovery-rule gap in the
previous comment: the local backward scan finds $DB but structurally cannot find $D3. Landing
this bead as written would leave the more consequential of blmaster two shadows undiscovered,
so the second discovery route is part of the work rather than a follow-up.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEGAMAN $42 HAND-CONFIRMED AS A WRITE-THROUGH SHADOW (2026-08-06, from the grm-hum megaman
trace). This bead description nominates "Mega Man $42 and Ironsword $C5" as candidates its
content-derivation rule should find. $42 is now confirmed from the code rather than from the
rule: FUN_d846 writes the PRG bank and $42 TOGETHER at every switch it performs -- at entry
(#6), before the b53f call (#6), and in the c3b3 tail (#5) -- and FUN_c39c does the same when
it sets the bank from $31. Write-through on every path, exactly the pattern this bead models.

Unlike blmaster $D3 (see the previous comment), $42 IS reachable by this bead discovery rule as
specified: the ST A is adjacent to the mechanism write in the same block, and it recurs at many
distinct switch sites. So megaman needs only the rule as written, while blmaster additionally
needs the second discovery route. Useful as the EASY acceptance case -- if $42 does not fall out
of the implementation, something is wrong with it.

NOTE $31 is NOT a second shadow. It is a stateful counter that c39c converts into a bank
(bank = $31 > 6 ? $31 - 6 : $31), INC'd/DEC'd/zeroed/table-loaded across the program. It mirrors
nothing and must not be treated as a mirror; see grm-hum for why its sites decline honestly.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CV2 $1C IS A THIRD CONFIRMED SHADOW, AND A SECOND EASY CASE (2026-08-06, from the cv2 def-use
pass on grm-8iy.5).

    c183:  STA $1C            ; set bank to A and remember it
    c185:  LDA $1C            ; restore bank from the shadow
    c187:  5x STA/LSR $FFFF   ; the mechanism chain

$1C is stored two bytes before the chain, in the same block, holding the same register the
mechanism write stores -- so this bead discovery rule as WRITTEN finds it, no second route
needed. Three call sites read it back at c185 to restore a bank previously set at c183.

RUNNING GRADATION ACROSS THE THREE TITLES TRACED SO FAR:
  megaman  $42   written alongside every mechanism write            FOUND by the rule as written
  cv2      $1C   STA two bytes before the chain, same block         FOUND by the rule as written
  blmaster $DB   stored by the wrapper before it reaches the chain  FOUND by the rule as written
  blmaster $D3   written in five functions, none with a mechanism write   NEEDS the second route

THREE OF FOUR TITLES TRACED BY HAND HAVE A BANK SHADOW. That is no longer a per-game quirk; it
is how 6502 bank switching is written, and it is the main reason this bead was raised to P2.
Suggest sequencing megaman $42 and cv2 $1C first as acceptance cases for the rule as specified,
then blmaster $D3 for the second discovery route -- the two halves can land separately.

CAVEAT ON THE >= 2 DISTINCT SITES REQUIREMENT: cv2 has exactly ONE PRG mechanism chain (its
other 15 mechanism writes are CHR and CTRL). If the rule counts distinct MECHANISM WRITE SITES
rather than distinct STORE sites, cv2 $1C qualifies at only one and would be rejected. Worth
confirming which is counted before implementing, or cv2 silently fails an easy case.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TMNT: THE BANK-IDENTIFYING ROM OFFSET EXISTS *AND THE GAME READS IT AS AN API* (2026-08-06,
from the tmnt def-use pass on grm-8iy.5). This is the strongest evidence yet for this bead's
first half, and it raises the stakes on it.

CONTENT TEST PASSES: the first byte of every tmnt ROM bank, at $8000 and $C000, is that bank's
own number -- the same property this bead cites for Contra (00 01 02 ... at byte 0 of banks
0..7). So the content-derivation rule proposed here would find tmnt's offset at $8000.

BUT TMNT ALSO READS IT AT RUNTIME, which Contra does not:

  cec0: LDA $8000        ; "which bank am I in?"
        STA $59          ; stash the answer
        ... set bank 0, JSR 9016 ...
        JSR cf0b         ; restore PRG bank from $59

That is a literal BANK READ-BACK -- the subject of this bead's title -- observed in shipped code
rather than derived as an analysis convenience. CONSEQUENCE: deriving the offset is not optional
polish here. Unless LDA $8000 answers with the live bank from tracked in-state, the whole
cec0/cf0b save-restore pair stays opaque and the bank it restores is unknown.

$59 IS NOT A WRITE-THROUGH SHADOW and must not be discovered as one: it is filled from a
READ-BACK (LDA $8000), not from the register being stored to the mechanism. tmnt's actual
write-through shadow is $21, written at cea5 immediately before the chain in the same block --
an easy case for the rule as written, like cv2 $1C and megaman $42. The two must be
distinguished, or the discovery pass will mis-type one of them.

UPDATED TALLY -- FOUR OF FOUR TITLES TRACED BY HAND HAVE AT LEAST ONE BANK SHADOW:
  megaman  $42        write-through, adjacent            rule as written
  cv2      $1C        write-through, 2 bytes before      rule as written
  tmnt     $21        write-through, 2 bytes before      rule as written
  tmnt     $59        READ-BACK save slot                needs the identifying-offset half
  blmaster $DB        write-through, in the wrapper      rule as written
  blmaster $D3        input/save slot, no mechanism write nearby   needs the second route

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WIZWARR $00 IS A COMPOSITE SHADOW -- A SHAPE THE OTHER FOUR TITLES DO NOT SHOW (2026-08-06,
from the wizwarr def-use pass on grm-8iy.5).

Every shadow found so far holds a bank NUMBER: megaman $42, cv2 $1C, tmnt $21, blmaster $DB.
wizwarr's $00 shadows the ENTIRE AxROM REGISTER, which packs the PRG bank in bits 0-2 and the
VRAM page in bit 4. The game manipulates the two fields independently through it:

  ff69:  LDA $00; PHA; AND #$18; ORA $1D; STA $00; STA $8000   ; keep VRAM bits, replace bank
  ce38:  LDA $00; PHA; AND #$F8; ORA #2;  STA $8000            ; keep everything else, set bank 2

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS BEAD:
  - The stored value is ($00 & mask) | arg, so read-back alone is not enough -- recovery needs
    MASK ALGEBRA OVER THE SHADOW, and a notion of which bits of the shadow are the bank.
  - A shadow can be PARTIALLY known: after ff69's merge the bank bits are known from $1D while
    the VRAM bits carry whatever the in-state held. A model that treats a shadow as known or
    unknown wholesale will discard the useful half.
  - The masks the game itself uses are the evidence for the field layout: AND #$18 keeps the
    non-bank bits, AND #$F8 clears the bank bits. Both agree that bank = bits 0-2, which the
    descriptor also declares. Worth CROSS-CHECKING derived field layouts against the masks
    observed in code -- agreement is corroboration, disagreement is a descriptor bug.

This does not block the write-through half of this bead, which wizwarr also exercises normally.
It is an argument for making the shadow's VALUE a masked quantity rather than a plain byte, and
it is better discovered now than after the simple form ships.

RUNNING TALLY, FIVE OF FIVE TITLES TRACED BY HAND HAVE AT LEAST ONE SHADOW:
  megaman  $42   bank number, write-through adjacent          rule as written
  cv2      $1C   bank number, two bytes before the chain      rule as written
  tmnt     $21   bank number, two bytes before the chain      rule as written
  tmnt     $59   READ-BACK save slot (LDA $8000)              needs the identifying-offset half
  blmaster $DB   bank number, written by the wrapper          rule as written
  blmaster $D3   input/save slot, no mechanism write nearby   needs the second discovery route
  wizwarr  $00   COMPOSITE register shadow, masked fields     needs masked-value support

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DOWNSTREAM MEASUREMENT UNBLOCKED BY THIS BEAD (from grm-093, closed 2026-08-08).

grm-093 asked whether runDataflow's helper block being gated on instr.getFlowType().isCall()
(BoardBankAnalyzer:676) silently drops JMP-reached call sites. It turns out that question is
UNMEASURABLE across the whole corpus today, and this bead is what unblocks it.

The reason: every title with JMP-reached call sites has its helper rejected before flow type
is ever consulted. blmaster's FUN_e61b is the clean case -- twelve call sites, seven JSR and
five JMP, and its golden annotates NONE of them, because e61b saves A to ZP $DB and reloads
it later, i.e. it is a shadow-ESTABLISHING wrapper of the same class as cv2's c185 (the
c0f3/c110 declines this bead addresses), not the pass-through class grm-2dr admitted.

WHEN THIS LANDS, measure blmaster specifically: if the seven JSR sites gain "via FUN_e61b"
comments and the five JMP sites (cc6a, df07, df0c, e694, f026) stay silent, isCall() gating
is a real gap and gets its own bead then. If all twelve come back, it never was one.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DESIGN PASS 2026-08-09 (agent). THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S TEXT, then two soundness
hazards that change the shape of the work. Nothing implemented yet.

--- STALE TEXT, verified against HEAD ---

1. THE CONVENTION FALLBACK IS GONE. grm-6pi removed it; MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy:261-263
   now reads "Evaluation only. There is deliberately no convention fallback". So the epic's
   wizwarr acceptance story ("the golden stays byte-identical while the path underneath
   changes") is dead text. Acceptance here is the synthetic fixture plus the derived facts.

2. THE 2d HAZARD IS HALF-SOLVED ALREADY, AND consultsInState SHOULD NOT BE INVENTED.
   cacheable() now has ONE call site (BoardBankAnalyzer:648, matchCache). The requiresOnEntry
   derivation moved to sr.strategy().effectDependsOnPriorState() at :2649, itself a separate
   default on BankSwitchStrategy:242-244 defined as !cacheable(). The right fix is a per-site
   OVERLOAD of the method that already exists, not a new predicate:
       effectDependsOnPriorState(Program, Instruction site, BankState siteInState)
   Widening to three args (not two) matters: passing BankState.unknown() would OVER-report,
   because a mirror answers non-null even when fully unknown. :2649 already reads
   flow.stateIn().get(addr) three lines later, so supplying it is one hoist.

3. THE 2026-08-09 BLMASTER RE-MEASUREMENT NOTE ON THIS BEAD IS SUPERSEDED -- see
   docs/human-research-todo.md's Answered table (commit ef20aad). grm-2dr increment 2 measured
   it: e61b is a FORWARDING wrapper (STA $DB on entry, reloads $DB inside its own body),
   already covered by grm-mu7's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource model, and the isCall() gate
   is refuted outright. blmaster was never blocked on this bead.

--- FINDING 1: THIS BEAD SCOPES CONSUMPTION TO THE WRONG STRATEGY ---

VERIFIED: machines/nes-mmc1.yaml:123 is 'strategy: serial-shift'. Only nes-uxrom.yaml:52,
nes-axrom.yaml:43 and nes-gxrom.yaml:43 are memory-latch.

Section 2c scopes all strategy-side work to MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy. But the 5x STA/LSR
$FFFF chain cited for cv2 ($1C), tmnt ($21/$59) and blmaster ($DB/$D3) IS the MMC1 shift
register -- those are SERIAL-SHIFT boards. Memory-latch covers only megaman ($42), contra,
wizwarr and ironsword, and every one of those is independently blocked by something outside this
bead: megaman's consumer reads $31 (a stateful counter, not the shadow), contra needs the stack
(mej.3), wizwarr/ironsword mask the field out with AND #$18.

So this bead AS WRITTEN discovers the shadows on the three titles that raised it to P2 and then
drops them on the floor. That is the same class of gap as the 2026-08-06 "the rule as specified
is too local to find $D3" comment, one level up.

Serial-shift consumption is nearly free and carries NONE of the 2d hazard --
SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy already threads the real inState into resolveStoredValue (:303),
is already non-cacheable, and already overrides effectDependsOnPriorState() -> false (:358).
Its resolveLoad (:236) is a hard "return null" that stays true for the latch RANGE and is
orthogonal to a RAM shadow or a ROM offset. RECOMMENDATION: consumption lands in BOTH
strategies, as separate commits.

--- FINDING 2a (H1): MIRRORS MUST RANK BELOW STORE-FORWARDING ---

A write-through shadow is written BEFORE the commit, so in that gap the shadow holds the NEW
bank while tracked in-state holds the OLD one. cv2 is exactly this shape:
    c183: STA $1C     ; shadow := new bank (A)
    c185: LDA $1C     ; <-- reads the NEW bank
    c187: 5x STA/LSR  ; commit
StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue's LD<reg> branch (:295-313) calls hooks.resolveLoad FIRST
and returns on any non-null answer -- short-circuiting forwardedStoreValue even for a partial
one. Resolving mirrors inside resolveLoad would therefore PREEMPT grm-mej.1's correct forwarded
value with the STALE in-state: a silently wrong bank on the easiest acceptance case in the bead.

RULE: mirrors are a LAST RESORT. Separate hook resolveMirrorLoad, consulted only after
resolveLoad declines AND forwardedStoreValue returns knownMask() == 0. bankInvariantRomByte
keeps its existing first-place slot (nothing can store to non-writable ROM, so forwarding can
never preempt it).

--- FINDING 2b (H2): SAVE_SLOT MUST NOT RESOLVE FROM IN-STATE ---

This refines the "both kinds resolve from tracked in-state" ruling. tmnt disproves it for the
READ side:
    cec0: LDA $8000 / STA $59    ; save the CURRENT bank
          ... set bank 0, JSR 9016 ...
          JSR cf0b               ; restore PRG bank FROM $59
At the restore, in-state says bank 0; $59 holds the OLD bank. The game saved precisely BECAUSE
it was about to change the bank. Answering LDA $59 from in-state ships a confidently wrong
bank, which this codebase rates strictly worse than no bank.

CORRECT DECOMPOSITION: a save slot's value is established at its STORE site, and that store site
DOES resolve from in-state -- via the ROM_IDENTIFYING mirror at the LDA $8000, which this bead
implements. Carrying it forward to the reload is cross-block memory forwarding = grm-mej.3.
So SAVE_SLOT and INPUT cells enter the mirror set WITH FULL PROVENANCE (for .3 and .4 to consume
and label) but resolveMirrorLoad DECLINES for them. Only WRITE_THROUGH and ROM_IDENTIFYING
answer. blmaster $D3, which carries INPUT|SAVE_SLOT at one address, is delivered and declines.

--- OTHER RULINGS MADE THIS SESSION ---

- Scope: both halves land together (route (a) local backward scan AND route (b) the wrapper-
  argument route), plus the ROM identifying offset.
- The ">= 2 distinct sites" rule counts >= 2 distinct STORE sites, OR 1 store site corroborated
  by a load of the same cell feeding a mechanism write. This admits cv2 $1C, which the literal
  rule rejects. Note cv2's two evidences come from ONE backward scan: walking back from the c187
  chain you cross c185 LDA $1C and then c183 STA $1C.
- Provenance typing with both kinds in the mirror set (as above, subject to H2).

--- DESIGN DETAIL NOTHING HAD PINNED: ADDRESS-SPACE NORMALIZATION ---

The mirror set MUST be keyed by raw long offset, never Map<Address,...>. Address.equals is
space-sensitive, so an overlay-space $8000 would silently miss a base-space entry, and the
failure mode is a SILENT DECLINE that no non-overlay fixture would catch. Membership is
addr.getAddressSpace().getPhysicalSpace().equals(baseSpace) && byOffset.containsKey(getOffset()).
Precedents: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.inLatchRange:448-454 (the canonical form, whose comment
already gives the physical-bus justification) and bankInvariantRomByte:477-481.
Clean interaction: bankInvariantRomByte refuses any overlay-covered offset, and a ROM-identifying
offset in a switchable window IS overlay-covered by construction, so it declines and control
falls through to the mirror path. No reordering needed.

--- COORDINATE CONVERSION: THE EASIEST PLACE TO SHIP A WRONG BANK ---

resolveMirrorLoad must answer in RAW BYTE space, because evaluateLatch applies the byte->field
extraction afterwards at :235-236. So the conversion is field-local -> raw byte, inside the
strategy (the only place that knows "shift"), and byteShift is 0 for ROM_IDENTIFYING (the ROM
byte holds the bank NUMBER right-justified) but "shift" for WRITE_THROUGH.
GxROM check (shift=4, mask=0x3): field-local prg=2 -> byte 0x20 -> (0x20 >> 4) & 0x3 = 2.
Reversed it yields 0 -- a valid-looking bank, no warning, wrong overlay. This is the single most
important unit test in the increment.

--- BLAST RADIUS: THE "ZERO REAL-ROM MOVEMENT" CLAIM DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT ---

cv2 and tmnt are the only expected movers, and only once serial-shift consumption lands. tmnt's
cec0 may gain a correct "bank ->" annotation while its cf0b restore stays unresolved (that is
mej.3). blmaster stays silent ($DB already covered by grm-2dr; $D3 declines per H2) -- which
makes it the free grm-093 JSR-vs-JMP measurement. Everything else silent: facts land, no
consumer exists yet. Commits 1 and 2 must be PROVABLY zero-movement on all twelve.

--- SUGGESTED LANDING ORDER ---
  1. Derivation only, zero consumers (BankMirrors.java, observeMirrors default no-op,
     bankUniverse hoist from :290, pass-2 gate widening). Every golden byte-identical.
  2. Memory-latch consumption -- ATOMIC, cannot be split: resolveMirrorLoad + H1 ordering,
     operandByte, in-state threading, cacheable() -> false, per-site effectDependsOnPriorState
     + the :2649 switch. nesmirrortest fixture lands here.
  3. Serial-shift consumption. No cacheability change. cv2/tmnt measured here, isolated.
  4. Route (b) typing hardening + the grm-093 blmaster measurement.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RULINGS 2026-08-09, resolving the two open questions from the design pass above.

1. CONSUMPTION LANDS IN BOTH STRATEGIES, as separate commits (Finding 1 accepted). Memory-latch
   in commit 2, atomic with the cacheable() flip and the per-site effectDependsOnPriorState.
   Serial-shift in commit 3, isolated -- no cacheability change, so cv2/tmnt movement can be
   accounted for line by line against an otherwise-unmoved baseline. Landing memory-latch alone
   would discover the shadows on the three titles that raised this bead to P2 and then have no
   consumer for them.

2. H2 ACCEPTED -- the 'both kinds resolve from tracked in-state' ruling is NARROWED. SAVE_SLOT
   and INPUT cells enter the mirror set with full provenance, for grm-mej.3 and grm-mej.4 to
   consume and label, but resolveMirrorLoad DECLINES for them. Only WRITE_THROUGH and
   ROM_IDENTIFYING answer from in-state. Rationale is tmnt cec0/cf0b: at the restore, in-state
   says bank 0 while $59 holds the old bank, because the game saved precisely BECAUSE it was
   about to change banks. A wrong bank is strictly worse than no bank. The save slot's value is
   established at its STORE site (which does resolve, via the ROM_IDENTIFYING mirror at the
   LDA $8000); carrying it to the reload is grm-mej.3's cross-block forwarding.

The rest of the earlier rulings stand unchanged: both discovery routes land together, the
'>= 2 sites' rule counts stores-or-corroborated-store, and provenance typing keeps both kinds in
the set with blmaster $D3's dual role tolerated.

title: Local memory store-to-load forwarding in StoredValueScanner (any RAM address, not just ZP)
description:
Increment 1 of grm-mej. Make the backward mask-algebra scan follow a value laundered through a memory cell WITHIN ONE BASIC BLOCK, so a helper that stashes its register argument in RAM and splices it back in is DERIVABLE instead of merely assumed.

MOTIVATING SITE (measured, Ironsword / wizwarr FUN_ffc0, AxROM):
  FFC2: STA $C3        ; stash the caller's bank argument
  FFC4: LDA $C5 / PHA  ; save the current shadow
  FFC7: AND #$18       ; keep the untracked VRAM bits
  FFC9: ORA $C3        ; splice the argument back in -- NON-IMMEDIATE, scan stops here
  FFCD: STA $8000      ; the commit
Bits 0-2 are AxROM's ENTIRE tracked field and come wholly from $C3, i.e. from the caller's A.
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument's javadoc already names this exact gap:
'The engine simply cannot derive it without zero-page store-to-load propagation, which it does
not have.'

*** NOT ZERO-PAGE ONLY. *** The bead text that spawned this says 'zero-page' only because the
measured examples happen to live there ($C3, $C5, $42, $F2, $F9). Nothing here may key on the
zero page:
  - plainAbsoluteTarget (:709-723) already returns an Address for zp and absolute alike; there is
    no separate code path to restrict.
  - The one documented asymmetry runs the OTHER way: effectiveOperandTarget declines zero-page
    INDEXED because it wraps inside the page (:341-346), while absolute-indexed resolves exactly.
  - Contra's save slots are $07EC/$07ED -- RAM, not zero page. A zp restriction would exclude
    exactly the sites grm-mej.3 targets.

IMPLEMENTATION (all in StoredValueScanner.java):
1a. New package-private forwardedStoreValue(...): given a use instruction and a resolved target,
    walk backward within the same basic block for the nearest ST<r> target, then recurse into
    resolveStoredValue on that store for register r. Reuse EVERY existing guard verbatim --
    fall-through block linkage (:195-199), isControlFlowJoin (:200-205), the
    hooks.isMechanismWrite mid-scan abort (:207-211), MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN, and the shared
    Budget/MAX_RESOLVE_DEPTH query tree (:104-136).
    DECLINE on anything between the use and the store that might write the target: a store whose
    effective target is not statically certain, an indexed or indirect store, a read-modify-write
    (storeRegister already returns null for INC/DEC/ASL/LSR/ROL/ROR, :618-624), or a call.
1b. Wire in at TWO places in resolveStoredValue:
    - LD<reg> <mem> (:252-261): when hooks.resolveLoad returns null, try forwarding before
      falling through to the modifier clobber.
    - non-immediate AND/ORA on A (:215-241): today an unconditional bail-out. Resolve the operand
      target with effectiveOperandTarget and try forwarding.
    ACCEPT ONLY A FULLY KNOWN forwarded value (knownMask == 0xFF) in the AND/ORA branches. A
    partial operand would need a third 'forced unknown' accumulator alongside (aAcc, oAcc),
    perturbing the algebra BitAlgebraEquivalenceTest exhaustively proves. All-or-nothing costs
    nothing on the measured case and keeps that proof untouched -- the same reasoning
    constantRegisterValue already documents for itself at :393-398.
1c. DO NOT retire MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy's convention fallback (:295-306). It still covers
    helpers that launder the argument OUTSIDE the switch site's own basic block. Narrow it only
    where measurement shows it stopped firing.

ACCEPTANCE -- a sharp two-sided prediction:
wizwarr's 11 bank comments are recovered TODAY by the convention fallback. After this they must be
recovered BY EVALUATION with THE SAME VALUES: the golden stays byte-identical while the path
underneath changes. If wizwarr's golden MOVES, the forwarding model is wrong. If the fallback
still fires for wizwarr, the forwarding did not reach. Every other golden byte-identical.

TESTS (Tier 2, BankStrategyProgramTest:62-97 idiom; note MemoryLatchStrategyProgramTest:63-70 --
ProgramBuilder blocks are read-only, so zero page must be made writable or bankInvariantRomByte
treats RAM as constant ROM):
  - resolves: the Ironsword shape end to end
  - declines: intervening opaque store to the same target; indexed/indirect store; INC $C3; an
    intervening call; a block boundary; a control-flow join; budget/depth exhaustion
  - works OUTSIDE the zero page: same resolve/decline pair through an absolute RAM address
    ($07EC-shaped), pinning the no-zp-restriction rule against a later quiet narrowing
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERION CORRECTED (2026-08-02). This bead was filed predicting that wizwarr's 11 bank
comments would flip from convention-fallback to derived, with the golden staying byte-identical.
THE GOLDEN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL, BUT THE FLIP DID NOT HAPPEN, and the reason is not a defect in the
forwarding -- it is that depositHelperArgument evaluates the WRONG SITE for this helper. Filed as
grm-6pi (P2). Do not treat the unchanged golden as evidence this bead did nothing; see below for
what was actually measured.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (analyzeHeadless run directly against the isolated build/ghidra-home, with
temporary System.err probes in depositHelperArgument and forwardedStoreValue, since realrom-test.sh
caches candidates and would otherwise have replayed a stale dump):
  - Forwarding FIRES on the real ROM at exactly the predicted place:
        GRMPROBE forward use=ffc9 cell=00c3 store=ffc2 -> 0/0
    ORA $C3 at $FFC9 forwards to STA $C3 at $FFC2. It answers unknown there because that call is
    computeSwitch with env = RegisterEnv.NONE -- no caller, so A genuinely is unknown. Correct.
  - The helper path never reaches it: 20/20 call sites hit 'GRMPROBE fallback at ffd6', and
    'GRMPROBE derived' never printed once. $FFD6 is the RESTORE (PLA / STA $C5 / STA $8000),
    picked by findHelpers' max-address rule; its chain starts with a PLA and cannot resolve.
  - contra and megaman: zero forwards. Nothing in those ROMs launders a bank through memory inside
    a switch site's own basic block.
So increment 1 is CORRECT AND SOUND BUT CURRENTLY UNEXERCISED ON EVERY PINNED REAL ROM. Its value
is the capability plus being a prerequisite for grm-mej.2/.3, not a real-ROM number today.

WHAT PINS IT INSTEAD: src/test/java/retromachines/StoreForwardingProgramTest.java, 11 tests.
The decisive one is ironswordCommitSiteDerivesArgumentLaunderedThroughRam -- it reproduces
FUN_ffc0's shape, evaluates the COMMIT site under a caller RegisterEnv, and passes
argValue = BankState.unknown() so ONLY a derivation can satisfy it (the convention would contribute
nothing). NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the scanner change stashed, exactly the 4 positive tests fail
and all 7 decline tests still pass -- so the suite is not passing vacuously, which is the trap
grm-hum recorded ('the abstracted unit test passed while the real ROM did not move at all').

TWO IMPLEMENTATION FACTS WORTH KEEPING:
1. PHA MUST NOT END THE WALK. Ironsword has a PHA at $FFC6 sitting between the STA $C3 this
   forwards from and the ORA $C3 that consumes it. So the stack hazard is guarded by the CELL
   BEING READ (StoredValueScanner.inStackPage refuses $0100-$01FF) rather than by treating pushes
   as memory writes, which would have killed the motivating case. Verified against Ghidra's
   SleighInstructionPrototype.getResultObject: a STORE contributes a result Address ONLY when its
   offset varnode isConstant(), so PHA (computed from SP) reports only the SP register and
   writesMemory() correctly returns false for it.
2. writesMemory() unions THREE detectors on purpose -- getResultObjects, write references, and a
   mnemonic set -- because each alone has a blind spot: getResultObjects misses computed
   destinations like STA ($10),Y; references are missing for refless stores (the same gap
   writesInRange needs two tiers for); and the mnemonic set is what catches the read-modify-write
   stores, which storeRegister deliberately does not recognize.

GATE AT CLOSE: full headless gate SUITE OK (every golden byte-identical), unit 156/156, full
real-ROM set pass=11 fail=0 skip=1 (smb ROM not supplied).

title: writesInRange misses refless indexed stores and overlay-space write references
description:
Two independent detection gaps in MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange (MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.java:193-203), both found while investigating grm-2yx (2026-07-31). Candidate root cause for Contra's zero-annotation result; scope the fix by what the grm-2yx probe reports.

GAP 1 -- REFERENCE-ONLY PREDICATE. writesInRange inspects ONLY instr.getReferencesFrom(). But a 6502 indexed operand's base arrives as a Scalar, not an Address, so CodeManager lays down NO default operand reference at disassembly time; references appear only once constant propagation covers the code, and const-prop only covers function bodies. The canonical UxROM bus-conflict switch idiom IS 'LDA #n / TAX / STA banktable,X'. So a latch store in code outside any function is invisible even if it is disassembled. Note the class javadoc (:64-67) already ANTICIPATES indexed stores, so this is an unnoticed gap rather than a deliberate limit.

GAP 2 -- DEFAULT-SPACE ONLY. Line :196 requires to.getAddressSpace().equals(space) where space is the default space captured at configure (:130). A latch store EXECUTING FROM INSIDE a PRG_LO_B<n> overlay gets its write reference in the overlay space and is silently skipped. bankInvariantRomByte (:229) already has to undo exactly this normalization, which shows the shape was known elsewhere in the same file.

FIX SHAPE: two-tier predicate -- keep today's reference tier, add an operand-decode tier gated on StoredValueScanner.storeRegister != null (so RMW like INC $8000 keeps reference-only behavior and does not newly poison state), decoding via StoredValueScanner.plainAbsoluteTarget (:341) and LoopIdioms.indexedBase (LoopIdioms.java:82). Normalize the reference tier's space test by OFFSET in a separate commit, since it can move real-ROM goldens.

SOUNDNESS RULING (record in the javadoc): with addr_mask present AND an indexed operand, DECLINE -- base & 0xF says nothing about (base+X) & 0xF, and claiming a match would latch prg_bank off an IRQ-register write, exactly what addr_mask exists to prevent. Declining under-reports, which is the pre-existing failure mode; poisoning with unknown() instead would flood four Bandai goldens with WARNINGs as a side effect of a reachability fix. Do NOT require base+0xFF <= end -- that rejects the canonical $FFE0 bank table.

REGRESSION SURFACE: cacheable() stays true (operand decode is a pure function of (program, instr)). memory-latch is the only cacheable strategy in the tree, so MMC1/MMC3/C64/C128/PET are untouched by construction. Real-ROM goldens that may move: contra, db3, wizwarr (AxROM), dragonpower/shenlong (GxROM), and megaman -- megaman is measurement-only per grm-g73, do NOT bless it.
close_reason: Both gaps fixed (f1251fd, f6adf70) and goldens blessed (638b5c3). Full gate green. Reachability closed and the decline rule confirmed by byte-identical Bandai goldens; the annotation predictions did not hold -- value recovery tracked as grm-hum.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED AND CONFIRMED as the root cause of grm-2yx (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31). Raising confidence and scope -- this affects FOUR real titles, not one.

Per-title (sites / abs / indexed / withWriteRef / wouldMatchToday / invisible-but-reachable):
  contra        1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1   -- 'STA $FFD0,X' at $C142 in FUN_c13f, reachable, no write ref
  dragonpower   1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1   -- identical shape on GxROM
  megaman      25 / 18 / 7 / 18 / 18 /  7   -- the WORKING control still loses all 7 of its indexed sites
  wizwarr      10 / 10 / 0 /  6 /  6 /  4   -- 4 ABS sites with no reference at all

GAP 1 (refless stores) is confirmed and is broader than 'indexed': wizwarr shows refless ABS sites too, i.e. absolute stores in code constant propagation never covered. The operand-decode fallback covers both.

GAP 2 (overlay-space refs) was NOT exercised by any of these titles -- every observed site had ovl=false, so no evidence for or against it here. Keep the fix but expect no golden movement from it on this sample.

EXPECTED GOLDEN MOVEMENT after the fix: contra and dragonpower should go from 0 refs to resolving; megaman +7 sites (coordinate with grm-g73, which is measurement-only per the user); wizwarr +4. dbz2/dbz_datach/dbz_saiyan/db3 should NOT move -- their invisible sites are correct addr_mask decode rejections, and the ruling that an indexed operand with addr_mask present must DECLINE keeps them that way. If a Bandai golden moves, the decline rule is wrong and the change must not land.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED (2026-07-31). Both gaps fixed as specified; the fix works, the
PREDICTIONS DID NOT HOLD. Recording the correction so the next reader is not misled.

WHAT HELD:
- The decline rule is right. All four Bandai titles re-blessed BYTE-IDENTICAL, i.e. the
  stated go/no-go condition passed. zelda/smb3 identical too (MMC1/MMC3 untouched).
- Reachability IS fixed. Contras board-level "no bank-switch write observed" warning is
  gone; the analyzer now sees STA $FFD0,X at c142 and identifies helper FUN_c13f.
- GAP 2 moves nothing, exactly as the probe predicted. Verified experimentally rather
  than by commit boundary: the five moved dumps are byte-identical with and without the
  gap-2 commit. The prescribed split was still honored (f1251fd, f6adf70).

WHAT DID NOT HOLD -- all three annotation predictions were wrong:
- "contra and dragonpower should go from 0 refs to resolving": they did NOT. Both stay at
  0 refs / 0 bank comments; they trade one board-level warning for 6 site warnings.
- "megaman +7 sites": megaman went BACKWARDS -- 1781 -> 1703 overlay refs, 153 -> 151
  bank comments, 3 -> 37 warnings.
- shenlong moved too (1 -> 6 warnings); the issue listed it only as "may move".

ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS: seeing a mechanism write and recovering its value are different
problems. Every newly-visible site is inside a bank-switch helper taking the bank in a
register from its caller, which the block-local backward scan cannot resolve. And
StoredValueScanners mid-scan mechanism-write abort means MORE visible writes = MORE
aborted scans, which is precisely how megaman lost coverage. Filed as grm-hum (P1),
including the open question of whether megamans lost 78 refs were correct or were
artifacts of the blind spot.

DISPOSITION: landed. Goldens blessed for contra/wizwarr/dragonpower/shenlong (638b5c3);
megaman deliberately held back per grm-g73, so the real-ROM tier steady state is
unchanged at 10 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 SKIP.

title: Per-game descriptor tier: title-keyed hints, harvested annotation, and export/reapply
description:
Third descriptor tier alongside per-machine (c64.yaml) and per-board (nes-mmc3.yaml): a descriptor keyed by ROM CONTENT that carries program facts rather than machine facts. Design: docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md; vision: docs/vision-board-banking.md section 5.5 + principle 7 + M4b.

MOTIVATION (measured, not speculative): grm-2yx found Contra (UxROM) and Dragon Ball 3 (Bandai FCG) build a provably correct overlay layout yet resolve ZERO bank annotations, while Mega Man on the SAME board resolves 1781 refs. Static analysis has a real ceiling -- a switch routine entered only via a computed jump, or copied to RAM and executed there, is unreachable by any amount of dataflow. Above that ceiling the honest answer is to RECORD the answer once, not to interrogate the next user for it.

SETTLED DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-31):
(1) DISTRIBUTION: curated in-repo set (machines/games/*.yaml -> data/games/*.map, bundled) PLUS a user-directory overlay scanned at runtime.
(2) IDENTITY: PRG-content hash primary + whole-file SHA-256 alias. Descriptor-declared matching criteria deferred (separate bead).
(3) FORMAT: YAML everywhere -- ship MapCompiler + snakeyaml in the extension so runtime and build read ONE format through ONE validator, and an exported file is directly usable as a PR.
(4) PRECEDENCE: site hints are SEEDS (no precedence question -- they cannot contradict analysis, only give it a starting point); value hints rank below recovered dataflow values and above descriptor defaults, the slot placement overrides already occupy.

THREE USES, ONE ARTIFACT: hints where analysis provably stalls; annotation harvested from mature public disassemblies (Zelda/Metroid/Mega Man/SMB) so a first import beats FUN_c34a soup; portability -- exporting your own annotation layer and replaying it on a fresh import is the same file pointed the other way.

SUCCESS MEASURE: each generation of hint files should be SMALLER than the last. A hint recording something the analyzer should have derived is a defect, not a win.

title: Tier-2 JUnit cannot see bundled sleigh languages (6510:LE:16:default et al)
description:
PROBLEM
`new ProgramBuilder("Test", "6510:LE:16:default")` from `gradle test` throws
LanguageNotFoundException. Every ProgramBuilder-based test in the repo
(BankStrategyProgramTest.java:62, DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzerTest.java:82) is forced onto
the stock `6502:LE:16:default`, so our OWN bundled language has zero Tier-2 coverage --
its only coverage is the Tier-3 headless golden suite, which is slow and coarse
(no per-opcode mnemonic/p-code assertions).

This blocks writing real per-opcode tests for the language variants in grm-azg.

WHY IT FAILS (Ghidra 12.1.2 source)
- Ghidra discovers languages through *module data directories*, not the java classpath, so
  putting data/ on testImplementation would not help.
- `AbstractGenericTest.createApplicationLayout()` (Ghidra/Framework/Generic/.../
  AbstractGenericTest.java:208-209) returns a plain `GhidraTestApplicationLayout`.
- `GhidraTestApplicationLayout.findGhidraModules()` discovers modules under
  `applicationRootDirs` (the Ghidra INSTALL only) filtered by `ClasspathFilter` +
  `getDependentModulePatterns()` -- which is why stock languages work: the pattern set
  includes File.separator + "Processors" + File.separator.
- `GhidraTestApplicationLayout.findExtensionInstallationDirectories()` returns
  `<userTempDir>/ExtensionInstallDir`, NOT the settings dir -- so the
  `-Dapplication.settingsdir` trick that tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh:121-132 uses for
  headless does NOT carry over to JUnit.
- build.gradle:437-441's `test {}` sets no system properties and does not dependsOn
  sleighCompile, and data/languages/*.sla is gitignored, so on a fresh checkout the .sla
  does not exist when tests run.

APPROACH
`createApplicationLayout()` is protected and overridable, and Ghidra's own tests already
use exactly this pattern (Ghidra/Test/IntegrationTest/.../DWARFRegisterMappingsTest.java:52,
TutorialDebuggerScreenShots.java:154 -- both return an anonymous GhidraTestApplicationLayout
subclass).

Add a repo-local abstract base test class that overrides `createApplicationLayout()` to
return a GhidraTestApplicationLayout whose `findGhidraModules()` merges in THIS repo as a
module. The repo root already has Module.manifest + extension.properties, so
ModuleUtilities recognizes it as a module root; data/languages/*.sla is then found the
same way a stock processor module's is.

Then in build.gradle `test {}`:
  - dependsOn 'sleighCompile'   (so the .sla exists)
  - systemProperty for the module dir (projectDir), read by the base class

Hermetic: no extension install, no %APPDATA%, no settings dir -- reads data/languages
straight out of the working tree, so it is safe under parallel git worktrees.

ACCEPTANCE
- A JUnit test doing `new ProgramBuilder("Test", "6510:LE:16:default")` +
  `setBytes(addr, "a9 05", true)` disassembles and asserts mnemonic "LDA".
- Existing JUnit tests unaffected; `build-and-test.sh check unit` green.
- `build-and-test.sh check` (full gate) green.
close_reason: Tier-2 JUnit now resolves 6510:LE:16:default via AbstractBundledLanguageTest, which grafts this repo in as a GModule in the test application layout. All four pre-existing AbstractGenericTest subclasses reparented (required: AbstractGenericTest.initialize() early-returns if already initialized, so the first class constructed wins the layout). Full gate green.

title: c64.yaml declares context_register c64bank no language provides; warns on every analysis
description: BoardBankAnalyzer logs 'context_register c64bank is not a register declared by this language; context stamping skipped' on every C64 disassembly. Cause: machines/c64.yaml:145 still carries the aspirational context_register: c64bank. grm-bk6 decided the bundled 6510 language is system-neutral and declares NO bank-state register; grm-5zg made the field optional and stripped the equivalent fake nesbank from the NES descriptors but missed c64bank; grm-tpg then upgraded the silent skip to a warning as a typo diagnostic, so the leftover placeholder now fires that diagnostic on every run. docs/SCHEMA.md:153-160 already documents the convention: descriptors whose language has no such register omit the property. Fix: drop the field from c64.yaml, keep the design rationale as a comment. Preserves the typo warning for real typos.
close_reason: Removed context_register: c64bank from machines/c64.yaml (design rationale kept as a comment). The name never resolved: grm-bk6 made the bundled 6510 language system-neutral with no bank-state register, grm-5zg made the field optional and stripped the equivalent fake nesbank from the NES descriptors but missed c64bank, and grm-tpg turned the analyzer's silent skip into a warning as a typo diagnostic -- so the leftover placeholder fired that diagnostic on every C64 analysis. SCHEMA.md's documented convention (omit when the language has no such register) is now followed. Verified: freshly built/installed c64.map has its banking block and zero context_register, so stampContextRegister returns at the !banking.has guard before logging. Full build-and-test.sh check green, no golden churn. The typo warning still works for real typos; grm-wkk remains the issue that would introduce a real register.

title: Descriptor build tasks declare no inputs/outputs: every build re-runs all 26 .gdt/.map compilations
description:
The per-machine buildXxxGdt/buildXxxMap tasks (and buildPetsciiMap/buildScreencodeMap) are plain JavaExec with no inputs/outputs declared, so Gradle can never mark them UP-TO-DATE. Every `gradle buildExtension` -- including every tools/install-gui.ps1 run -- forks ~26 JVMs to recompile identical .gdt/.map artifacts from unchanged YAML.

Dependency shape (verified in tools/gdtbuilder):
- MapCompiler/GdtBuilder use YamlSupport.loadComposed, which follows `include:` directives resolved RELATIVE TO THE DESCRIPTOR'S OWN DIR (all current uses point at machines/fragments/nes-common.yaml).
- Both also resolve `source:` keys (register sets / type defs) the same relative way -- all current uses point at machines/generated/*.yaml.
- PetsciiCompiler: single plain load of machines/generated/petscii.yaml.
- ScreencodeCompiler: plain load of both petscii.yaml and screencode.yaml.
- The compiler classes themselves are an input: a gdtbuilder source change must invalidate outputs.

So a per-task input of just its own yaml would be WRONG (stale on fragment/generated/compiler edits).

sleighCompile already declares inputs/outputs correctly; this is the same treatment for the descriptor pipeline.

REPORTED BY: user, observing tools/install-gui.ps1 rebuild everything unconditionally.
close_reason: Declared inputs/outputs on all 26 per-machine buildXxxGdt/buildXxxMap tasks plus buildPetsciiMap/buildScreencodeMap. Shared input is fileTree('machines', excludes:['*.yaml']) -- Ant '*' does not cross '/', so it drops sibling top-level descriptors but keeps fragments/ and generated/, covering both the include: and source: reach; gdtBuilder classes are an input too. No-op rebuild now 38/38 up-to-date in 1s (was 25s). Full gate green.

title: Extension zip ships repo metadata: .beads Dolt DB is 30 MB of a 31 MB extension
description:
The built extension packages the entire repo working directory, not just the extension. Top-level entries in dist/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC_20260725_ghidra-retro-machines.zip include .agents, .beads, .claude, .codex, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs, gsrc, machines, tools -- alongside the legitimate lib, data, ghidra_scripts, extension.properties, Module.manifest.

SIZE (uncompressed, by top-level entry):
  30.75 MB  .beads      <-- the Dolt issue-tracker database
   0.47 MB  tools
   0.41 MB  lib         <-- the actual extension
   0.21 MB  docs
   0.20 MB  data
   0.16 MB  machines
So the shipped artifact is roughly 75x the size of the code it exists to deliver (15.6 MB compressed, essentially all of it the beads DB), and installing it drops a full copy of the project issue tracker -- including every issue description and note -- into the user's Ghidra Extensions dir. Confirmed on disk: the pre-2026-07-25 GUI install at %APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/Extensions/ghidra-retro-machines/ contained .beads/issues.jsonl, export-state.json and last-touched.

FIX POINT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNUSED. build.gradle carries the stock comment 'Exclude additional files from the built extension / Ex: buildExtension.exclude .idea/**' with no actual excludes below it. Adding excludes there is the documented mechanism.

CARE REQUIRED -- do not blanket-exclude. data/ IS read at runtime (the loaders read data/machines/<id>.map and the .gdt archives), so it must stay. machines/ holds the authored YAML that the gdtBuilder compiles INTO data/ at build time and is probably not needed at runtime, but that needs proving rather than assuming. Verify with the full acceptance gate after any exclusion, since a wrongly-excluded resource would surface as a loader failure, and note that tools/banktest's dump cache key includes the extension identity so a contents change is expected to invalidate it.

RELATED: grm-9ut (release-build strategy on GitHub Actions) should not ship artifacts in this shape; fixing this is effectively a prerequisite for publishing a release.

DISCOVERED: while writing tools/install-gui.ps1 (the GUI install helper), which installs exactly this zip.
notes:
2026-07-25 (Chris): PREFER AN ALLOWLIST over adding excludes. Being deliberate about what ships is the right shape here -- a denylist silently ships whatever new top-level file or dir lands next (this bug exists precisely because Ghidra's stock denylist predates .beads/.claude/.agents/.codex), whereas an allowlist fails loudly and safely: forget an entry and a resource is MISSING, which the acceptance gate catches, rather than silently leaked.

MECHANISM (read from D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/support/buildExtension.gradle:94-142). buildExtension is a Zip task assembled from three child specs: from(extension.properties) with token filtering, from(project.jar) into lib/, and -- the culprit -- from(project.projectDir) carrying a FIXED exclude list: build/**, *.gradle, certification.manifest, dist/**, bin/**, src/**, .gradle/**, .vscode/**, .classpath, .project, .pydevproject, .settings/**, developer_scripts, .antProperties.xml, gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/*. That list is Eclipse-era and knows nothing about our layout. It lives in the install's support/ file, and our build.gradle marks that region DO NOT MODIFY, so we cannot edit the spec directly -- we can only add via buildExtension.exclude/.include from the designated hook in our own build.gradle.

SUGGESTED SHAPE -- allowlist as the source of truth, fed through the supported hook, so it is fail-safe without forking the stock task or fighting Gradle's root-vs-child CopySpec pattern semantics (a bare root-level include risks filtering the jar and extension.properties children too, and should not be attempted without testing):

  def SHIPPED = ['lib', 'data', 'ghidra_scripts', 'extension.properties', 'Module.manifest', 'README.md', 'LICENSE'] as Set
  projectDir.listFiles().each { f ->
      if (!(f.name in SHIPPED)) { buildExtension.exclude f.name; buildExtension.exclude f.name + '/**' }
  }

Anything new at the top level is then excluded by default and must be added deliberately.

STILL TO PROVE before landing, do not assume: which entries are genuinely runtime-required. data/ IS (loaders read data/machines/<id>.map and the .gdt archives). ghidra_scripts/ and Module.manifest are Ghidra-required. gsrc/ and machines/ (authored YAML compiled into data/ at build time) are probably not, but verify. Run the full acceptance gate after: a wrongly-excluded resource surfaces as a loader failure, and tools/banktest's dump cache key includes the extension identity, so expect cache invalidation on the first run.
close_reason: Allowlist added at build.gradle's buildExtension.exclude hook; zip 16.9 MB -> 510 KB, top level now exactly lib/data/ghidra_scripts/extension.properties/Module.manifest/README.md/LICENSE. machines/ proven droppable (findFilesByExtensionInMyModule -> accumulateDataFilesByExtension walks data/ only). gradle.properties was also leaking (stock denylist covers *.gradle, not *.properties). Full acceptance gate green.

title: Reference-precedence retargeting: redirect refs from base to a copied overlay
description: Constructive complement to the overlay-friction bead. Once a copied overlay exists at a destination, it holds the authoritative bytes and can be assumed to take precedence over base. An analyzer pass could then override the default reference creation for addresses covered by such an overlay -- retargeting incoming references (e.g. JSR $0073) from base:dst to the overlay copy program-wide, rather than bridging each call site one at a time (as grm-1.7.1's per-site bridgeJump does). Depends on the run-from-elsewhere materialization (grm-1.7.1) existing to mark which ranges are overlay-backed copies.
notes: 2026-07-25 (grm-chu): NARROWED. grm-chu changed the default materialization for a verbatim copy into uninitialized RAM to an in-place carve in the BASE space, so those copies now resolve incoming references natively -- a JSR/JMP at the destination address hits the materialized code with no retargeting at all. Program-wide reference-precedence retargeting is therefore no longer needed for the common run-from-elsewhere case. This bead still applies to (a) the overlay FALLBACK path (destination already initialized, straddling two blocks, or already in an overlay space -- see TransferMaterializer.canCarve) and (b) banking overlays generally, which remain the real motivator. Consider re-titling toward banking if the fallback path alone does not justify it.

title: Real-ROM reachability gap: Contra (UxROM) / DB3 (Bandai FCG) bank-switch routine never disassembled, so no mechanism write is ever seen
description: Root cause behind grm-9oz's silent-zero (now diagnosed by a WARNING bookmark). On Contra (U) (UxROM/m2) and Dragon Ball 3 (Bandai FCG/m16) the correct overlay layout is built but the forward dataflow classifies ZERO stores as mechanism writes -- no bank comments/refs. Contrast Mega Man (same UxROM board) which resolves 1781 refs. Hypothesis (issue grm-9oz (a)): the switch routine is reached only via an indirect/table jump that auto-analysis never disassembled, so MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange() (src/main/java/retromachines/MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.java:193) never runs on the real store. Distinct from grm-m95 (Bandai FCG/GxROM sites that ARE detected but whose VALUE is unrecoverable). Candidate directions: (a) seed disassembly of the switch routine (follow indirect/table-jump targets), or (b) a ROM-wide scan for in-range writes independent of dataflow reachability, feeding those sites into runDataflow. Repro: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir> (contra, db3); the new 'no bank-switch write observed' WARNING bookmark now flags exactly these titles.
close_reason: Diagnosed and superseded. The premise in the title is disproven: Contra's bank-switch routine is disassembled, in a function, and reachable -- BankReachProbe measurement recorded in the comments. The real cause is a detection bug in writesInRange (grm-3x1, now measured across four titles), and DB3's separate RAM-resident-stub cause is split to its own bead. Nothing left under this title that is not tracked more accurately elsewhere. The probe that produced the diagnosis is committed as tools/banktest/BankReachProbe.java (d3d1da0).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PROBE RESULTS (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31) -- THE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD IS WRONG.

Contra's bank-switch routine IS disassembled, IS inside a function, and IS reachable from the seed set. This is NOT a reachability gap.

  BANKREACH site c142 mech=0 reg=A mode=IDX base=ffd0 ovl=false decode=MATCH func=FUN_c13f reach=YES refs=1 write=NO today=NO space=RAM
  verdict.i   orphan-sites 0            <- NOT case (i)
  verdict.ii  no-site-in-disassembled-code false   <- NOT case (ii)
  verdict.iii invisible-reachable-sites 1          <- CASE (iii), decisively

Root cause: 'STA $FFD0,X' at $C142 in FUN_c13f -- the canonical UxROM bus-conflict bank table at $FFD0. It carries NO write reference in range (write=NO), so MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange, which inspects only instr.getReferencesFrom(), never sees it. Exactly grm-3x1 gap 1.

NOT ISOLATED -- cross-title measurement (sites / abs / idx / withWriteRef / wouldMatchToday / invisible):
  contra        1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1     all lost
  dragonpower   1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1     IDENTICAL shape (GxROM)
  megaman      25 / 18 / 7 / 18 / 18 /  7     works only because 18 ABS sites carry it; loses all 7 indexed
  wizwarr      10 / 10 / 0 /  6 /  6 /  4     4 refless ABS sites lost
  db3           1 /  1 / 0 /  1 /  0 /  1     see below
  smb3, zelda   no memory-latch mechanism (MMC3/MMC1) -- probe correctly finds nothing

So the indexed/refless gap is systematic across memory-latch boards, not a Contra quirk. Fixing grm-3x1 should resolve Contra and dragonpower outright and add sites on megaman/wizwarr.

DB3 IS A DIFFERENT STORY: its single disassembled site is mode=ABS with a write reference but decode=MISS -- i.e. correctly rejected as a sibling CHR/IRQ register write, not the PRG bank register. There is NO PRG-register write anywhere in DB3's disassembled code, which confirms the RAM-resident-stub hypothesis in substance. Splitting per plan.

PROBE CAVEAT worth knowing: verdict.iii conflates 'wrongly missed' with 'correctly rejected by the addr_mask decode'. On dbz2/dbz_saiyan it reports ~50 because those boards have ~50 sibling register writes that SHOULD be rejected. The per-site decode= column disambiguates; read it, not the verdict, on addr_mask boards.

ACTION: retitle/repoint this bead at grm-3x1 as the fix, or close it in favour of grm-3x1 + the DB3 split.

title: Real-ROM tier: megaman dump is bistable run-to-run (refs -1 / instrs +2), flaky golden
description: The megaman (UxROM, mapper 2) real-ROM golden (grm-zai) pins refs.intoOverlay=1781 and instrs.inOverlay=7437. During grm-y20, two consecutive fresh imports both produced 1782/7435 -- a stable shift -- while the bank-> comment text stayed byte-identical (so this is unrelated to the grm-y20 comment-format change). Ghidra auto-analysis on a large real ROM (7400+ instrs) appears bistable in disassembly/ref counts (likely analysis thread-scheduling nondeterminism), making exact-count assertions in RealRomDump goldens fragile for large ROMs. Options: (a) tolerate small deltas on large-ROM count lines; (b) replace exact instrs.inOverlay/refs.intoOverlay with a coarser bucket for real ROMs; (c) root-cause the bistability. Not blocking -- real-ROM tier is opt-in, out of CI. The megaman golden is intentionally left at 1781/7437 (currently FAILs on check) pending this decision.
notes: Discovered while blessing zelda+smb3 for grm-y20; only megaman among the 12 pinned titles showed count drift. contra/wizwarr/db3/dbz2/datach/saiyan/dragonpower/shenlong all still PASS; smb SKIP (not in indexed dir).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 REPRODUCED EXACTLY, and confirmed unrelated to the grm-1.7.x work. Running the real-ROM tier on H:/emulators/nes/ROMs, megaman is the ONLY failing row, and its whole diff is:
  - REALROM count refs.intoOverlay 1781   -> 1782
  - REALROM count instrs.inOverlay 7437   -> 7435
i.e. verbatim the pair this bead already records. No COPY_ blocks are involved (the copy-loop recognizer produces none on megaman after the evidence gate landed), so nothing in the run-from-elsewhere work touches it. Deliberately NOT blessed: the value would just flip again on the next run.

Useful datum for whoever fixes this: the counts move in OPPOSITE directions (refs +1, instrs -2), which smells like an analysis-order race rather than a simple off-by-one -- one extra reference resolving into an overlay appears to cost two instructions somewhere else.

ALSO, a separate real-ROM harness bug found and FIXED this session (commit 375c4f5), which was masking everything else: realrom-test.sh never stripped CR when parsing manifest.tsv, so on a Windows CRLF checkout whichever column happened to be LAST on a row carried a trailing backslash-r into a path. That surfaced as 'golden not found: .../expected/contra.dump' for files plainly present, and made 4 of 5 supplied ROMs fail for a reason that had nothing to do with their content. If this bead was ever investigated on Windows before now, the observations may have been taken through that fog.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-29, grm-phv: the refs.intoOverlay BASELINE for megaman has legitimately moved, so
whoever fixes this bead must re-baseline rather than compare against 1781/1782.

MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer (grm-phv) retargets indexed 6502 references from the computed
address to the addressing mode's base, which COLLAPSES N computed refs per indexed access
(one per index value the propagator resolved) into ONE base ref. Measured on this corpus:

  megaman  refs.intoOverlay  1781 (golden) -> 1704     [-77, ours]
  megaman  instrs.inOverlay  7437 (golden) -> 7435     [the pre-existing drift value this bead records]
  smb3     refs.intoOverlay   871 -> 846               [-25, ours; blessed]
  zelda    refs.intoOverlay   unchanged                 [only sample.ref 8094 moved ::8029 -> ::8028; blessed]

So megaman's instrs.inOverlay=7435 is still exactly the alternate value recorded here, NOT
something grm-phv caused -- the bistability is unchanged. Only the ref count moved, and for a
deliberate reason.

megaman.dump was deliberately NOT blessed, honoring this bead's standing decision ("the value
would just flip again on the next run"). It still FAILs on check, now with refs 1781 -> 1704
instead of 1781 -> 1782. zelda and smb3 WERE blessed (their diffs are one line each, both
explained above).

When this bead is resolved, the correct new pin for megaman is refs.intoOverlay=1704 with
instrs.inOverlay still bistable between 7435 and 7437.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEGAMAN BASELINE for the grm-3x1 fix (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31), captured per the measure-don't-bless decision.

Probe today: sites.total 25, sites.abs 18, sites.indexed 7, sites.inFunction 24, sites.orphan 1, sites.reachable 25, sites.withWriteRef 18, sites.wouldMatchToday 18, verdict.iii invisible-reachable-sites 7.

So megaman currently resolves via its 18 absolute sites and loses all 7 indexed ones to grm-3x1.
