When that fix lands expect roughly +7 switch sites and a corresponding change in refs/comments/instruction counts. megaman.dump stays DELIBERATELY UNBLESSED; record the post-fix delta here rather than accepting it.

Real-ROM tier re-run 2026-07-31 with the probe attached: 10 PASS / 1 FAIL (megaman, expected) / 1 SKIP (smb) -- same as 08af5e8, so the probe itself perturbs nothing.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TOOLING (grm-hb6.1, 2026-08-01): realrom-test.sh now takes --only/--except <comma-separated manifest ids> on both check and bless, so the 'megaman is deliberately unblessed' state this bead created is now expressible directly:

  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh bless --except megaman H:/emulators/nes/roms Z:/nes/db

Previously bless had no ID filter, so sparing megaman meant staging the other ten ROMs into a separate directory by hand -- easy to get quietly wrong, and the failure mode was blessing away the very golden this bead depends on. An id that is not in the manifest is now a hard error (exit 2) rather than a no-op, precisely so a typo in the exclusion cannot bless the title it was meant to spare. Filtered rows report as filtered=N, never SKIP.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
STILL BISTABLE after grm-hum, with NEW numbers (2026-08-02). The pair is now:
  refs.intoOverlay 1704 / instrs.inOverlay 7429   <- blessed
  refs.intoOverlay 1703 / instrs.inOverlay 7431
(was 1781/7437 vs 1782/7435 before grm-hum). Same shape: refs and instrs move in
OPPOSITE directions by small amounts, consistent with a race or iteration-order
dependence in the phase-2 disassembly cascade rather than a value-recovery difference.
Note the delta is now 1 ref / 2 instrs, where it used to be 1 ref / 2 instrs -- unchanged
in magnitude, so grm-hum neither worsened nor fixed it.

Consequence: `realrom-test.sh check` on megaman flaps between PASS and FAIL run to run.
Everything else in the 12-title set is stable. Do NOT read a megaman FAIL as a regression
without diffing -- if the ONLY differing lines are those two counts, it is this bead.

ALSO FIXED THIS SESSION (grm-hum, commit 55dfc05): the CRLF half of this bead's
"diagnostic trap" note is gone. .gitattributes now pins *.dump to eol=lf, so a golden
written by bless (LF) is no longer rewritten to CRLF by the next checkout. That was
making byte-identical goldens present as whole-file replacements. The bistability above
is the remaining, genuine half.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-08-02, second filing merged. grm-h4k was filed independently against this same defect and
is closed as a DUPLICATE of this bead. What it adds beyond what was already recorded here:

  - RATE: 4 fresh imports of the same ROM against the same build split 3/1 (three at the golden
    1704/7429, one at 1703/7431). n=4 -- do NOT treat 1-in-4 as the true rate.
  - THE OBSERVER IS EXONERATED. BankReachProbe was attached to three of the four. It is genuinely
    read-only, it runs as a -postScript AFTER RealRomDump has already printed, and both a run WITH
    it and the one control run WITHOUT it passed. The variable is the analysis, not the probe.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN STANDING STATE, which the earlier comments get wrong: megaman
WAS re-blessed, at grm-hum (commit 71959b1), to refs.intoOverlay=1704 / instrs.inOverlay=7429.
The "deliberately NOT blessed, always FAILs" posture recorded in the 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-31
comments is SUPERSEDED. Practical consequence, and it is a worsening: the row no longer FAILs
consistently (a marker you can recognize), it FLAPS between PASS and FAIL (noise you cannot).

Fixing the stale statements of that posture in tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh, docs/testing.md,
and the nes-rom-library bd memory is part of the work on this bead.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
LOCALIZED, 2026-08-02. The difference is a DISASSEMBLY-ALIGNMENT divergence -- the same bytes
decoded from different instruction boundaries -- confined to ONE overlay (PRG_LO_B5) in three
tight clusters inside a ~1KB span. Not a value-recovery difference: bankComments is 156 in both.

Method: new read-only diagnostic tools/banktest/DeterminismProbe.java emits EVERY overlay
instruction (address + length, no bytes/mnemonics) and EVERY ref into an overlay, sorted,
unbounded. Attached via the existing REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT hook so it costs no extra import.
Two runs' blocks diffed = 30 changed lines out of 9137. Its own counts agree with RealRomDump's
on the same import, so the two are measuring the same thing.

  GOLDEN 1704/7429                 ALTERNATE 1703/7431
  instr a528 len=1                 instr a527 len=2
  instr a660 len=2                 instr a65e len=3
  instr a662 len=1                 instr a661 len=3
                                   instr a664 len=2
                                   instr a666 len=3
  instr a903 len=3                 instr a904 len=1
  instr a906 len=2                 instr a907 len=1

  refs GAINED by the alternate: a666 -> a677 UNCONDITIONAL_JUMP
  refs LOST   by the alternate: a906 -> a912 CONDITIONAL_JUMP, a925 -> a999 DATA
  net -1 ref / +2 instrs -- exactly the pair this bead has tracked across three baselines.

All addresses are in PRG_LO_B5 and all sort above a527, consistent with the free bound the
golden already gave: its 25 sample.ref lines span 80b2..9070 and are identical in both outcomes,
so the moving ref had to be above 9070.

MECHANISM (verified in the Ghidra 12.1.2 source, D:/git/ghidra on tag Ghidra_12.1.2_build).
ConstantPropagationAnalyzer -- which our Mos6502ConstantReferenceAnalyzer extends and whose
added() it inherits unchanged -- dispatches per-location flow walks to a TWO-thread ConcurrentQ
(:192, maxThreadCount default 2 at :69). Two independent races follow:

  (a) AbstractAnalyzer :170-193, the worker's first act is
        synchronized (analyzedSet) { if (analyzedSet.contains(loc)) return EMPTY_ADDRESS_SET; }
      so whether a location is analyzed AT ALL depends on whether the sibling thread's walk
      already covered it. Binary per location.
  (b) ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator :228-234 commits disassembly INLINE on the worker
      thread -- getUndefinedDataAt() then DisassembleCommand.applyTo() -- bypassing the analysis
      manager's single-threaded queue. That is a non-atomic check-then-act, and 6502 instruction
      alignment is 1, so every byte is a legal instruction start: two seeds a byte apart give two
      different self-consistent decodings and the first thread to arrive wins permanently
      (Disassembler :489). That is precisely the shape observed above.

The narrow, fixed race window explains why this is BISTABLE (~25/75) rather than drifting.

IN PROGRESS: bisection via -Dcpu.core.override=1, which SystemUtilities :454-459 short-circuits
getDefaultThreadPoolSize() with, sizing every GThreadPool to 1 and bounding maxThreads to 1 at
AbstractAnalyzer :196-198. realrom-test.sh already exports GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS, so this
needs no code change to test.

TRAP worth recording: analyzeHeadless -max-cpu 1 does NOT do this. It sets cpu.core.limit, and
SystemUtilities :488-490 computes Math.max(1, limit+1) -- so -max-cpu 1 yields a pool of TWO,
exactly the racy configuration.

ORTHOGONAL SUSPECT that would SURVIVE cpu.core.override=1, if the split persists:
DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer :106 uses `Collection<Function> definedFunctions = new HashSet<>()`.
FunctionDB.hashCode() returns super.hashCode() and DatabaseObject overrides neither hashCode nor
equals, so that is System.identityHashCode -- the set iterates in a DIFFERENT order every JVM
run regardless of thread count. It feeds ParallelDecompiler directly, and its command deletes
refs, creates labels and disassembles (DecompilerSwitchAnalysisCmd :126,133,136). NES ROMs use
JMP (indirect) tables, so this analyzer is live on megaman.

STILL OPEN: which outcome is CORRECT. Determinism is not correctness -- one of these two
decodings of PRG_LO_B5:a527..a925 is wrong, and pinning the run does not by itself say which.
Answer that before re-blessing.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WHICH OUTCOME IS CORRECT? NEITHER. That is the answer, and it matters for how this gets closed.

Reconstructing byte coverage from the probe dumps (instruction address + length gives exact
extents) shows each outcome wins some clusters and loses others:

CLUSTER 1 -- a521..a529.  ALTERNATE is better.
  golden: a521+3, a524+2, a526+1, [a527 UNCOVERED], a528+1, a529+2   <- 1-byte hole
  alt:    a521+3, a524+2, a526+1, a527+2,            a529+2          <- contiguous

CLUSTER 2 -- a65c..a669.  ALTERNATE is better, decisively.
  golden: a65c+2, [a65e-a65f HOLE], a660+2, a662+1, [a663-a668 HOLE], a669
  alt:    a65c+2, a65e+3, a661+3, a664+2, a666+3, a669               <- contiguous, meets both
                                                                        neighbours exactly
  The alt's a666+3 is the 3-byte JMP that yields the `a666 -> a677 UNCONDITIONAL_JUMP` ref, and
  it terminates the block exactly where a669 resumes. The golden's version leaves an 8-byte
  hole across two gaps and a stream that connects to neither neighbour.

CLUSTER 3 -- a901..a908.  GOLDEN is better.
  golden: a901+2, a903+3, a906+2, a908+3                             <- contiguous
  alt:    a901+2, [a903 HOLE], a904+1, [a905-a906 HOLE], a907+1, a908+3

Totals reconcile exactly: alt = golden +2 instructions and +6 covered bytes
(+1 cluster 1, +8 cluster 2, -3 cluster 3), and 15887 vs 15881 bytes over 7431 vs 7429
instructions. So the arithmetic of the whole bistability is accounted for with nothing left over.

CONSEQUENCE: do NOT "just bless the other one". There is no good side of this race -- whichever
run you keep, you are keeping a locally-degraded disassembly somewhere. The fix has to remove the
race; the golden then follows from it.

BOTH RACES ARE FIRING, not just the alignment one. The ref `a925 -> a999 DATA` is present in the
golden and absent in the alternate, while `instr a925 len=3` is IDENTICAL in both. Same
instruction, different reference -- that cannot be an alignment effect. It is the
`analyzedSet.contains(loc)` skip (AbstractAnalyzer :170-193) changing which entry contexts get
walked at all, i.e. mechanism (a) from the previous comment, independent of mechanism (b).

Mechanism (b) is confirmed to be capped by the bisection flag: ConstantPropagationAnalyzer
:360-362 reads
    if (maxThreadCount > pool.getMaxThreadCount() || maxThreadCount < 1) { maxThreadCount = 1; }
so a pool sized to 1 by -Dcpu.core.override=1 forces this analyzer's thread count to 1 as well.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, 2026-08-02 (user's insight: the seed at a528 comes from a switch target, not
from flow). It is not "a race" in the abstract -- it is a SPURIOUS JUMP TABLE planting ~32 bogus
disassembly seeds, and the race is merely which seed reaches a byte first.

THE TABLE. PRG_LO_B5:a734 is a 3-byte `JMP ($a737)`. The REAL table at a737 is EIGHT entries,
16 bytes, a737..a746, and every entry is sane:
    a747 a76d a784 a7a1 a7cd a7fa a827 a893
Entry 8 would sit at a747 -- which IS the table's own first target, i.e. code. Ghidra's switch
recovery read straight past the end of the table into the code it dispatches to and reinterpreted
instruction bytes as little-endian addresses.

MEASURED FROM THE ROM: all 40 recovered COMPUTED_JUMP targets map back to even offsets in
a737..a835. That is a 255-byte read of a 16-byte table -- 239 bytes of OVER-READ. Of the ~120
garbage values produced, 40 happened to land inside the $8000-$BFFF bank window and so became
COMPUTED_JUMP references; the rest fell outside and were dropped. Sample of the garbage, with
the table offset each came from:
    a75b -> a9a9    a769 -> a660    a773 -> a9a7    a777 -> a963
    a765 -> a9c4    a771 -> af20    a775 -> 8580    a77b -> a964
Adjacent "targets" one byte apart (a960/a961/a963/a964, a9a7/a9a8/a9a9, 8502/8503) are the
signature: real dispatch tables do not have entries one byte apart.

THIS EXPLAINS ALL THREE DIVERGENCE CLUSTERS, not just one. Every cluster address is in the bogus
target list:
    cluster 1  a528   <- garbage target; contends with the real 2-byte instruction at a527
    cluster 2  a660   <- garbage target; contends with the contiguous flow decoding from a65e
    cluster 3  a906, a908 <- garbage targets; contend with flow around a903
So the "alignment race" is a spurious COMPUTED_JUMP seed racing legitimate flow-following
disassembly for the same bytes, at exactly the addresses this over-read named. Whichever arrives
first wins permanently (Disassembler :489, and 6502 alignment is 1 so every byte is a legal
start). That is the whole bistability.

PROVENANCE: not ours. `grep -rE 'COMPUTED_JUMP|JumpTable|createJumpTable|switchTable'` over
src/main/java finds NOTHING. The refs come from Ghidra's decompiler switch recovery
(DecompilerSwitchAnalysisCmd, which disassembles table targets); BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences
only re-homes them into the bank overlay, which is why they surface as PRG_LO_B5::-to-PRG_LO_B5::.

BISECTION RESULT -- -Dcpu.core.override=1 (all thread pools to 1):
  * It DOES appear to fix the flapping: 3/3 runs so far byte-identical (arm still running).
  * But it produces a THIRD value, 1698 refs / 7413 instrs, distinct from BOTH bistable outcomes.
  * It LOSES coverage: 15834 bytes disassembled in overlays vs 15881 (golden) and 15887 (alt).
  * And the bogus table is UNTOUCHED -- still exactly 40 COMPUTED_JUMP refs from a734.
So single-threading is a determinism band-aid that costs ~50 bytes of disassembly and leaves the
actual defect in place. It converts "wrong in a different place each run" into "wrong in the same
place every run". NOT shipping it on this evidence. (A maxThreadCount=1 override in
MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer was drafted and REVERTED for exactly this reason -- do not re-add it
as a fix for this bead without re-reading this comment.)

THE REAL FIX is to stop the table over-read, which is upstream behavior. Filing separately.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION -- -Dcpu.core.override=1 does NOT fix this. The previous comment reported "3/3 runs
byte-identical, appears to fix the flapping" from a partial arm. The completed 12-run arm
falsifies that:

  11 runs: refs 1698 / instrs 7413   (15834 bytes covered)
   1 run:  refs 1703 / instrs 7430   (15885 bytes covered)   <- run10

So forcing every Ghidra thread pool to 1 changes the RESULT (a third and fourth distinct value)
but does NOT remove the nondeterminism -- it lowers the flip rate, roughly 1-in-12 here against
6/6 stable in the control arm, both small samples. Do not read either rate as reliable.

The outlier has exactly the same signature as the original bistability: one-byte alignment
shifts, and again at bogus-table addresses.
    stable-11               outlier run10
    a527 len=2              a528 len=1          <- a528 is a garbage COMPUTED_JUMP target
    a544 len=2, a546 len=2  a542 len=3, a545 len=3
    a699 len=2              a698 len=3
    a92f len=1              a92e len=3, a931 len=3, a934 len=2, a936 len=1, a937 len=3, ...

WHAT THIS RULES IN. A source of nondeterminism that survives a single-threaded pool. The
candidate identified earlier and now strongly supported is DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer :106:
    Collection<Function> definedFunctions = new HashSet<>();
FunctionDB.hashCode() returns super.hashCode(), and DatabaseObject overrides neither hashCode nor
equals -- so this is System.identityHashCode and the set iterates in a DIFFERENT ORDER ON EVERY
JVM RUN, thread count irrelevant. That set is fed to ParallelDecompiler, and
DecompilerSwitchAnalysisCmd (applied inside the worker) deletes references, creates labels and
DISASSEMBLES table targets (:126,133,136).

That closes the loop with the over-read table: the SAME analyzer both (i) manufactures the ~32
spurious seeds by reading 239 bytes past the end of a737's 8-entry table, and (ii) applies them
in an order that varies run to run for reasons unrelated to threading. Capping threads was never
going to be sufficient.

STANDING CONCLUSION FOR THIS BEAD: there is no configuration-level workaround. The fix has to
address the table over-read itself. Everything downstream -- which seed wins which byte, which
count the golden lands on -- is a consequence.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THIS IS NOT ONE TITLE AND IT IS NOT BISTABLE. Measured 2026-08-03 on a full 31-row
'check --all' plus targeted repeat runs, clean tree, no analyzer change in the session (only
tools/banktest probe scripts moved).

FULL-CORPUS BASELINE: pass=27 fail=4 skip=0. The four failures are ALL count-line-only diffs --
no sample line, no comment text, no block list moves:

  megaman    refs.intoOverlay 1704 -> 1703                                   (this bead)
  ff1        refs 1880 -> 1847, instrs 7426 -> 7382, warnings 618 -> 604     (grm-4nr)
  dodge      refs 2739 -> 2740, warnings 299 -> 298                          (NEW)
  rcproam    refs 1298 -> 1296                                               (NEW)

So the instability touches at least 4 of 31 rows, not 1. This bead's title says "megaman dump is
bistable"; the accurate statement is that the real-ROM corpus has a run-to-run nondeterminism in
overlay REFERENCE counting that surfaces on whichever titles are near a tipping point.

DODGE DISPROVES "BISTABLE". Six runs (one baseline + five targeted), same build, same ROM:

  refs=2740 warnings=298
  refs=2739 warnings=298
  refs=2736 warnings=299
  refs=2739 warnings=298
  refs=2736 warnings=299
  refs=2739 warnings=299   <- the golden

THREE distinct refs values {2736, 2739, 2740} and FOUR distinct (refs,warnings) combinations.
The two counters are NOT correlated -- refs=2739 pairs with warnings 298 AND 299 -- so this is not
one switch flipping, it is at least two independent sources of variation. Any fix that assumes a
single binary divergence will not cover this.

rcproam is flaky but mostly stable: 1296 in the baseline, then 1298 (== golden) on two consecutive
targeted runs.

>>> THE STRONGEST STRUCTURAL CLUE, AND IT IS NEW: instrs.inOverlay IS STABLE WHERE refs IS NOT.
Across all six dodge runs instrs.inOverlay is 10692 every single time while refs moves three ways;
rcproam holds 4810 while refs moves; megaman holds its instrs while refs moves. The ONE title
where instrs also moves is ff1 (7426 <-> 7382), which is also the only one whose delta is large
(33/44/14 rather than 1-3). That splits the phenomenon in two:

  (a) a common, small, REFERENCE-ONLY jitter -- same instructions disassembled, different number
      of references recorded into overlays. Since instrs.inOverlay is identical, the same code is
      being reached; only ref creation/dedup differs. Suspect the reference side specifically
      (addOverlayRef's existing-reference reuse and setPrimary, or MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer's
      indexed-base retargeting from grm-phv), not disassembly scheduling.
  (b) ff1's much larger divergence where instructions themselves move -- a genuinely different
      amount of code reached. That is the one that looks like the analysis-order race this bead
      originally hypothesised, and it is tracked separately in grm-4nr.

Whoever fixes this should re-scope the bead title, use dodge as the reproducer (cheapest: 3 runs
usually show 2+ values) and treat (a) and (b) as possibly different bugs. DeterminismProbe.java
already exists for exactly this and localized megaman to PRG_LO_B5 a527..a925.

OPERATIONAL NOTE: the "if those two count lines are the ONLY diff it is grm-g73" rule now applies
to four titles and to warnings as well as refs. Do NOT bless any of them to make check green --
the value flips again on the next run.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THIRD BISTABLE TITLE: dodge (Super Dodgeball, MMC1). Observed 2026-08-09 while measuring grm-2dr
increment 2 across the GME corpus.

  refs.intoOverlay   2739 -> 2736   (-3)
  instrs.inOverlay   10692 (=)
  bankComments       29 (=)
  warnings           41 (=)
  sample lines       ZERO changes

DEFINITELY NOT CAUSED BY grm-2dr INCREMENT 2, and this was demonstrated rather than assumed. Same
binary, same working tree, three consecutive runs within ~20 minutes:
    run 1 (full --gme sweep):   PASS
    run 2 (full --gme sweep):   FAIL, the diff above
    run 3 (--only dodge):       PASS
It flipped back on its own. Increment 2 was applied in all three.

WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. It carries the signature this bead and
grm-4nr both describe -- A COUNT MOVES WHILE NO ANNOTATION DOES -- in its purest form yet: exactly
one count line changes and literally nothing else, so there is no room to argue the delta reflects
a real analysis difference. That makes dodge a better minimal reproducer than either megaman
(refs -1 / instrs +2) or ff1 (refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14, which also moves warnings).

It also widens the population usefully. megaman is UxROM (mapper 2), ff1 and dodge are MMC1
(mapper 1), and dodge at 10692 overlay instructions is the LARGEST of the three -- consistent with
this bead's "large ROM" framing, and against any theory tied to one board family.

DEODGE'S GOLDEN WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BLESSED. It is currently correct in its stable state.

FEEDS THE OPEN "bistable-golden distribution" ITEM in docs/human-research-todo.md (run the tier ~10
times, keep every dump, ask whether the titles co-flip). Three known instances now, and dodge's
single-line delta is the cheapest one to run that experiment against.

title: Silent zero-detection: some banked real ROMs get correct layout but no bank annotations OR warnings (Contra m2, Dragon Ball 3 m16)
description: Found in grm-hdn real-ROM acceptance (tools/banktest/realrom, goldens contra.dump/db3.dump). On Contra (U) (UxROM/mapper 2) and Dragon Ball 3 - Gokuu Den (Bandai FCG/mapper 16) the loader builds the correct block/overlay layout (7 and 7 overlay banks resp.) but the analyzer emits ZERO bank-> comments, ZERO cross-bank overlay refs, ZERO banked instructions, AND ZERO warnings. Contrast Mega Man (U) -- same UxROM board -- which resolves 1781 overlay refs / 153 comments. The zero-WARNINGS part is the concern: the forward dataflow never classified any store as a mechanism write, so the user gets no signal that banking analysis found nothing (vs. the 'undeterminable value' warnings other titles do get). Likely the bank-switch routine is reached only via an indirect/table jump that auto-analysis never disassembled, so the mechanism write is never seen. Investigate: (a) is the switch code unreached (banked-code reachability), or (b) is a real store being silently skipped by the memory-latch scanner? At minimum, surface a diagnostic when a board declares a switch mechanism but the analyzer observed no mechanism writes at all. Repro: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir> (contra, db3).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Fixed the 'silent' concern (the at-minimum ask): BoardBankAnalyzer now emits a WARNING bookmark 'no bank-switch write observed' on the settled/fixpoint-stable run when a board declares bank-switch mechanism(s) but zero mechanism writes (switchResults + callSwitches) were observed; it retracts the bookmark if a later settled run does find a write, so it reflects only the settled state. RealRomDump counts it, so contra.dump/db3.dump go warnings 0->1 (re-blessed). All chunks + full acceptance gate pass; only contra/db3 goldens changed. Root-cause reachability (why the switch is unreached) split out to grm-2yx.

title: grm-z15 #5: PRG placement coverage validation (prg_placeable flag + MapCompiler check)
description: Regression #5: planPrgSlices throws mid-import on matching.size()!=1 (a map gap/overlap in RAM placement coverage), and nothing validates coverage at build time. The C64 P6510 placement target is kind:io, invisible to a generic kind-based check. Fix (user decision): introduce a prg_placeable:true region flag (schema + MapCompiler.buildRegions passthrough), set on P6510 in c64.yaml; C64PrgLoader.isAdditionalPrgTarget reads the flag instead of the hardcoded name 'P6510'. Add a machine-neutral MapCompiler coverage check: union(kind:ram regions, prg_placeable regions, per-window-collapsed ram-occupant ranges) must be internally contiguous with no gaps/overlaps, else IllegalArgumentException naming the gap/overlap. Keep the loader's matching.size()!=1 throw as defense-in-depth. MapCompilerVerify: add verifyRamCoverage negative tests (ram gap + ram overlap fail; gapless map with a prg_placeable io region compiles).
acceptance_criteria: A gapped/overlapping RAM map fails to COMPILE with a clear error naming the gap/overlap; shipped c64.yaml still compiles (gate re-compiles it); loader reads prg_placeable instead of the P6510 name hardcode; verifyMapCompiler passes with new negatives; full gate green.
close_reason: Added prg_placeable declarative flag (base isAdditionalPrgTarget reads it; C64PrgLoader name-hardcode override deleted; c64.yaml P6510 flagged, behavior-identical). MapCompiler.validateRamCoverage rejects a gapped/overlapping RAM placement union at COMPILE time, gated on formats.prg.placement:load_address (fires for c64/pet4032/c128, correctly skipped for NES whose non-contiguous RAM is loaded by NesRomLoader). MapCompilerVerify negatives (gap+overlap) + positive (prg_placeable io region) added. All three CBM maps still compile; full gate green. Commit b0ac942.

title: grm-z15 #4: degrade path aborts (windows NPE guard + honest up-front skip validation)
description: Regression #4: (a) planPrgSlices (~550) iterates map.getAsJsonArray('windows') unguarded though load() guards map.has('windows') (369) — NPE on a windows-less map. (b) When window setup is skipped (banking incomplete, ~374-378), window-occupant slices never get a placement space and persistPrgPlacement throws 'No address space was created for PRG target ...' (720-723), aborting the import the skip message promised to survive. Fix: guard the planPrgSlices windows loop on map.has('windows'); when window setup will be skipped, decide up front — if any planned PRG slice targets a window occupant, throw a clear IOException naming the incomplete banking + the needed window placement, instead of the deep persist throw; otherwise (no window-targeted slices, PET-like) proceed. Verification is inspection-level + the existing PET windows:[] path; the incomplete-banking C64 path can't be fixtured without map-injection plumbing (loader hardwires machines/c64.map) — file a P4 follow-up for a malformed-map harness.
acceptance_criteria: Windows-less map plans region slices with no NPE; a skipped-window map with window-targeted slices fails with a clear message (not the deep persist throw); PET no-window path still imports; full gate green. Regression-4 runtime coverage documented as inspection-level with a filed follow-up bead.
close_reason: planPrgSlices now guards map.has('windows') (no NPE on a windows-less map). When banking is incomplete, load() fails up front with a clear message if any PRG slice targets a banked-window occupant (windowOccupantSliceTargets), instead of the confusing deep persistPrgPlacement 'No address space' abort; otherwise the skip proceeds (PET-like). Both need a hand-edited map to reach; verified by inspection + existing PET windows:[] path. Fixture deferred to grm-abg. Full gate green. Commit 6f1894a.

title: grm-z15 #3: struct typing across a carved init/uninit boundary (per-field fallback)
description: Regression #3: AbstractCbmPrgLoader.createCarvedTarget (~632-633) applies a region struct at region.start even when PRG slices split the region into initialized+uninitialized blocks; DataUtilities.createData cannot span a memory-block boundary in Ghidra 12.1.2, so it fails (only logged) and the 6510 port registers are left untyped. Repro: load $FF00, 0x101 payload (wrap places 1 byte at $0000, so R6510 at $0000-$0001 straddles). Fix: add a per-field fallback in DescriptorSupport.applyStructType — keep whole-struct createData as the fast path; on failure, if the resolved type is a Structure, createData each getDefinedComponents() component at start+component.getOffset(), catching/logging per field. R6510 is DDR@0 + PORT@1 (two 1-byte fields), so DDR@$0000 types even when PORT@$0001 is in a separate block. Single-block callers never hit the fallback (unchanged). Fixture: prgstraddletest.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapped $FF00 import leaves the R6510 DDR field typed at $0000 (port registers no longer fully untyped); single-block struct typing unchanged; prgstraddletest golden passes; full gate green.
close_reason: Regression #3 does NOT reproduce in Ghidra 12.1.2: built the reviewer's exact repro (load $FF00, 0x101 payload -> R6510 straddling init $0000 / uninit $0001) as headless fixture prgstraddletest; Listing.createData spans the carved block boundary fine (whole R6510 struct typed, len=2, neither field dropped). The reviewer's 'createData can't span a block boundary' premise is empirically false. No code change needed; kept prgstraddletest as a permanent guard. Full gate green. Commit be78857.

title: grm-z15 #1+#2: restore unconditional entry point + 2-byte zero-payload PRG acceptance
description: Regression #1: AbstractCbmPrgLoader.java entry block (~454-485) gates addExternalEntryPoint on entryBlock.isExecute(); a load address in a non-executable block (e.g. $0000 P6510 io) silently gets no entry point/function/log. Fix: call addExternalEntryPoint unconditionally (old behavior — records entry only, no code assumption); keep markAsFunction gated on executableEntry; add a log line when the function mark is skipped for a non-exec entry block. Regression #2 (user decision: RESTORE acceptance): lower findSupportedLoadSpecs threshold 3->2; in load(), when prgLength==0 build the full map/symbols but skip placement, label the load address with a clear log, do not resolve an entry against absent slices; remove the now-reachable dead prgLength==0 throw. Fixtures: prgentrytest (load $0000, non-exec P6510) and prgemptytest (2-byte zero payload) in the c64-loader chunk.
acceptance_criteria: PRG at $0000 gets an external entry point + no function + a log explaining the skipped function mark; 2-byte PRG imports under C64PrgLoader with full map/symbols; new prgentrytest/prgemptytest goldens pass; full gate green with existing goldens byte-identical.
close_reason: addExternalEntryPoint now unconditional (entry point recorded even for a non-exec load block, e.g. $0000 P6510); markAsFunction still gated on executability with an explanatory log. 2-byte zero-payload PRG accepted again (threshold 3->2, dead throw removed, dedicated zero-payload entry path). Fixtures prgentrytest/prgemptytest added. Full gate green, existing goldens byte-identical. Commit c2cbecb.

title: Single source of truth for targeted Ghidra version (currently 12.1.2)
description: User decision 2026-07-19: one canonical declaration of the targeted Ghidra version, everything else by reference; user commits to keeping the D:\ install and the D:\git\ghidra checkout in step with it. Implementation: (1) gradle.properties: ghidraTargetVersion=12.1.2; conventions derived from it: install dir D:/ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC, source checkout on tag Ghidra_<ver>_build. (2) build.gradle guard: after resolving ghidraInstallDir (env var wins per stock header), read <install>/Ghidra/application.properties application.version and throw GradleException on mismatch with ghidraTargetVersion, message naming both versions and the fix — converts the stale-GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR-env-var trap into a loud failure. (3) tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh: derive default GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL/GHIDRA_HEADLESS from gradle.properties ghidraTargetVersion instead of the hardcoded D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC (existing env overrides preserved). (4) CLAUDE.md: replace literal 12.1.2 mentions (build section, 'Reading Ghidra source code' section) with references to the property + the two conventions. (5) bd memory build-ghidra-install-dir: update to point at property + guard rather than naming a version. DO NOT start while another agent is editing tools/banktest scripts.
acceptance_criteria: grep -r '12.1.2' over CLAUDE.md and tools/banktest finds only derived/comment uses or none; gradle with a mismatched install fails with the guard message; full build-and-test.sh check green.
close_reason: Landed: gradle.properties ghidraTargetVersion=12.1.2 canonical; build.gradle version guard (verified failing correctly against a 12.0.4 path and passing against 12.1.2); banktest scripts derive defaults; CLAUDE.md de-literaled; bd memory build-ghidra-install-dir updated. Full gate SUITE OK.

title: PETSCII string search analyzer, system.text descriptor key, headless fixture
description: Phases E+F-fixture of the grm-1.4 plan. MapCompiler.buildSystem passes system.text through verbatim (~6 lines; buildSystem currently whitelists keys) + MapCompilerVerify assertion. Add system.text blocks to machines/c64.yaml, pet4032.yaml, c128.yaml: { encoding: petscii, variant: <match machine petscii_variant>, string_search: { min_length: 4 } }. New PetsciiStringAnalyzer: descriptor-gated via DescriptorSupport.MAP_PATH_PROPERTY (mirrors C64BasicAnalyzer conventions, AnalyzerRunLog), gated on PRESENCE of system.text.string_search, late priority; StringSearcher(Program, CharSetRecognizer, minLen, 1, false, false) with recognizer accepting 0x20-0x5F (+0xC1-0xDA shifted); callback skips non-1-byte-datatype finds (UTF-16 side-scan guard), acts only on fully-undefined ranges, applies TerminatedPetsciiStringDataType when trailing 0x00 else fixed PetsciiStringDataType via DataUtilities.createData CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA. Fixture: tools/banktest/mkpetsciistringtest.py C64 PRG with terminated + unterminated strings both cases, too-short decoy, graphics-run negative case; golden dump; new build-and-test.sh chunk petscii-strings (+ verifyCharsets in its checks, basic-petscii, and all).
acceptance_criteria: New petscii-strings chunk green; golden shows expected PetsciiString data and untouched decoys; full gate green.
close_reason: Analyzer + descriptor key + fixture landed. system.text passthrough with verify; PetsciiStringAnalyzer types terminated/fixed PETSCII runs (undefined-only, UTF-16 guard, terminator-in-range convention documented); petscii-strings chunk green; full gate SUITE OK with all pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: PETSCII charset SPI, TableCharset, six string datatypes, verifyCharsets
description: Phases C+D+F-gradle of the grm-1.4 plan. (C) retromachines.charset.RetroCharsetProvider (CharsetProvider SPI; lazy, exception-swallowing init — a throwing provider poisons Charset.availableCharsets() JVM-wide; loads compiled maps via getResourceAsStream, NO Ghidra imports) + TableCharset (int[256]->codepoint decoder, surrogate-aware maxCharsPerByte=2; codepoint->canonical-byte encoder maxBytesPerChar=1) + META-INF/services/java.nio.charset.spi.CharsetProvider. Charset names: x-petscii-unshifted (aliases petscii, x-petscii), x-petscii-shifted (alias petscii-shifted), x-c64-screencode-unshifted (alias c64-screencode), x-c64-screencode-shifted (screencode charsets may initially be absent until grm-1.4.5's map exists — provider must tolerate a missing resource per-charset). Gradle: stageCharsetResources Copy task data/*.map -> build/generated-resources/retromachines/charset/, wired into sourceSets.main.resources + processResources (buildExtension packs project.jar per buildExtension.gradle:117 — verified, resources will ship). (D) Six fixed-charset AbstractStringDataType subclasses in retromachines/data/ following StringDataType pattern (no-arg ctor, (DataTypeManager) ctor, clone, static dataType singleton; non-null charsetName hardwires charset): PetsciiStringDataType, TerminatedPetsciiStringDataType, PetsciiShiftedStringDataType, TerminatedPetsciiShiftedStringDataType, ScreencodeStringDataType, ScreencodeShiftedStringDataType (screencode fixed-length only). (F) tools/charset/CharsetProviderVerify.java + verifyCharsets JavaExec task (own source set; classpath = main output + staged resources + gson): proves real ServiceLoader SPI in plain JVM; asserts charsets resolve by name+alias, decode == PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode for all bytes x variants, canonical round-trip.
acceptance_criteria: verifyCharsets passes in plain JVM; extension zip contains the services file and staged .map resources; datatypes auto-discovered (headless check in grm-1.4.4).
close_reason: Charset SPI + datatypes landed: RetroCharsetProvider/TableCharset (lazy, failure-swallowing), 6 fixed-charset string datatypes, stageCharsetResources jar wiring (dist-zip verified), verifyCharsets 1037 cases green in plain JVM. Full gate SUITE OK.

title: PETSCII unicode layer: petscii.yaml schema 2, compiler expansion, PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode
description: Phase A of the grm-1.4 plan. Add a unicode: section to machines/generated/petscii.yaml (schema 2): C0/C1 pass-through for controls (codepoint = byte value, user-confirmed), true glyphs for ASCII divergences (0x5C GBP U+00A3, 0x5E U+2191, 0x5F U+2190), full per-variant graphics table (box drawing U+2500s, block elements U+2580s, Symbols for Legacy Computing U+1FB00-FF), mirror rules (0xC0-DF=0x60-7F, 0xE0-FE=0xA0-BE, 0xFF=0x7E) decoding to canonical glyphs, provenance block for the Unicode mapping source. PetsciiCompiler accepts schema 2, emits unicode_variants (2x256 codepoints) + encode (codepoint->canonical byte) into data/petscii.map beside the existing variants: key; escaped-layer output must stay byte-identical (frozen petcat convention; basic-petscii/basic-dialects goldens guard). PetsciiMapper parses the layer, adds toDisplayUnicode(int|byte[], Variant) and loadFromStream(InputStream) (loadFromMapFile refactored onto it). PetsciiMapperVerify extended: unicode completeness 256x2, mirror equivalence, control policy, encoder canonicalization round-trip encode(decode(b))==canonical(b).
acceptance_criteria: verifyPetsciiMapper passes with new unicode checks; full build-and-test.sh check green with byte-identical existing goldens; toDisplayUnicode defined for all 512 byte-variant combos.
close_reason: Unicode layer landed: petscii.yaml schema 2, compiler expansion (escaped layer byte-identical), PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode/encodeUnicode/loadFromStream, verify extended to 4480 cases. Full gate SUITE OK.

title: C64PrgLoader entry/degrade-path regressions from arbitrary load-address rework
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727 (grm-dvx arbitrary PRG load addresses). Five related regressions vs the old fixed-0x0801 loader, all in src/main/java/retromachines/C64PrgLoader.java:

1. ENTRY POINT SILENTLY DROPPED (CONFIRMED, ~line 409): entry creation is gated on entryBlock.isExecute(); a load address landing in a non-executable block (P6510 io-kind at $0000, canExecute=false) gets a label but no external entry point, no function, and no log message. Old loader added them unconditionally. Repro: full-memory-snapshot PRG with load address $0000.

2. 2-BYTE HEADER-ONLY PRG REJECTED (CONFIRMED, ~line 210): findSupportedLoadSpecs minimum went 2 -> 3, so a zero-payload .prg falls through to the raw Binary loader instead of importing with the full C64 map/symbols as before; also makes the prgLength==0 IOException (~272) dead code.

3. STRUCT ACROSS CARVED BOUNDARY (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 556): createCarvedTarget applies the region struct (2-byte R6510) at the region start even when slices split the region into initialized+uninitialized blocks; createData fails (only logged), 6510 port registers left untyped. Repro with shipped map: load $FF00, 0x101 payload (wrap covers only $0000).

4. DEGRADE PATH ABORTS (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 644): when banked-window setup is skipped ('skipping banked-window setup'), window-occupant slices never get a placement space and persistPrgPlacement throws 'No address space was created for PRG target RAM_A000', aborting the import the skip message promised to survive. Sibling: planPrgSlices (~494) NPEs on a map with no windows array — a shape load() explicitly supports. Both need hand-edited/variant maps today (MapCompiler always emits the keys) but the loader's own code claims to support the shapes.

5. PLACEMENT GAPS ABORT IMPORT, NO VALIDATOR (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 532): != 1 placement targets per PRG byte now throws instead of the old log-and-single-block degrade. Shipped c64.yaml is gapless today, but nothing (MapCompiler or CI) validates coverage, so the first map edit that opens a gap breaks every spanning PRG import.

Suggested split if needed: 1+2 are quick behavioral fixes; 3 needs applyStructType to skip/split when the region is carved; 4 wants either upfront validation with a clear error or a real degrade; 5 wants a MapCompiler coverage check.
acceptance_criteria: PRG at $0000 gets an entry point (or an explicit log explaining the drop); 2-byte PRG imports with C64 map again or the rejection is deliberate+documented; wrapped $FF00 import leaves R6510 typed; skipped-window and gap cases either import degraded or fail with a clear validation error, covered by banktest fixtures.
notes: Item #3 (struct across carved boundary) was PLAUSIBLE and does NOT reproduce in Ghidra 12.1.2 -- verified empirically in grm-z15.2 (fixture prgstraddletest): createData spans an init/uninit block boundary fine, so R6510 types correctly at $0000-$0001. Resolved as a guarded non-bug, no code change.
close_reason: All five reviewed regressions resolved across sub-beads z15.1-z15.4: #1 entry point restored (unconditional external entry + gated function mark + log), #2 2-byte PRG accepted again, #3 verified NOT reproducible in 12.1.2 (createData spans a carved block boundary; kept a guard fixture), #4 degrade path made honest (windows NPE guard + up-front clear error), #5 compile-time placement coverage check + declarative prg_placeable flag. Follow-ups: grm-abg (malformed-map harness for #4 runtime coverage), C128 P8502 prg_placeable. Full gate green throughout.

title: AnalyzerRunLog lifecycle: markCompleted fires on failure paths and before the phase-2 follow-on round
description:
From /code-review of codex commits 065577e..fd17727 (commit 837148d, grm-olp quieting). Two confirmed defects in when AnalyzerRunLog.markCompleted is called:

1. FAILURE PATHS CONSUME THE ONE-SHOT VERBOSITY: BoardBankAnalyzer.added() calls markCompleted on the map-load IOException path (~line 228), BoardModel.parse null (~234), and empty-mechanisms (~244); C64BasicAnalyzer does the same on gdt/petscii open failures (~175/185). A transient first-run failure permanently silences the first *successful* run (no 'running', no helper list, no summary) — and AnalyzerRunLog has no reset API.

2. MARKED BEFORE THE FOLLOW-ON FULL ROUND: markCompleted fires at the end of round 1 (~line 337), but the adjacent LAST_COMPLETED comment documents that phase-2 disassembly side effects deliberately trigger a framework re-run 'in full'. That completing round of the same initial analysis runs verbose=false, so the only summary ever logged carries stale round-1 counts.

Fix direction: mark completed only after a successful, fixpoint-reached run (e.g. move the body into doAdded() and mark at the single wrapper exit only when the run did real work and the LAST_COMPLETED fingerprint matches), and consider an AnalyzerRunLog reset when analysis config changes. Also note markCompleted call sites are copy-pasted on ~9 exit paths across the two analyzers — a structural wrapper removes the whole class of miss.
acceptance_criteria: First successful analysis after a failed run logs verbosely; the summary logged reflects the final (fixpoint) round's counts; regression covered by a banktest fixture or unit check.
notes: Implementation staged 2026-07-18: AnalyzerRunLog uses a v2 persisted key so saved Programs polluted by the old failure policy get one clean retry; C64BasicAnalyzer centralizes completion so false/exception/cancellation paths remain initial while successful work/no-ops complete; BoardBankAnalyzer defers summary, cache stamp, and completion until entry/exit function+instruction fingerprints are stable, and no longer completes descriptor/resource/strategy failure paths. Regression additions cover legacy-key migration, failure followed by verbose successful BASIC retry, real banking v2 completion, and the fixpoint predicate. Validation completed: production compileJava PASS; VerifyBankTest.java standalone compilation against Ghidra 12.1.2 jars PASS; diff check PASS; independent final review found lifecycle logic sound. Remaining before closure: run focused c64-banking + basic-petscii and full headless suite. Attempts were blocked before execution by the external-execution account usage limit (resets 2026-07-25), not by a test failure.
close_reason: Completed by follow-on session after in-flight agent hit its session limit. Implementation (staged by that agent, reviewed here): AnalyzerRunLog v2 persisted key (one clean verbose retry for Programs polluted by the old failure policy); C64BasicAnalyzer added()->analyze() wrapper so completion is recorded at a single exit (failures/cancellation/exceptions stay retry-eligible, successful work and no-ops complete); BoardBankAnalyzer defers summary + LAST_COMPLETED stamp + completion until the entry/exit structural fingerprint is stable (reachedFixpoint), so phase-2 changing rounds stay verbose and the one summary carries final counts. Validation: orchestrator + independent subagent review clean; focused c64-banking + basic-petscii chunks PASS (new B5 lifecycle criterion demonstrates failure-stays-incomplete + verbose retry); FULL build-and-test.sh check PASS. Known gap noted: C7/C8 cover banking completion + fixpoint predicate but not a BoardBankAnalyzer-specific failure-retry/legacy-key scenario (B5 covers those only for C64BasicAnalyzer).

title: Analyzers: quiet routine logging on re-analysis runs, verbose only on first pass
description: The retromachines analyzers emit routine log output on EVERY added() call -- i.e. every time instructions are (re)disassembled, including manual/incremental disassembly after the initial autoanalysis, not just the first full autoanalyze run. BoardBankAnalyzer is the worst (23 log.appendMsg); C64BasicAnalyzer (8) and others also log per-run summaries. Desired: the first full autoanalyze run may be verbose, but SUBSEQUENT runs should be quiet -- only log messages of Great Importance (genuine warnings/errors), suppressing routine INFO/summary chatter. Approach options: (a) set a marker after the first analysis (a program property / Options flag) and gate routine logging on its absence; (b) detect incremental vs full (added-set size, or whether prior analysis state exists); keep WARNING/error bookmarks always on. Applies to BoardBankAnalyzer + C64BasicAnalyzer + any analyzer with per-run summary logging. Observed by user after the grm-mbm GUI test.
close_reason: Implemented persistent per-analyzer initial-run logging policy. BoardBankAnalyzer now gates six routine progress/summary messages and C64BasicAnalyzer gates its run banner after the initial attempt; all warnings, failures, malformed-input messages, and warning bookmarks remain unconditional. Markers live in Program.ANALYSIS_PROPERTIES and are isolated by concrete analyzer class. compileJava and buildExtension pass against Ghidra 12.1.2.
