title: Self-modifying code strategies: run-from-elsewhere, decrypt-on-the-fly, cross-processor code upload
description: Umbrella for making the extension useful on the self-modifying-code patterns retro software actually uses — an axis Ghidra has traditionally handled poorly (static listing assumes bytes at an address are THE code). Three concrete use-case families (children), plus a cross-cutting question: the Ghidra Debugger's emulator/trace machinery may be leverageable for all of them (execute the copier/decryptor in the p-code emulator, capture the resulting memory image, feed it back into static analysis) — traditionally SMC was hopeless statically, but Debugger-assisted 'run it, then analyze what it produced' changes the economics. Design tension to resolve early: which patterns deserve STATIC modeling (descriptor-driven, like banking) vs EMULATION-ASSISTED recovery vs manual workflow documentation. Relationship to banking engine (grm-5tl): banking changes which pre-existing bytes are visible; SMC creates NEW bytes at analysis time — different problem, but the overlay/alternate-view plumbing and the analyzer-pass architecture are shared infrastructure.
notes: 2026-07-12 grm-1.7.4 survey COMPLETE — design tension RESOLVED, full findings in docs/smc-survey.md. Machinery: EmulatorHelper is @Deprecated(since 12.1, forRemoval=true); all emulation work targets ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator + PcodeEmulationCallbacks (readUninitialized = IO fault policy hook, dataWritten = exact dirty-set capture) + EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (plain-emulator harness, no Trace needed). Interpreted emulator is SMC-safe by construction (SleighInstructionDecoder re-decodes each instruction from live state; avoid JIT emulator for SMC). In-tree precedent: EmuX86DeobfuscateExampleScript. DEBUGGER (per user direction, evaluated first-class): pure-emulation mode + GUI Copy Into Program = the manual/interactive tier (document in grm-fy0); headless Trace round-trip buys nothing over direct Memory.setBytes; TraceRmi retro connector (VICE/Mesen) does not exist and stays NO-GO until demonstrated need — VICE .vsf snapshot import is the cheap 80% (real-hardware-fidelity memory image, zero protocol work). Approach split: 1.7.1 STATIC now; 1.7.2 emulation pilot; 1.7.3 static-first with SPC700 language sourcing as new prerequisite (stock Ghidra has NO SPC700 sleigh — SPCdra is the community candidate). Shared EmulationRecovery harness bead created; reuses the same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer the banking vision picked for L4 (§7.1) — one callback stack serves both features.

title: State-field packing has no cumulative-width validation (>32 bits silently corrupts)
description: MapCompiler.java:604. parseStateFields accepts each field with bits<=31 but never checks the SUM. packState does packed |= fieldValue << shift; shift += bits. Once cumulative shift >= 32, Java shifts are mod-32 so the field wraps into low bits and packed int corrupts. Failure: two 20-bit fields (sum 40) -> second field overwrites first, wrong initial_state/states.value, no error. Fix: reject total width > 32. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed. Added a cumulative-width check in parseStateFields: sum of all banking.state field widths must be <= 31. Refined the bead's '>32' threshold to '>31' via primary-source evidence: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:193 derives the whole-state mask as (1 << stateBitNames.size()) - 1 where stateBitNames has one entry PER BIT, so total==32 gives (1<<32)-1 == 0 (empty mask) in addition to packState's mod-32 shift wrap. Cap at 31 keeps both the packing and the runtime mask correct. Verified: all descriptors+sketches still compile; a sketch with two 20-bit fields (total 40) now fails at build with 'banking.state total width 40 bits exceeds 31'.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: Truncated ROM: vector read past EOF throws uncaught IOException out of load()
description: NesRomLoader.java:345. checkRange validates window offsets against the DECLARED prgSize, never actual file length. A .nes declaring 32KB PRG with a 16KB body passes all gates; the high window block creation fails-and-is-swallowed but is still added to placed; labelVectorTargets then readBytes(fileOffset,2) past EOF -> IOException propagates out of load() (try/finally does not catch it), aborting import with an exception dialog instead of a logged skip. Fix: validate declared PRG against provider length up front, or guard the vector read. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed by option (a): validate declared PRG against actual provider length up front, right after InesHeader.parse. If header.prgFileOffset()+header.prgSize() > provider.length(), log 'Truncated iNES image...' and return gracefully. Placed BEFORE any resource allocation (board resolution, gdt open, block creation) so the early return leaks nothing. This is the right-altitude fix: guards the single trusted invariant (declared==actual PRG bytes) once, covering both the swallowed block-creation failures and the previously-unguarded vector read at labelVectorTargets (provider.readBytes past EOF -> IOException out of load() -> exception dialog). No NES headless test harness exists (banktest is C64-only); verified by compile + reasoning.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: MapCompiler accepts maps: keyword offset that the runtime cannot resolve
description: MapCompiler.java:66 (EXPR_KEYWORDS includes offset) vs DescriptorSupport ExprParser.parseFactor (no offset case) and referencedFields (excludes only last/second_last). A descriptor using offset compiles clean but at load time referencedFields returns {offset}, which != the banked field name, so NesRomLoader logs needs exactly one banking.state field and never places the window (or env.get(offset) throws). Valid-looking descriptor -> silently incomplete memory map. Fix: either drop offset from the compiler keyword set or implement it in the runtime. Verdict CONFIRMED.
notes: Fixed by DROPPING offset from the grammar (not implementing it). Rationale: the loader places every computed window as a CONTIGUOUS Ghidra block, so the window-relative CPU offset is added IMPLICITLY by the affine mapping; evalExpr returns one base offset per window/bank with no per-byte term. 'offset' in an expression would double-count (PRG[bank*0x4000+offset]) or be misread as a state field (PRG[offset] -> referencedFields {offset} -> 'unknown state field'). It was also unused by every descriptor. Removed offset from MapCompiler.EXPR_KEYWORDS + its javadoc; synced docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/MAP_FORMAT.md, docs/vision-board-banking.md to state the offset is implicit. Verified: all machines/*.yaml + sketches recompile clean; a sketch using 'offset' now fails at BUILD time ('identifier offset is neither a banking.state field nor one of [second_last, last]') instead of compile-clean/fail-at-load. Runtime (DescriptorSupport.ExprParser) needed no change -- it never claimed offset.
close_reason: Dropped the unimplementable/unused 'offset' keyword; compiler grammar + docs now match the runtime. Build-time rejection verified.

title: Descriptor include/shared-fragment mechanism (NES boards duplicate regions/symbols/types 6x)
description: The six NES board descriptors (nes-nrom + 5 discrete mappers, grm-4iq) copy memory.regions, symbols, types, formats, and validation verbatim because the schema has no include/composition mechanism. Every PPU/APU struct fix must now be applied six times. Add a shared-fragment mechanism to MapCompiler/GdtBuilder (e.g. 'include: nes-common.yaml' resolved at compile time) and de-duplicate. Also revisit: MapCompiler unconditionally requires banking.context_register whenever banking: is present, forcing the NES boards to declare a provisional 'nesbank' register no language declares yet — make it optional or tie the requirement to the bundled-language milestone (grm-bk6).
notes: Implemented compile-time descriptor composition via YamlSupport.loadComposed for machine roots only: relative string/list includes, recursive canonical cycle detection, missing/absolute/type validation, deterministic left-to-right deep map merge, list append, local override, numeric nested-key preservation, deep-copy isolation, and controlled cyclic-alias rejection. MapCompiler and GdtBuilder share composition; raw PETSCII/external sources remain unchanged. GdtBuilder validates schema and unique type names before touching the last good GDT. Added verifyDescriptorComposition to buildExtension. Migrated all 10 shipping NES descriptors to machines/fragments/nes-common.yaml (core regions, MMIO symbols, NES_PPU/NES_APU_IO types, iNES format), preserving board-specific regions/windows/banking/validation. Removed fake nesbank from 9 banked descriptors and both sketches; context_register is optional and documented. Validation: composition verifier, buildMap, buildGdt, validateSketches, compileJava PASS; all 10 generated NES maps exactly match pre-change baseline after removing only context_register; all GDTs retain NES_PPU/NES_APU_IO; nes-banking chunk PASS; post-review canonical full suite PASS. Final review found and verified fixes for cyclic YAML aliases and duplicate-type output preservation.
close_reason: Implemented and fully validated shared descriptor composition, NES common-fragment migration, and optional context-register support.

title: Suppress 6502-language default block conflicts (ZERO_PAGE/STACK) in descriptor loaders
description: NES (and likely C64) imports log 'Failed to add language defined memory block due to conflict: ZERO_PAGE/STACK' — the stock 6502 pspec declares default blocks at $0000/$0100 that collide with our descriptor-driven RAM blocks. Cosmetic (import succeeds), but noisy. Options: shouldSetImageBaseOnNewProgram/default-block suppression hook, or name our RAM regions to subsume the pspec blocks. Observed during grm-9ux headless verification (SMB, Pac-Man).
close_reason: Fixed: descriptor loaders (AbstractCbmPrgLoader, NesRomLoader) override createDefaultMemoryBlocks with DescriptorSupport.createDefaultMemoryBlocksQuietly — pspec default blocks that conflict with descriptor memory are skipped silently; overflow/invalid-address failures still log. Full build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK; manual headless NES + C64 PRG imports show zero conflict messages.

title: M2: NES discrete mappers — UxROM/AxROM/CNROM/GxROM/BNROM via memory-latch strategy
description: First NES banking, per docs/vision-board-banking.md M2. Add the memory-latch strategy: store anywhere in a declared range, written value (or field) is the state, optional bus-conflict rule (effective value = written AND ROM byte at target — some discrete boards). Descriptors for UxROM (16K switchable $8000, fixed-last $C000), AxROM (32K $8000), CNROM (PRG fixed; CHR-only banking — near-trivial PRG side), GxROM/BNROM. Overlay-generation L4 (interim): one overlay per bank on the switchable window only — fixed windows are single blocks; no bank-by-window duplication (contrast GhidraNes MMC1Mapper.java:27-45). ACCEPTANCE: on real UNROM titles (Mega Man, Castlevania, Contra, DuckTales), bank-switch stores are detected, cross-bank JSR/JMP auto-resolve to the correct overlay, unknown-state sites get explicit ambiguity markers. GME payoff: nes/megaman + nes/bionic music-driver RE gets bank-aware disassembly.
close_reason: M2 discrete mappers shipped. memory-latch strategy (range store, shift/mask field extraction, bus-conflict AND when target is constant bank-invariant ROM, write-only-latch load resolution) via shared StoredValueScanner extracted from register-write with zero C64 regression (banktest suite byte-identical, 13/13, re-run on final build). Five shipping descriptors: nes-uxrom(2)/cnrom(3)/axrom(7)/gxrom(66)/bnrom(34); nes.yaml renamed nes-nrom.yaml; build.gradle machine tasks now data-driven glob. Loader realizes switchable computed windows home-in-base + <window>_B<v> overlays and records the board in program info; NesBankingAnalyzer reads it. Engine: computed-window retargeting, residence clamp (execution implies mapping), helper-call propagation (const helper state or call-site immediate arg recovery), and disassembly/function kick at cross-bank flow targets. ACCEPTANCE on real ROMs: Mega Man (UNROM) 153 switch annotations, 1507 cross-bank JSR/JMP refs primary into PRG_LO_B4/B5/B6, 7435 instructions disassembled inside bank overlays (13337 total vs 353 without banking), helper FUN_dc21 unrecoverable-arg site gets explicit WARNING. Castlevania: helper JSR sites detected with honest ambiguity markers (bank arg loaded from memory variable - stage-driven, statically unresolvable). W&W (AxROM): single 32K window, home+B1-B3, vectors from switchable home, 17 switches incl 'bank -> 2 via FUN_ff69'. Contra imports clean but stalls at 717 instrs (indirect-jump dispatch, generic coverage limit). DuckTales absent from ROM collection. Deviation: descriptors carry provisional context_register nesbank (MapCompiler requires it; dormant until grm-bk6). Follow-up filed: grm-5zg (descriptor include mechanism + optional context_register). Unblocks grm-6a7/grm-hsv (M3).

title: M2: extract BoardBankAnalyzer + strategy library (register-write) from C64BankingAnalyzer
description: Split C64BankingAnalyzer into (a) a machine-independent BoardBankAnalyzer engine — CFG worklist dataflow, per-bit partial-knowledge state (migrate PortState toward RegisterValue, which it reimplements), agree-bit merges, call-clobber rules, initial-state defaults, context stamping via ProgramContext.setRegisterValue, switch-site comments/bookmarks — and (b) a strategy library discovered via ClassSearcher, starting with register-write (fixed-address store; masked-RMW backward-scan value recovery already built and verified). Strategy interface owns: candidate-write recognition, value recovery (delegating to shared dataflow), state-field update emission with per-bit confidence. Configuration comes entirely from the schema-v2 descriptor (banking.mechanisms). ACCEPTANCE: C64 banktest/banktest2 headless suites pass unchanged (zero regression) with the C64 path running through the generic engine + register-write strategy. See docs/vision-board-banking.md section 6 (L2).
close_reason: BoardBankAnalyzer engine + strategy library extracted; ZERO REGRESSION proven by the new committed banktest suite (tools/banktest: 13 criteria + golden behavior dumps blessed against the pre-refactor analyzer, byte-identical after). Engine (BoardBankAnalyzer, abstract): CFG worklist dataflow, BankState per-bit value+mask (PortState renamed/promoted; RegisterValue's model on ints — full RegisterValue binding blocked on grm-bk6's context register, documented), agree-bit merges, initial-state defaults, effective-state fallback, switch-site EOL comments w/ known/assumed provenance, WARNING bookmarks only when zero bits known, overlay reference retargeting incl on_write, and ProgramContext.setValue context stamping that engages only when the language declares banking.context_register (dormant until grm-bk6 — stock 6502 has none). Strategies: BankSwitchStrategy ExtensionPoint (data/ExtensionPoint.manifest suffix; ClassSearcher discovery, fresh instance per mechanisms[] entry, configured from params) + RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy owning the verified masked-RMW backward scan. C64BankingAnalyzer is now ~60 lines: loader gate + map path + name (bookmark category preserved via getSimpleName). Documented deviation: WARNING bookmark message TEXT generalized (was register-write-specific prose); location/presence unchanged, dumps unaffected. Suite: tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless. Unblocks grm-4iq (memory-latch tier).

title: M1: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline (nes.yaml)
description: NES entry point per docs/vision-board-banking.md M1: iNES header parsing (mapper number, PRG/CHR sizes, trainer), board-descriptor registry keyed by mapper number with user override as a loader Option (pattern: Loader.getDefaultOptions, Loader.java:176 — board choice rides alongside the language pair, no LoadSpec changes), nes.yaml descriptor in schema v2. NROM end-to-end first: fixed PRG mapping (16K mirrored or 32K), CPU-space MMIO regions with PPU/APU/controller register types+symbols, vectors labeled and disassembled. CHR stays out of CPU space (GhidraNes parks it at $0000 in CPU space — known-wrong precedent, see NesMapper.java:161-203). No banking yet; this proves the loader stack is system-neutral. GME payoff: nes/smb (NROM) becomes the first Ghidra-navigable GME music target.
close_reason: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline shipped, verified end-to-end headless vs ghidra 12.1.2. machines/nes.yaml (schema v2): PPU/APU register structs (NESdev-checked), nes-mmio symbol set, vector slots, physical PRG + computed windows PRG[0]/PRG[last] — the last expression handles NROM-128 mirroring AND NROM-256 with zero special-casing. NesRomLoader: iNES header parse (magic/PRG/CHR/mapper/trainer), constant maps:-expression evaluator (ints, last, second_last, arith; state-field exprs deferred to bank engine), NES Board import option; NesBoardRegistry scans bundled machines/*.map for system.board.ines_mappers (data-driven: new boards = new descriptors, no Java). Loader stack proven system-neutral: descriptor interpretation extracted from C64PrgLoader into DescriptorSupport (regions/perms/volatile/subregions/types/symbols), C64 loader delegates, compiles green. VERIFIED: SMB (NROM-256) — correct blocks/perms, MMIO labels, typed vectors, NMI/RESET/IRQ functions, 1066 instructions from canonical reset; Pac-Man (NROM-128) — mirror windows placed, vectors resolve, $FF00 reset disassembled. CHR deliberately not loaded (PPU space deferred per vision §5.4). Follow-up filed for cosmetic ZERO_PAGE/STACK pspec-block conflict messages. Unblocks grm-4iq. GME payoff: nes/smb is now Ghidra-navigable.

title: M1: descriptor schema v2 — state tuples, mechanisms list, physical spaces, computed occupants, mode layouts
description: Generalize the board descriptor schema (SCHEMA.md / machines/c64.yaml) per docs/vision-board-banking.md section 5: (a) banking.state becomes a named tuple of fields mapping onto context-register sub-fields (RegisterValue per-bit partial knowledge); (b) banking.mechanism becomes mechanisms[] list, each a strategy instance with params and the state fields it feeds; (c) physical: spaces backing ROM images laid out once, with windows mapping into them via a deliberately tiny expression language (state fields, integer arithmetic, last/second_last, window-relative offset); (d) mode-dependent layouts[] selected by state fields (MMC1/MMC3 PRG modes). Enumerated occupants + truth-table states (C64 style) remain first-class. ACCEPTANCE: c64.yaml expressed in v2 regenerates the current .map/.gdt byte-identically (or with documented, reviewed diffs); MapCompiler + SCHEMA.md/MAP_FORMAT.md updated; UxROM and MMC3 sketches from the vision doc validate against the schema.
close_reason: Schema v2 shipped. (a) banking.state = named field tuple ({name,bits}, first field = bit 0); (b) banking.mechanisms[] = strategy instances with opaque params + sets validation; (c) top-level physical[] spaces + window maps: 'SPACE[expr]' with compile-time-validated mini-expression language (ints, state fields, last/second_last/offset, + - *, parens); (d) memory.layouts[] mode-dependent window sets keyed by when:{field:value}. ACCEPTANCE: c64.map regenerates byte-identical except one reviewed 36-line banking hunk (state_bits->state, mechanism->mechanisms) documented in MAP_FORMAT.md; .gdt unaffected (GdtBuilder reads only types:); C64BankingAnalyzer updated to v2 keys, full buildExtension green vs ghidra 12.1.2; UxROM+MMC3 sketches (machines/sketches/) compile via new validateSketches gradle task. Note: maps: values must be quoted inside YAML flow mappings ([ is a flow indicator) — documented in SCHEMA.md; vision doc examples show the unquoted aspirational form.

title: Board-level banking engine: machine-independent four-layer roadmap
description: Umbrella for the design vision recorded in docs/vision-board-banking.md (v1, 2026-07-07): first-class, data-driven board-level banking — four layers (L1 optional CPU-assist register; L2 strategy-driven write detection + value recovery; L3 pure-data interpretation; L4 application via context register + resolution hook, overlays as interim ceiling). Stepping stones: C64 (M0, shipped) -> schema v2 + NES NROM (M1) -> strategy library + discrete mappers (M2) -> MMC1/MMC3 protocol strategies + bank-placement inference (M3) -> MMC5 + GB MBC machine-independence proof (M4) -> core hook integration gated on RFC #9349 signal (M5). Guiding principles in the doc, notably: analysis over interrogation (infer bank placement from flows, never ask upfront — retire the GhidraNes per-bank combo-box pattern) and physical-space backing with windowed views (no bank-by-window block explosion). Related: grm-bk6/grm-wkk (C64 L1/L2 upgrades, parallel track); GME bead gib.2 (upstream engagement).

title: Bundle 6510 sleigh language (PORT register + c64bank context fields)
description:
Bundle a 6510 language variant with the extension (precedent: grue74/ghidra-c64helpers), replacing the fallback_language 6502:LE:16:default used today (c64.yaml cpu.language already names 6510:LE:16:default).

Contents beyond stock 6502:
- PORT register modeling the on-die $00/$01 port; specialized zp constructors (operand==$01, and ==$00 for DDR) route LDA/STA/etc through the register instead of memory — makes bank-switch idioms ordinary register dataflow (see grm-wkk for why).
- c64bank context register with three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (TMode-style; RegisterValue gives per-bit partial knowledge for free).
- Consider undocumented/illegal opcodes while in there (games use them).

Keep decode otherwise identical to stock 6502. Loader stops passing fallback_language once bundled.
notes: 2026-07-07 DESIGN CORRECTION (user): on-die-ness places only the mechanism REGISTER, never banking semantics — the PLA wiring of port bits to LOROM/HIROM/CHAREN is external, C64-board-specific. Counterexample: 6510T in the 1551 drive has the identical port wired to drive-control signals. Therefore the 6510 language must be SYSTEM-NEUTRAL: define PORT as an anonymous 8-bit on-die register routed from $00/$01 accesses; NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN naming, no c64bank truth-table knowledge in the slaspec. Per-system bit naming, if wanted, goes in a per-system pspec variant via register alias (ARM precedent: ARMt.pspec 'TB alias ISAModeSwitch') or stays entirely analyzer/descriptor-side.
close_reason: Bundled 6510 sleigh language shipped. data/languages/6510.{slaspec,ldefs,pspec,cspec} + sleighArgs.txt; build.gradle sleighCompile task (ghidra.pcodeCPort.slgh_compile.SleighCompile, SoftwareModeling/Generic/Utility lib classpath, -a) wired into buildExtension; compiled .sla gitignored (build artifact) + packaged. LANGUAGE: 6502 decode/semantics byte-identical PLUS on-die PORTDDR($00)/PORT($01) registers; specialized zero-page constructors (OP1/OP2, inherited by OP2LD/OP2ST) route DIRECT $00/$01 accesses through the registers so STA $01 -> PORT = A is register dataflow (verified via pcode probe: results=[PORT] inputs=[A]); indexed ($01,X) stays memory. SYSTEM-NEUTRAL per the 2026-07-07 design correction: port named anonymously, NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN, NO c64bank context register in the slaspec (bank meaning is board wiring, not CPU arch). Two sleigh gotchas solved+documented: (1) unquoted register-name display token is parsed as an operand ref and breaks export-size inference -> quote it ("PORT"); (2) dynamic *[register] export compiles to a STORE-via-pointer (results empty) not a clean register write -> static export PORT is required and works (coexists with the tables' memory exports like stock OP2:A). LOADER: DescriptorSupport.resolveLanguageId reads system.language, verifies availability, falls back to 6502 only if unavailable; C64PrgLoader uses it; fallback_language removed from c64.yaml (loader stops passing it, per acceptance). ANALYZER kept green without the grm-wkk propagator refactor: register-write mechanism gained optional 'register' param (c64.yaml: register: PORT); StoredValueScanner.writesRegister/readsRegister detect the on-die register via getResultObjects/getInputObjects; strategy ORs address|register so 6510 (register) and the 6502 fallback (address) both work. ZERO REGRESSION: C64 banktest suite 13/13 PASS and both dumps BYTE-IDENTICAL to goldens under the 6510 language; NES Mega Man byte-identical (153 switches/1507 cross-bank refs/13337 instrs) confirming the shared StoredValueScanner change is safe. Clean-from-scratch gradle build green; zip packages the language. Illegal/undocumented opcodes DEFERRED to grm-azg (not a pure win -- defining them makes data bytes decode as instructions, hurting code/data separation; needs an opt-in-variant design decision). context_register kept as c64bank in c64.yaml (MapCompiler still requires the field; making it optional is grm-5zg) but documented as the not-yet-realized application-layer channel; stampContextRegister stays dormant. Unblocks grm-wkk (TMode-style propagator refactor now has its PORT register).

title: Phase 0 bank-aware analyzer: flow-track bank state, retarget refs into overlay banks
description: The gib.2 Phase 0 interim (RFC docs/rfc-banked-memory.md): a Ghidra analyzer that (a) tracks C64 bank state along control flow from banking.initial_state, updating at determinable writes to the banking mechanism address ($0001, from banking.mechanism in the descriptor — which MapCompiler must now emit into c64.map, currently dropped); (b) for instruction operands targeting a banked window, when the effective occupant for the access differs from the base-space home block, adds an explicit primary reference into that occupant's overlay space (legal today: ReferenceDBManager.addMemoryReference has no same-space constraint). Includes write-under-ROM: WRITE accesses route via the occupant's on_write (STA $A000 with BASIC banked in -> RAM_A000::a000 even in the default state). Data-driven from c64.map; no hardcoded C64 facts beyond schema. Unknown/conflicting state -> leave defaults + bookmark. Demonstrates demand for the upstream RFC and gives correct cross-bank xrefs today.
design: Bank-state tracking: simple forward dataflow over the CFG (worklist; per-block in/out state; merge conflict -> unknown), NOT SymbolicPropogator — transparent and sufficient for the LDA #imm/STA $01 idiom; stored value from immediate-load lookback within the block (A/X/Y). state = value & mechanism.mask; occupants from banking.states. Refs: addMemoryReference(instr, overlayAddr, refType, SourceType.ANALYSIS, opIndex) + setPrimary; skip when effective occupant == home AND access is not a rom write-under. EOL comment or bookmark at bank-switch instructions showing the new state. Gate canAnalyze on executable format == C64 PRG loader name. Extend synthetic test PRG with a state-5 section + state-7 write-under-ROM to verify.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). C64BankingAnalyzer (AbstractAnalyzer, INSTRUCTION_ANALYZER, priority REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), gated on executableFormat == loader name): forward dataflow to fixpoint (known->conflict->UNKNOWN lattice) from entry/function seeds at banking.initial_state; bank switches recognized via WRITE ref to banking.mechanism.address with backward immediate-load scan (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm, block-bounded, clobber-aware); refs into banked windows retargeted to the state occupant's overlay (reads/exec) or its on_write occupant (writes — incl. write-under-ROM in the HOME state), SourceType.ANALYSIS, set primary, default demoted; EOL 'bank -> N (...)' comments; WARNING bookmark on undeterminable switch; idempotent. MapCompiler now emits banking.mechanism (was dropped); MAP_FORMAT.md updated. Verified: LDA $A000@state5 -> RAM_A000::a000 READ primary; STA $E000@state5 -> RAM_E000::e000 WRITE; STA $A000@state7 -> RAM_A000::a000 WRITE (write-under-ROM); JSR $FFD2 untouched. Subagent-found API gotcha: CodeUnit.getScalar(0) returns null for bare immediates — pull Scalar from getOpObjects instead.

title: C64 PRG loader (6502): overlays, IO struct annotation, KERNAL symbols; consume .gdt+.map
description: The grm-1.3 POC loader. Ghidra 12.x AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (class name MUST end 'Loader'): override load(Program, ImporterSettings); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default), gated on .prg extension / valid 2-byte load-addr header. In load(): read 2-byte LE load address, place PRG bytes; read bundled c64.map (gson) + c64.gdt (FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive); create region MemoryBlocks; create per-bank OVERLAY blocks (MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock/createUninitializedBlock isOverlay=true, distinct block name per occupant -> distinct overlay space); apply IO structs from .gdt at subregion addresses (program.getDataTypeManager().resolve + DataUtilities.createData CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA); apply inline symbols (SymbolTable.createLabel IMPORTED + addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL entry stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction); set entry point at load address. Defer 6510 language + c64bank context register + flow-tracked banking (separate bead). Locate bundled resources via Application.findDataFileInAnyModule.
design: MEMORY LAYOUT (corrected per user 2026-07-04 — references must resolve in the BASE space): Do NOT make all window occupants overlays; that reproduces the #6651 dangling-reference bug (JSR $FFD2 resolves in base space, so labels in overlay spaces are never consulted). Instead: the occupant selected by banking.initial_state (C64 state 7 = BASIC/IO/KERNAL) is the HOME block in the BASE (default) space; only the ALTERNATE occupants become overlay spaces. Base space = 7 always-visible regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF) + PRG (initialized, split RAM_MAIN around it) + window HOME blocks: BASIC@$A000 (empty ROM slot R+X), IO@$D000 (apply VIC/SID/CIA .gdt structs + color RAM + IO1/IO2), KERNAL@$E000 (empty ROM slot R+X). Overlays (own spaces, same nominal addr): RAM_A000, RAM_D000, CHARGEN, RAM_E000. CONSEQUENCE: KERNAL symbols (CHROUT@$FFD2 etc.) and IO structs are applied in the BASE space home block, so refs from PRG code resolve NOW without gib.2. Residual (refs INTO alternate/overlay banks) is the gib.2 problem — POC creates overlay blocks + labels but does NOT wire cross-refs into them; a future overlay-aware labelling/analyzer pass (or gib.2) attaches those. Program entry point = PRG load address (base space).
notes: REOPENED for code-review fixes (2026-07-04): (1) RAM regions were read-only (write flag passed as isIo) — centralize r/w/x into canWrite(kind)/canExecute(kind): RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w, applied at all block-creation sites (fixes the ad-hoc drift across createRegionBlock/createRamMainSplit/createWindowOccupant/createIoSubregions). (2) RAM_MAIN split produced two blocks both named RAM_MAIN — give the carved halves distinct address-suffixed names (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader: separate blocks are normal; join() can't merge FileBytes-initialized PRG with uninitialized RAM). (3) drop unused regionsByName param from createRegionBlock/createPrgBlock.
close_reason: Review fixes applied + re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). #1 RAM now writable (centralized canWrite/canExecute: RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w — consistent across all 4 block-creation sites, base & overlay); #2 split halves distinctly named RAM_MAIN_0800/RAM_MAIN_0807 (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader; join() can't merge init+uninit); #3 dead regionsByName param removed. Re-smoke confirms all RAM blocks w=true, IO w=true/x=false, ROM w=false/x=true, distinct names, CHROUT Function@ffd2, entry@0801, IO structs applied, Import succeeded.

title: Build-time map compiler: c64.yaml -> c64.map JSON; bundle .gdt+.map into extension data/
description: Runtime loader (grm-1.3.2) needs the C64 memory map without a YAML parser. Add a build-time compiler (MapCompiler, in the existing build-only gdtBuilder source set) that reads machines/c64.yaml and emits a c64.map JSON resource (regions, windows/occupants/subregions, banking states, inline symbols). JSON chosen because Ghidra bundles gson (Framework/Generic/lib/gson-2.13.2.jar) so the runtime loader parses it with ZERO shipped dependency. Also redirect the grm-1.5 .gdt output and the new .map into a bundled data dir (data/machines/) and make buildExtension package them, so both artifacts ship in the extension zip. Both are generated build artifacts: gitignore them, never commit.
design: c64.map JSON schema (contract with grm-1.3.2): { system:{id,name,language}, regions:[{name,start,end,kind,type?,comment?}], windows:[{name,start,end,occupants:[{name,kind,image?,on_write?,subregions?:[{name,start,end?,size?,repeat_to?,kind?,type?,comment?}]}]}], banking:{initial_state,context_register,state_bits,states:[{value,:,...}]}, rom_images:{:{size,occupant}}, symbols:[{set,default(bool),region?,entries:[{addr,name,kind,comment?}]}] }. Addresses as decimal JSON numbers. Compiler emits INLINE symbol entries only (source: sets not yet generated). Passes repeat_to through (loader decides mirror policy). Output data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; buildExtension.dependsOn buildGdt+buildMap (attach lazily). Document the schema in docs/MAP_FORMAT.md.
close_reason: Build-time map compiler complete + verified: gradle buildExtension alone bundles data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; c64.map matches frozen schema (7 regions, 3 windows w/ IO subregion types+repeat_to, 8 banking states, kernal-api inline symbols); snakeyaml stays build-only. Commit 872c669.

title: Generalized string detection: PETSCII + per-game tile-table text mappings
description:
Future feature: extend string detection beyond ASCII for retro systems.
- C64: PETSCII (KERNAL/CHROUT strings) AND screen codes (direct screen-RAM writes) — two DIFFERENT mappings, each with shifted/unshifted charset variants. Prior art: PETSCII visualizer in grue74/ghidra-c64helpers fork (inspect for reuse ideas).
- NES/SNES: per-game tile->character mappings, published as .tbl 'table files' by the ROM-hacking/translation community (romhacking.net, Data Crystal) — a de-facto standard format we could ingest directly, giving per-game string detection from community-documented data.
Integration points to investigate: Ghidra string data types support pluggable Java Charsets (extension could register PETSCII charsets); string-search analyzer charset hooks; descriptor schema could reference charset/table per system or per game.
Fits the descriptor-driven vision: text encoding is system knowledge (or game knowledge, for tile tables) that belongs in data, not code.
notes: DESIGN INPUT (user, 2026-07-11): the CBM BASIC detokenizing analyzer (grm-odt.1, epic grm-1.6) now DEPENDS ON this bead and is its first concrete consumer — its needs must inform this design, not be retrofitted. Requirements from that consumer: (1) a Java-callable byte->display-string mapping API for PETSCII usable OUTSIDE Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery — the detokenizer builds EOL comment text programmatically (string literals inside quotes, raw REM text) and cannot go through StringDataInstance; (2) both PETSCII variants (shifted/unshifted) selectable per call site; screen codes are a SEPARATE mapping (direct screen-RAM writes) the detokenizer does NOT need — do not conflate; (3) control/graphics bytes ($00-$1F, $80-$FF inside quotes) need a printable escaped rendering convention (e.g. {CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}) — pick one, document it, and keep it stable since it lands in golden test dumps; (4) the mapping data should be data-driven (descriptor/shared data file) per project convention, and shared with any future Ghidra charset registration rather than duplicated. Suggested shape: a small PetsciiMapper (or CharsetTable) class + data file, with Ghidra Charset registration layered on top later for string search. The NES/SNES .tbl half of this bead is unaffected by the BASIC consumer but should share the table-data plumbing where natural.
close_reason: All 5 children complete: PetsciiMapper escaped layer (.1), unicode layer schema 2 (.2), charset SPI + 4 JVM charsets + 6 fixed-charset string datatypes + verifyCharsets (.3), descriptor-gated PetsciiStringAnalyzer + system.text key + petscii-strings fixture (.4), screen-code permutation family (.5). PETSCII and screen-code strings are now first-class in Ghidra: charset dropdown, datatypes, and auto-analysis string search, all descriptor-driven and gate-verified. The NES/SNES .tbl half was split out to grm-pqk by user decision (dynamic per-game tables cannot be JVM charsets); grm-td4 (typing BASIC text runs) is unblocked by the new datatypes.

title: POC: C64 loader that maps banked RAM/ROM, IO ports, and PRG load address
description: Implement a minimal proof-of-concept Ghidra loader for the Commodore 64 that (a) reads a PRG file's 2-byte load-address header and places code correctly, (b) maps the banked memory layout — RAM under KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN, plus the IO region — using Ghidra overlay address spaces to represent the overlapping banks selectable via the $00/$01 processor port, (c) annotates IO chip registers (VIC-II, SID, CIA1, CIA2, color RAM), (d) applies initial struct/label definitions for known hardware registers. Validates that the system descriptor design (gib.1.2) is sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Open question to resolve in design: how faithfully to model banking given Ghidra's static memory model.
notes: DESIGN (2026-07-03, decided w/ user): (1) Descriptor delivery = COMPILE MAP AT BUILD TIME. Build tooling emits c64.gdt (types, existing) PLUS c64.map (regions/windows/banking/symbols) as bundled extension data resources; the runtime loader reads BOTH via non-YAML means (no snakeyaml in shipped extension). (2) POC language = stock 6502:LE:16:default; defer bundling 6510 + c64bank context register + flow-tracked bank state to a later bead (gib.2 track). Banking already decided = overlay address spaces. LOADER API (Ghidra 12.x, source-verified): override load(Program, ImporterSettings) on AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (NOT the classic 6-arg load); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default); class name MUST end in 'Loader'. Overlays: MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock(...,isOverlay=true) once per bank, distinct block name per bank -> distinct overlay space (BASIC_ROM:a000). Bundled .gdt: Application.findDataFileInAnyModule('c64.gdt') -> FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive(f,false); apply via program.getDataTypeManager().resolve(dt,DEFAULT_HANDLER) + DataUtilities.createData(...,CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA). Symbols: SymbolTable.createLabel(addr,name,IMPORTED)+addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction(prog,name,addr). Decomposition: grm-1.3.1 build-time map compiler+bundling; grm-1.3.2 the 6502 PRG loader.
close_reason: POC complete + headless-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2). Both children done: grm-0xt (build-time c64.map compiler + .gdt/.map bundling) and grm-974 (6502 PRG loader). Acceptance (a) PRG 2-byte load-addr header read + code placed, (b) banked layout mapped, (c) IO chip registers annotated (VIC/SID/CIA/color RAM via .gdt structs), (d) struct+label defs applied — ALL verified. DESIGN REFINEMENT vs original description: original said 'use overlay spaces to represent overlapping banks'; we improved to HOME-IN-BASE (occupant selected by initial bank state = home block in BASE space; only ALTERNATES become overlays) because pure-overlay banks reproduce the #6651 dangling-reference bug — base-space code (JSR $FFD2) never consults overlay labels. Result: default bank config fully cross-referenced today (CHROUT Function@base:ffd2), pre-gib.2. Descriptor design (gib.1.2) validated as sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Residual = refs INTO alternate/overlay banks (gib.2 context-aware resolution).

title: Game System Architecture Loader
description:
Root epic for ghidra-retro-machines: a descriptor-driven Ghidra loader extension that sets up complete retro system architectures — memory maps, banked windows (mechanism + initial state), IO chip register structs, copyright-safe ROM slots, symbol sets — from per-machine YAML descriptors (machines/*.yaml). Initial target: Commodore 64. Design docs: docs/SURVEY.md (founding survey), docs/SCHEMA.md (descriptor schema).

LINEAGE: incubated in CBongo/game-music-extraction as beads epic gib.1 (children gib.1.1-gib.1.5 = grm-1.1-grm-1.5); migrated here at repo-birth 2026-07-03. Related work still tracked in GME: gib.2 (Ghidra core banked-memory upstream proposal), gib.3 (Ghidra MCP tooling).
notes:
ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03):
1. MVP input format: PRG (2-byte load address header).
2. Banking: overlay address spaces for MVP — best Ghidra can do today. IO region always needed by music code; BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN rarely needed by music code itself but frequently involved in the LOADER code paths (esp. KERNAL). Long-term: improving Ghidra core banked-memory support is a stated motivation of this whole effort — see bead game-music-extraction-gib.2.
3. ROMs (copyright): symbol-only labels by default (e.g. KERNAL entry points); reserve labeled memory-map slots so users can pull their own ROM dumps in via File > Add To Program; optional loader ROM-path options possible later.
4. Schema: evolving descriptor schema from day one, NOT hardcode-C64-first. Solo development until project is more baked; collaborators later.
5. Build-vs-contribute still open pending RetroGhidra survey (gib.1.1).
REPO NAME DECIDED (user, 2026-07-03): ghidra-retro-machines. Verified collision-free on GitHub (no exact match; no confusable neighbor in the Ghidra/RE space). Pitch: 'give Ghidra the whole machine, not just the file' — descriptor-driven system architecture loaders for retro computers and consoles. Layout affordance: machines/c64.yaml, machines/nes.yaml. Repo-birth trigger reached: gib.1.5 (.gdt build pipeline) is the first extension code; at repo creation, migrate this epic's subtree per the MIGRATION NOTE above and move GME's ghidra/ design docs (SURVEY.md, SCHEMA.md, descriptors/) into the new repo.

title: Suppress or prune overlay banks for PRG modes the ROM never uses
description:
IDEA from the user, 2026-08-09, filed while settling grm-67g. Unrelated to that bug; do not fold in.

Boards with a switchable PRG MODE (MMC3's $8000 bit 6, MMC1's control register) get overlay blocks
created for EVERY mode the descriptor models. A ROM that only ever runs one mode therefore carries a
full set of blocks and spaces for windows it never uses. smb3 is the worked example: $8000 bit 6 is
set at every observed write, so PRG mode 1 is the only live mode, yet the mode-0 window blocks exist
regardless. blocks.total 103 / blocks.overlay 95 on that title.

WHY IT IS NOT TRIVIALLY SAFE, and this is the user's own framing: in theory a ROM could switch PRG
mode from code that has not been disassembled yet, so 'no mode-0 write seen' is an absence-of-
evidence argument, not proof. Worse, suppression at CREATION time would have to happen during the
LOAD, before any analysis has run -- which is exactly when the evidence does not exist yet. The two
halves of the problem pull in opposite directions.

SHAPES WORTH CONSIDERING (none chosen):
  (a) Post-analysis PRUNE rather than load-time suppression: create everything, then offer to remove
      mode-N blocks that hold zero instructions AND zero inbound references AND for which no
      mode-selecting write with that value was ever resolved. Evidence-based, and reversible by
      re-running the loader.
  (b) A user-invoked SCRIPT rather than automatic behaviour -- the user notes it is easy enough to
      delete them by hand today, which puts the real value in convenience, not correctness. That
      argues for an explicit, undoable action over anything that runs silently.
  (c) A per-game descriptor HINT (grm-hb6 tier) declaring the live mode for a known title. Sidesteps
      the inference problem entirely by making it a recorded fact rather than a deduction.

(c) is the honest fit for the per-game tier and (b) is the cheapest useful thing; (a) is the one that
needs the most care about what counts as evidence. Not urgent -- this is tidiness, not correctness.

title: smb3: unexplained helper FUN_c542 with unrecovered args at 867b/ac6d (new since 788f09b)
description:
Found in the smb3 realrom diff while settling grm-bj6 / grm-67g, and deliberately NOT folded into
either -- the human trace of smb3's banking (ffc2/ffd1/ffbf plus the direct sites c5f5/c9f7)
accounts for every disassembled direct write to $8000 and does not mention c542 at all.

WHAT APPEARS (new since 788f09b, absent from the golden):
  sample.warn 867b [NesBankingAnalyzer] ... call to bank-switch helper FUN_c542 whose bank argument
                   could not be recovered at this call site
  sample.warn ac6d  (same, same helper)

TWO POSSIBILITIES, and they want different responses:
  (a) c542 is a REAL bank-switch helper the human trace did not reach -- e.g. RAM-resident, reached
      only from a switched window, or a wrapper the trace did not walk into. Then these warnings are
      honest and the golden simply predates them.
  (b) c542 is a FALSE helper admitted by 788f09b's wrapper pass, in which case it is collateral of
      the same change as grm-67g and may vanish when that is fixed.

CHECK (b) FIRST, and check it AFTER grm-67g lands -- it is free at that point: re-run smb3 and see
whether 867b/ac6d survive. Only if they survive is a human look at c542 worth asking for.

DO NOT bless smb3 to absorb these; the golden is the correct baseline (grm-bj6).

REPRO: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --only smb3 H:/emulators/nes/roms

title: Wrapper models hand the caller's X/Y to depositHelperArgument without proving they survive the wrapper body
description:
SPLIT OUT OF grm-2dr increment 2 (2026-08-09), deliberately not fixed there.

recoverCallArgument hands the strategy the call site's WHOLE register environment via
callSiteRegisters (BoardBankAnalyzer, the RegisterEnv built at the depositHelperArgument call),
so a strategy that can do better than the argReg convention -- memory-latch does, Contra's helper
takes its bank in Y while findHelpers can only see the STA's A -- can re-evaluate its own switch
site under the caller's registers.

THE GAP. argumentSurvivesPrologue is run for argReg ONLY. For a WRAPPER model (pass-through, from
grm-2dr increment 1, or call-edge, from increment 2) the wrapper's body sits between the caller and
the helper and may freely write X or Y -- nothing in either admission predicate forbids it.
isPassThroughInto admits any instruction with no flows, LDX #imm included. So the caller's X/Y are
handed over as though they reached the helper, when the wrapper may have overwritten them.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN INCREMENT 2. The exposure is NOT new to call-edge wrappers -- increment 1's
pass-through wrappers already carry it identically, and the 19-title corpus showed no wrong banks.
Forcing X/Y to unknown for wrapper models was considered and rejected for this increment: it changes
behavior on an axis nothing measured, and it can only DECREASE annotations, which increment 2's
acceptance criteria forbid. Deferring keeps one rule for both wrapper kinds.

THE FIX, when it is worth doing. argumentSurvivesPrologue already takes a segment list
(grm-2dr increment 2). Run it once per register over the same segments and pass through only the
survivors, leaving the rest BankState.unknown(). That is uniform across ordinary helpers, pass-through
wrappers and call-edge wrappers, and is strictly more precise than either current option.

HOW TO TELL IF IT MATTERS. The shape needed is a MEMORY-LATCH helper behind a wrapper whose body
writes X or Y. contra is the title to read: it is the corpus's memory-latch/index-register case.
If no such shape exists in the corpus this can be closed as unreachable rather than implemented.

title: Does the $F0 interrupt guard defeat StoredValueScanner's backward scan? (tmnt; original interleaving premise disproven)
description:
Found by hand during the tmnt def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-06). Plausible direct cause of
tmnt's "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing", which is a different failure from cv2's
(a boundary problem) and blmaster's (an argument-path problem).

THE SHAPE. tmnt guards every MMC1 serial write against interruption. All four of its A-taking
helpers (ce56 CONTROL, ce6f CHR0, ce8a CHR1, cea7 PRG) replace the FIRST LSR of the five-write
serial sequence with SEC followed by ROR $F0, and execute ASL $F0 just before returning. Bit 7
of $F0 is therefore set for the duration of the switch and cleared at the end; the NMI handler
tests it and returns early, so an interrupt cannot land mid-sequence and corrupt the MMC1 shift
register.

This is good defensive 6502 and is likely to recur -- any game that switches banks from both
main-line and interrupt context needs some form of it.

WHY IT MATTERS TO US. The mechanism chain now contains INTERLEAVED NON-SHIFT INSTRUCTIONS. A
strategy that matches a strict 5x(STA/LSR) sequence will either reject these chains outright or
mis-parse the shift sequence, and in either case the stored value does not recover.

TWO READINGS, NOT YET DISTINGUISHED, WITH DIFFERENT FIXES:

  (a) FLAG ONLY. The bank value stays in A; $F0 is purely a lock byte. The chain is then an
      ordinary 5x(STA/LSR A) sequence with two extra instructions bracketing it. Fix is
      tolerance: allow unrelated memory writes to interleave without breaking the match.

  (b) THE VALUE LIVES IN $F0. SEC/ROR $F0 both sets the lock bit AND performs the first shift,
      making the chain STA reg / LSR $F0 rather than STA reg / LSR A. The serial shift then runs
      on MEMORY, not the accumulator. A register-based serial-shift strategy will not match this
      at all, and the value's provenance becomes a memory location rather than a register.

  (b) is the more consequential and would explain why tmnt's values recover nothing even where
  its sites ARE found. DETERMINE WHICH BEFORE DESIGNING ANYTHING -- read the full instruction
  sequence of ce56 (the simplest of the four) and record it verbatim on this bead.

ACCEPTANCE (provisional, pending the above): tmnt's four helper chains are recognised as
serial-shift mechanisms with their argument register identified, and the guard writes to $F0 are
not mistaken for mechanism activity. Measure against tmnt's direct-store recovery rate, today 6
of 30.

RELATED: grm-i7v (tmnt's cea5 is a second pre-body-entry instance, and the two together are what
gate this title). grm-lwu / grm-xym for the principle that a mis-parsed mechanism generates
warning traffic that then pollutes anything keyed on warnings.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-06: THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS WRONG. The guard does NOT interleave with
the serial chain; it BRACKETS it. Verbatim sequence, confirmed by hand:

    SEC
    ROR $F0            ; set bit 7 -- lock
    STA $xFFFF
    LSR A / STA $xFFFF     (x4)
    ASL $F0            ; clear bit 7 -- unlock

Five stores and four shifts, contiguous and standard. The bank value is carried in A throughout;
$F0 is ONLY a lock flag and is otherwise unused. My earlier reading -- that the first LSR was
replaced by SEC/ROR $F0, implying the shift might run on memory -- is disproven. Reading (a) in
the description is correct and reading (b) does not occur.

CONSEQUENCE: a strict 5x(STA/LSR) matcher should match these chains without modification, so
this bead is NOT the explanation for tmnt's "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing". Dropping
P2 -> P3 accordingly, and tmnt's diagnosis moves to grm-2dr (the cea5 wrapper) plus whatever
explains the remaining direct stores.

WHAT IS LEFT THAT IS STILL WORTH ASKING -- a much narrower question than the original framing:

  Does StoredValueScanner's backward scan survive the guard? Walking back from the first STA it
  encounters ROR $F0, a read-modify-write to memory, before reaching the instruction that loaded
  A. grm-hum records that the scanner aborts when it steps over a mechanism write, on the
  grounds that a base value read further back would predate it. ROR $F0 is NOT a mechanism write
  -- $F0 is zero page, outside any declared mechanism range -- but if the scanner is
  conservative about memory writes generally, or about RMW specifically, it would abort here and
  every one of tmnt's four helpers would lose its argument for a reason unrelated to the chain.

  CHEAP TEST: compare tmnt's argument recovery at cea7 against a helper with no guard on another
  MMC1 title (blmaster e63c, cv2 c187). If tmnt alone fails, the guard is implicated; if all
  three behave alike, close this bead.

KEEPING THE BEAD OPEN ONLY FOR THAT TEST. If the scan is unaffected, close as not-a-bug -- the
guard idiom is then simply well-written 6502 that costs us nothing. The idiom itself is still
worth having documented here: an NMI-safe bank switch is likely to recur in any game that
switches banks from both main-line and interrupt context.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED -- NOT A BUG. Closing per this bead's own stated close condition ("if all three behave
alike, close the bead as not-a-bug"). Human recon supplied the two comparison helpers
(user, 2026-08-08); the checked-in goldens supply the outcomes.

THE THREE-WAY TABLE. "Walk-back" = instructions between function entry and the first mechanism
STA. In-body warns = the five unrolled serial stores inside the helper itself.

  helper          walk-back from first STA        admitted?  in-body warns  call-site recovery
  blmaster e63c   NONE -- STA $FFFF *is* the      yes        5              FAILS, caller-side
                  entry instruction, preceded                               ($DB shadow at e627,
                  only by the previous fn's RTS                             ec5b) -- grm-mej.2
  cv2 c187        PHA / LDA #1 / STA $0103 / PLA  yes        5 (c18e..c19e) WORKS (c0ed, c10a)
  tmnt cea7       SEC / ROR $F0                   yes        5 (ceaa..ceba) WORKS (c003, cec7,
                                                                            cedb)

(The user wrote "blmaster e36c"; that is e63c. Byte arithmetic independently confirms both hand
sequences: cv2 c187's PHA/LDA #1/STA $0103/PLA is exactly 7 bytes, putting the first STA at c18e,
which is where the warnings begin, stride 4 = STA abs + LSR A. tmnt cea7's SEC/ROR $F0 is 3 bytes,
first STA at ceaa, same stride. cea5 = STA $21 two bytes before, i.e. the fallthrough entry.)

THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS POSITIVE. tmnt's golden carries real recoveries THROUGH the guarded
helpers -- c003 prg_bank=2 via FUN_cea7, cec7 and cedb via FUN_cea7, c354 via FUN_ce56, and six
sites via FUN_cea5 (c359, cfcf, d01f, d8e9, d8f7, dbc4, dbe1). Those comments cannot exist if the
SEC/ROR $F0 bracket defeated helper admission or argument identification. The guard is empirically
harmless.

Stated at evidence level deliberately: the goldens prove the OUTCOME (recovery works with the
guard present, identically to an unguarded helper), not the MECHANISM. Whether StoredValueScanner
walks back over the ROR $F0 or whether post-grm-2dr admission takes another path entirely is a
read of BoardBankAnalyzer's scan loop, not a golden grep. Not needed for this close.

cv2 c187 IS THE CONTROL THIS BEAD WANTED, and it is a stronger one than expected: between entry
and its chain sit an unrelated memory write (STA $0103) AND a PHA/PLA save-restore of the very
parameter being tracked -- and recovery still works. So the pipeline is not conservative about
intervening non-mechanism writes in general, which was the worry. blmaster e63c turns out to test
nothing on this axis (zero walk-back distance); its failure is caller-side and already parked on
grm-mej.2.

READING (a) CONFIRMED -- consistent with the 2026-08-07 correction comment. The value stays in A;
$F0 is purely a lock byte; the guard BRACKETS the chain rather than interleaving with it. No
tolerance work is needed.

REFRAME OF THE ORIGINATING METRIC. "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing" (grm-8iy.5) was
counting the IN-BODY serial stores. Those are parameter-valued by construction in EVERY MMC1
title -- five per helper, warning identically in cv2 (c18e..c19e, c143..c17f) and blmaster
(e63c..e688). It is a metric artifact of MMC1's serial write protocol, not a tmnt pathology. The
recovery that matters happens at CALL SITES, and tmnt now has 18 bank comments and 103
instrs.inOverlay against the 0 it had when this bead was filed.

CAVEAT ON COMPLETENESS: tmnt's dump caps its warning sample (count 28, 25 sample lines), so this
is not an audit of every tmnt warning. blmaster (24/24) and cv2 (23/23) are complete. The close
rests on the positive recoveries, which are all in the sample.

title: No-argument helpers report helperArgReg and emit a spurious unrecoverable-argument warning (e68c, blmaster)
description:
Found by hand during the blmaster def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05).

THE DEFECT. A helper whose stored value is a constant loaded inside its OWN body takes no
caller argument, but the model still assigns it an argument register and then reports that
argument as unrecoverable. 'This helper needs no argument' and 'this helper's argument could
not be recovered' collapse into the same output, and only the second raises a warning.

OBSERVED (blmaster). FUN_e68c is the whole of the MMC1 reset:

    e68c: LDA #$80
    e68e: STA $FFFF
    e691: RTS

HelperShapeProbe reports it, and its single call site at f25a:

  helper FUN_e68c entry=e68c body=e68c-e691 pop=MECH-ONLY strategy=serial-shift mechSites=1
    mechFirst=e68e mechLast=e68e latch=ffff storeReg=A
  call f25a flow=UNCONDITIONAL_CALL JSR 0xe68c ... arg=computed/unknown immReg=NONE
    helperArgReg=A regMatch=NA prev=BPL 0xf255

helperArgReg=A is wrong: A is a LOCAL of e68c, not a parameter. arg=computed/unknown then
follows mechanically because the instruction before the call is a BPL rather than a load --
but there is nothing at f25a that COULD load it, and nothing that should.

PROPOSED RULE. Set helperArgReg=NONE when the helper's own body loads the store register with
an immediate on every path reaching the mechanism write, and classify such calls as
arg=not-required rather than arg=computed/unknown. This is grm-mu7's prologue-clobber machinery
taken to its limit -- there the prologue clobbers the caller's value, here the prologue IS the
entire value source. regMatch=NA suggests something already half-notices. The same treatment
should cover the fff4 INC/RMW reset (grm-4kc), which likewise takes no argument.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING. It is the same failure mode as grm-lwu from a
different direction: a question that does not apply generating warning traffic. That traffic is
not merely noise -- any population keyed on warnings inherits it, which is precisely how
grm-8iy.3 was filed on 31 phantom helpers and 11 phantom constant-arg sites. Suppressing
inapplicable questions is a correctness measure for every downstream count, not an ergonomics
one.

ACCEPTANCE: e68c reports helperArgReg=NONE; f25a produces no unrecoverable-argument warning;
blmaster's warning total drops accordingly with no loss of genuine findings.

title: Function body over-extends past an always-looping BNE/BEQ pair: RESET routine f23b merged into FUN_f1ca (blmaster)
description:
Found by hand during the blmaster def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05). Directly caused a
wrong bead to be filed (grm-8iy.3), so it is a measurement-integrity issue, not cosmetic.

OBSERVED (blmaster, MMC1). FUN_f1ca's body extends past f237 and absorbs the routine at f23b.

  - f1ca proper touches NO MMC1 register.
  - The real end of f1ca is f237: a BNE/BEQ pair that always loops back, so control never falls
    through to f23b.
  - f23b is the guts of the hardware RESET routine. It calls e68c (MMC1 reset) and e678 with
    A=#$1E (MMC1 control: 4K CHR, PRG mode 3, vertical mirror), and finishes by JMPing to c24f.

CONSEQUENCE. f1ca appears to perform MMC1 register activity that belongs to RESET. grm-8iy.3
listed FUN_f1ca among blmaster's five bank-switch helpers on that basis; hand inspection shows
it is not one. The genuine mechanism-writing set is e63c/e650/e664/e678/e68c (see grm-8iy.5).

ROOT CAUSE NOT YET CONFIRMED -- two candidates, and the fix differs:
  (a) Ghidra's function-body assignment continued past an always-taken backward branch pair it
      could not prove terminates flow, so f23b was absorbed as fallthrough.
  (b) f23b is genuinely reached only via the RESET vector / an internal JMP and simply never got
      its own function created, leaving its bytes attributable to the preceding body.
  Check what the RESET vector at $FFFC points to and whether anything references f23b directly.
  If (a), this is a candidate for the same upstream treatment as grm-b3m / grm-6xh; if (b) it is
  a seeding gap on our side.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FUNCTION. Any analysis keyed on 'which function contains this
mechanism write' inherits the error. A body that swallows an unrelated routine mis-attributes
that routine's registers, its call sites and its warnings -- which is exactly how a phantom
helper reached a bead. Worth checking whether the other GME titles show the same over-extension
before assuming it is blmaster-specific.

ACCEPTANCE: FUN_f1ca's body ends at f237; f23b is a separate function; blmaster's helper
enumeration no longer lists f1ca.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND FUNCTION-BOUNDARY DEFECT FOUND BY HAND, OPPOSITE DIRECTION (2026-08-06). grm-i7v records
cv2's FUN_c187 starting TOO LATE, orphaning the routine's real entry points at c183 and c185
below the function start and hiding 13 of 16 call sites. This bead is a body extending TOO FAR
and swallowing an unrelated routine.

Two such defects in the first two titles traced by hand suggests neither is isolated. Anything
keyed on "which function contains this mechanism write" inherits both, and both have already
caused a wrong measurement -- this one manufactured a phantom helper that got a bead filed on
it (grm-8iy.3), and grm-i7v's makes cv2 look like it has no recoverable arguments.

Worth a survey pass over the GME set for the general shapes before either fix is designed:
functions whose body contains an always-looping branch followed by more code, and call targets
that fall through into a known helper from below its entry.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE FORK RESOLVED BY A HUMAN RE PASS (2026-08-08): it is (a), body over-extension --
NOT (b), a seeding gap. The bead asked to "check what the RESET vector at $FFFC points to and
whether anything references f23b directly." Answer, user-supplied:

  RESET -> fff4, which is a self-referencing INC RESET -- the classic MMC1 reset idiom, where
  the read-modify-write's double store presents a bit-7-set byte to the mapper -- followed by
  JMP f23b. f23b is the bulk of the reset handling: SEI / CLD / LDX #$FF / TXS, then the usual
  hardware register init. No other references to f23b.

So f23b IS reached, by a JMP from the RESET entry. Candidate (b) said it "simply never got its
own function created" for want of a reference; that is falsified. The inbound flow exists, and
the reason f23b's bytes ended up attributed to FUN_f1ca is that f1ca's body had already claimed
them by continuing past the always-looping BNE/BEQ pair at f237 -- Ghidra function bodies cannot
overlap, so whoever claims a range first wins, and the over-extension beat the JMP. Same family
as grm-b3m / grm-6xh, and a candidate for the same upstream treatment.

CORROBORATION FROM OUR OWN GOLDEN: blmaster.dump already carries a bankcomment at fff4 --
"bank -> mirroring=0,prg_mode=3,prg_bank=0 [switch-value flow]", fully known, no assumed bits.
So the analyzer already recognizes the INC-triggered reset at the RESET entry. The RESET path is
seen; only the body attribution downstream of it is wrong.

ACCEPTANCE NEEDS A SMALL CORRECTION. As written it asks that "f23b is a separate function".
That is probably not the right target and could never be met by fixing (a) alone: f23b is a JMP
target, not a call target, so in stock Ghidra its flow is absorbed into the body of the function
that jumps to it. With the over-extension fixed, the correct outcome is that f23b belongs to the
RESET function at fff4, not that it becomes its own function. Restate as:

  - FUN_f1ca's body ends at f237;
  - f23b is attributed to the RESET function entered at fff4 (or, failing that, is at least not
    part of FUN_f1ca);
  - blmaster's helper enumeration no longer lists f1ca.

title: RealRomDump: refs.intoOverlay conflates retargets with intra-overlay refs, so it is not an honest fix metric
description:
RealRomDump.java:107-115 counts every reference whose TARGET space is an overlay, regardless of
where the source lives. Once addOverlayRef bootstraps one instruction into an overlay,
Ghidra disassembles that overlay's code and its intra-overlay branches/calls/data refs resolve
WITHIN that overlay space -- and all of them count. For a working title that second term
dominates: megaman reports 1704 refs.intoOverlay, of which only a small fraction are actual
retargets.

CONSEQUENCE. The counter is fine as a coarse did-anything-happen signal (which is what grm-8iy
used it for: 0 vs nonzero), but it is NOT a fix-effectiveness metric. A change that doubles the
retargets and one that merely disassembles deeper inside an already-reached overlay move the same
number.

FIX. Split into two counters keyed on the SOURCE space:

    refs.intoOverlay.retargeted    srcSpace == default space && dstSpace.isOverlay()
    refs.intoOverlay.intraOverlay  srcSpace.isOverlay()      && dstSpace.isOverlay()

COST, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: it rewrites every one of the ~31 golden dumps. Do it standalone
so the bless diff is reviewable on its own and cannot be confused with a behaviour change.

INTERIM. grm-8iy.1's BankConsumerProbe emits both numbers, so the investigation is not blocked;
the analyzer's own verbose summary line (BoardBankAnalyzer.java:348-350) is the other source.

title: NES board gap: mapper 9 (MMC2) has no shipped descriptor
description: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! is iNES mapper 9 (MMC2), which no machines/nes-*.yaml claims -- shipped coverage is mappers 0,1,2,3,4,7,16,34,66,157,159 (plus synthetic 100/222). MMC2 exists essentially only for Punch-Out, so this is a narrow but self-contained board: PRG is 8K-switchable at 8000-9fff with three fixed 8K banks above, and its distinguishing feature is latch-driven CHR banking triggered by PPU tile fetches (irrelevant to PRG analysis). Nominating the GME set will confirm this and may surface others; 'realrom-test.sh nominate' reports any unclaimed mapper as a board gap. Decide whether a nes-mmc2 descriptor is worth shipping once the full nomination list exists -- this bead exists so the finding is not lost, not as a commitment to build it.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SAMPLES ARE AVAILABLE LOCALLY -- this bead is not blocked on finding a ROM (surveyed 2026-08-03).

'realrom-test.sh nominate' over the local NES library turns up seven mapper-9 dumps, all
Punch-Out!!, which is the canonical MMC2 title (MMC2 was built for it):

  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (JU) (V1.0) [!]
  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (JU) (V1.1) [!]
  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (PRG 1) (U)
  MikePOut
  Punch-Out!! (U)
  Punch-Out!! (U) [!]
  Punch-Out!! (U) (VC) [!]

All under H:/emulators/nes/roms (the depth-1 dir and the GoodNES USA/Japan-USA subdirs). There is
also a punchout/ directory in the game-music-extraction tree, so this title is already in that
corpus.

HOW TO GET A PASTE-READY MANIFEST ROW (no Ghidra needed -- nominate decodes the iNES header
itself and only reports the board a shipped descriptor claims):
  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh nominate H:/emulators/nes/roms
It prints 7-field TSV rows for claimed mappers and '# NO SHIPPED BOARD claims mapper N' comments
for unclaimed ones -- so once a nes-mmc2 descriptor ships, the Punch-Out rows flip from comment to
row automatically and can be pasted into manifest-gme.tsv.

CONTEXT FOR SIZING THE WIDER BOARD GAP, same survey, mappers with NO shipped descriptor ranked by
how many local dumps claim them:
  mapper 5 (MMC5)  16    mapper 9 (MMC2)   7    mapper 118  5    mapper 69 (Sunsoft FME-7)  4
  mapper 87  3    mapper 206  3    mapper 68  2    mapper 23  2    mapper 18  2    mapper 119  2
  mapper 11 (Color Dreams)  2, then a tail of singletons (6, 13, 19, 21, 47, 71, 75, 156, ...).
MMC5 is the bigger gap by sample count but a far bigger board; MMC2 is 7 samples of essentially
one game and a much smaller mechanism, so it stays the right next descriptor.

The surveys themselves (tools/banktest/realrom/manifest-all.tsv, manifest-goodnes.tsv) are
deliberately gitignored -- machine-specific, not hash-pinned test input. Regenerate with the
nominate command above.

title: Stack PHA/PLA pairing and cross-block memory forwarding: the save/restore idiom
description:
Increment 3 of grm-mej -- the piece the parent bead says to scope carefully, deferred out of the
1+2 session on purpose. This is a NEW DATAFLOW DOMAIN: StoredValueScanner today models A/X/Y and
the board state and nothing else. transferSource (:543-551) deliberately excludes TSX, 'the stack
pointer is not tracked'; PLA is an opaque clobber in A_MODIFIERS (:115); PHA is invisible to the
walk entirely (it does not modify A, so the scan walks straight past it).

TWO HALVES, both needed for the same idiom -- save current bank / switch / restore:

  STACK SLOTS. Pair a PHA with its PLA well enough to carry a value across a save/restore.
    contra NMI:  C0C1 LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA / C0D2 TAY / C0D3 JSR $C13F
    shenlong:    LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC   (the far-call trampoline takes its bank via PHA)
  Note MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN = 16 (:98) may bind across a real save/restore span.

  CROSS-BLOCK MEMORY FORWARDING. grm-mej.1 forwards only WITHIN one basic block. Contra's
  C139 LDA $8000 / STA $07EC .. C146 LDY $07EC / JMP $C13F crosses blocks, and $07EC is NOT a
  write-through shadow (it is not adjacent to a mechanism write), so grm-mej.2's discovery route (a)
  will not find it either. Note $07EC/$07ED are RAM but NOT zero page -- any design here must
  stay address-range-agnostic, same ruling as .1 and .2.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED ON grm-mej.2: pairing a PLA to a PHA of an UNKNOWN value buys nothing. Contra's
c0d3 only becomes recoverable once LDA $8000 resolves, which is exactly what .2's bank-identifying
ROM offset delivers.

TWO SOUNDNESS TRIPWIRES THIS WILL HIT, both already documented in code:
1. BoardBankAnalyzer.callSiteRegisters (:1220-1229) scans the CALLER with NO_HOOKS, so no
   strategy's load resolution applies there. Resolving contra's LDA $8000 at a call site needs
   those caller-side scans to see mirrors -- i.e. NO_HOOKS must become mirror-aware.
2. That immediately invalidates callSiteRegCache's stated soundness argument (:573-579):
   'callSiteRegisters is a function of (program, call address) alone, since its three scans use
   NO_HOOKS and never consult tracked state.' Make the caller-side scans state-dependent and the
   memo must be re-keyed or dropped. This is a second tripwire in the same family as
   MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.cacheable()'s -- treat it the same way.

UNBLOCKS grm-v60 (far-call trampoline), jointly with grm-e7v.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED IN PRACTICE BY grm-6pi (2026-08-02). wizwarr's 7 FUN_ffc0 call sites now WARN
rather than assert a wrong bank. That is honest but not optimal: the true post-call effect of a
switch/call/restore trampoline is UNCHANGED, which HelperDeposit can already express as
ownedMask = 0. Claiming it requires VERIFYING the pair -- pairing the PHA at $FFC6 with the PLA at
$FFD3 -- which is exactly this bead. So this bead now has a concrete, measurable payoff on a
pinned ROM: 7 warnings should become verified no-ops, and wizwarr's analysis gets strictly better
without inventing anything.

SECOND HALF, and the more interesting one: the requested bank IS live -- but only for the INNER
call. $FFD0 JSR $FFDA -> JMP ($00C1) runs the target routine in the requested bank. So a complete
model of this trampoline says 'callee runs in bank N, caller resumes unchanged', which is
grm-v60's far-call shape in a JSR-and-return variant rather than GxROM's return-address-rewriting
one. Worth handling together.

MEASURED CONTEXT for whoever picks this up (from grm-6pi):
  Call sites: 80c2 (bank 7), d56e (3), d691 (1), e5b1 (1, reached by JMP not JSR), e924 (4),
              e92b (6), e942 (4).
  $C1/$C2 is the indirect target pointer; the caller passes the LOW byte in Y (STY $C1) and the
  bank in A. e.g. $80BE LDY #$03 / $80C0 LDA #$07 / $80C2 JSR $FFC0.
  Every writer of the $C5 shadow in the image: 80ad, 8be8 (LDA $C5 / EOR #$10 / STA $C5 -- a
  mirroring toggle, note it touches bit 4 which is OUTSIDE the 3-bit tracked field), d682, and the
  trampoline's own ffcb/ffd4.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PARTIAL, NARROW IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (grm-mu7 increment 2, 2026-08-04) -- this bead is NOT closed by it, and the distinction matters.

WHAT LANDED. BoardBankAnalyzer.argumentSurvivesPrologue now models BOTH halves this bead names, but as a PRESERVATION model rather than a value model. It answers only 'does the caller's byte still reach the helper's first switch site', never 'what is it' -- the value still comes from the ordinary caller-side scan. So it needs no stack-slot value domain in StoredValueScanner, no cross-block forwarding, and nothing from grm-mej.2; it is not blocked the way this bead is.

  STACK HALF: a shadow stack over the entry..firstSite walk. PHA pushes 'is this the argument', PLA pops it back, PHP/PLP are modelled only to keep the DEPTH honest so an interleaved status push cannot make a later PLA pop the wrong byte. Anything else that moves the stack pointer abandons the model. (Note: comparing the written register to CompilerSpec.getStackPointer() must be done by BASE register -- the 6502 declares SP (2-byte) and S (1-byte) over the same bytes, and TXS's p-code writes the one getStackPointer() does not answer. An equals() test silently reports that TXS leaves the stack alone.)

  MEMORY HALF: the set of cells the walk watched the argument being stored to and which nothing has written since; a load from one is a restore. Straight-line only -- any non-fall-through flow clears it, because 'restored' is a claim that points the UNSAFE way if a branch could skip the restore. Indexed store clears everything (runtime-dependent target).

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT DO, i.e. what is left for this bead: carry a VALUE through a save/restore. contra's 'LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA / TAY / JSR $C13F' and shenlong's 'LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC' both need the value, not just the knowledge that A survived. Likewise the wizwarr FUN_ffc0 payoff in the comment above (7 warnings -> verified no-ops) needs pairing to prove ownedMask=0, which preservation alone cannot assert. Still blocked on grm-mej.2 for exactly the reason stated.

THREE NEW MEASURED SHAPES for this bead's corpus, all GME-set MMC1, all disassembled from the pinned ROM bytes (not inferred):

  cv2 FUN_c187 -- stack only:
    c187 PHA / c188 LDA #$01 / c18a STA $0103 / c18d PLA / c18e STA $FFFF (chain)
  kicarus FUN_c17f -- stack, with a shadow write after the restore:
    c17f PHA / c180 LDA $0100 / c183 AND #$7F / c185 STA $2000 / c188 PLA / c189 STA $B6 / c18b STA $FFFF (chain)
  dodge FUN_ff08 -- stack AND memory, the interesting one:
    ff08 PHA / ff09 SEI / ff0a LDA $FF / ff0c AND #$7F / ff0e STA $2000 / ff11 PLA / ff12 STA $0103
    / ff15 LDA $FF / ff17 PHA / ff18 AND #$7F / ff1a STA $FF / ff1c LDA $0103 / ff1f STA $FFFF (chain)
  dodge is why the memory half is not optional: the argument comes off the stack and is IMMEDIATELY parked in RAM because A is needed again for the mirroring shadow, then reloaded just before the chain. A stack-only model declines it. Note this store/reload is straight-line and within one block, so it is grm-mej.1 territory rather than this bead's cross-block case -- but the guard does not use the scanner, so it needed its own model.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the process matters more than the code: grm-mu7's first increment guarded on 'does anything write argReg between entry and firstSite', which is a poor proxy -- real helpers routinely save and restore. It passed all 45 synthetic goldens (not one of them saves and restores) and cost the real-ROM tier kicarus's 215 overlay instructions, dodge's 10692, and cv2's bank comments. build-and-test.sh does NOT run the real-ROM tier, so the full gate was green throughout.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TWO CONCRETE BLMASTER INSTANCES from the hand pass on grm-8iy.5 (2026-08-05), one for each half
of this bead.

CROSS-BLOCK MEMORY FORWARDING (the memory-slot save/restore). FUN_e9b8 and its sibling at e9d5
copy $DB into $D3 at entry, call out to routines that switch banks freely, then reload A from
$D3 and call e61b to restore. Same idiom as a stack save but through a fixed RAM slot. Also
FUN_eb98: JSR e63c with an immediate 5, JSR deeb, then JSR e63c with $DB to restore -- which is
why the one non-home bank blmaster does recover, ec53 prg_bank=5, dies two instructions later
(BANKCONSUME walk ec53 steps=2 stop=UNKNOWN). The walk hits the unknown restore leg; the real
consumer is the JSR deeb in between. Recovering the restore would keep the state alive across it.

STACK PHA/PLA PAIRING. FUN_c9a4 pushes the packed bank selector, calls out, and pops it back:
    TXA / PHA / JSR ea3a / PLA / LSR A x4 / AND #$0F / STA $D3
The JSR ea3a in the middle itself switches banks, so this is a genuine cross-call stack forward,
not an intra-block one. Note c9a4 needs three other things besides this to recover (see
grm-8iy.5 section 5 and grm-wul), so it is a test case for this bead but not an acceptance
target on its own.

title: Bank warnings/info as EOL comments, and a stop-reason classification for honest-vs-analyzer-limit gaps
description:
Two related pieces, deferred from grm-hum (its increment 4, descoped when 2b/3 turned out to be
the blocking work).

--- PART 1: CLASSIFY WHY RECOVERY FAILED ---
Today every unrecovered site gets the same WARNING bookmark, whether the value is genuinely
runtime-determined or the analyzer simply gave up. Those deserve different treatment.
Have resolveStoredValue report a STOP REASON alongside its BankState (a small enum on a return
record -- do NOT reuse StopReason/StopConditions, which belong to EmulationRecovery):
  RUNTIME_SOURCE   terminated on a load from a WRITABLE block, a PLA, or a register-clobbering
                   call. The value genuinely is not static. -> NOTE, not WARNING.
  HELPER_ARGUMENT  the site is inside a recognized helper and the unresolved input is a register
                   live at the helper's entry (contra c142, wizwarr ffcd/ffd6). -> NOTE.
  ANALYZER_LIMIT   scan budget, block boundary, control-flow join, mid-scan mechanism-write
