This REVERSES docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 question 2, which had recommended best-effort materialization; that question is now marked answered in the doc.

2. THIS BEAD NEEDS AN ANALYZER OR COMMAND FRONT-END, not loader-time-only work. Because the directive is ignored when the ROM is absent, the 'user supplies a KERNAL ROM later' path is only reachable if the directive can be re-evaluated after load. TransferMaterializer.materialize is idempotent (COPY_xxxx block-exists guard) and C64CopyLoopAnalyzer declares setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis, so a re-runnable front-end gets this for free -- a purely loader-time implementation makes it unreachable.

3. USE TransferMaterializer.materialize(program, spec, category, monitor, log). Do not reimplement placement. It already handles carve-vs-overlay selection, provenance, disassembly directive, and reference bridging. Emit TargetKind.SAME_SPACE unless you have a reason to force one.

NAMING NIT: this bead's title says 'copied_to', but docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 4 defines the schema key as 'copied_from' (attached to the DESTINATION region, naming its source). Code and docs were normalized to copied_from on 2026-07-25; the bead title is the last holdout and should be renamed.
close_reason: copied_from descriptor directive shipped: MapCompiler.buildCopiedFrom with address normalization and build-failing validation (source must resolve, range inside the region, entry inside the range), machines/c64.yaml carries the CHRGET hint, and DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer consumes it as a BYTE_ANALYZER at BLOCK_ANALYSIS priority with setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis. Analyzer not loader, because the ROM-gated rule makes 'supply the KERNAL later, re-run' the recovery path and only a re-runnable front-end reaches it. Both halves covered end to end in c64-loader against the synthetic kernal.bin: copyhinttest asserts COPY_0073 holds a2..b9, copyhintnorom asserts no block and ZEROPAGE not even split. Commit d1a8371.

title: Run-from-elsewhere: manual command/script front-end
description: The auto copy-loop recognizer (C64CopyLoopAnalyzer, grm-1.7.1 first increment) only catches loops matching its pattern. The user's workflow: after the analyzer catches what it can, the human works through the code and finds MORE copies the recognizer missed (especially complex loaders, e.g. SPC700). A user-invoked Ghidra script/command should take source/dest/size, a transform selector (identity now; constant-XOR / running-XOR later, the latter routing through grm-edg EmulationRecovery to also cover the grm-1.7.2 case), and a separate-Program flag (SPC700, grm-1.7.3). It emits a TransferSpec into the SAME materialize() core the analyzer uses, so provenance/disassembly/dual-home are shared. This is the long-tail workhorse; build quickly after the auto recognizer.
close_reason: Both front-ends shipped. ghidra_scripts/RunFromElsewhereTransfer.java (interactive ask* / headless key:value, split on ':' twice so overlay-qualified addresses survive) and RunFromElsewherePlugin (pure adapter, submits a BackgroundCommand since a Swing action holds no transaction). Both funnel through the new public RunFromElsewhere facade, as does the recognizer and the descriptor directive. Script covered headlessly by the rfemanual fixture; the plugin has NO automated regression path by construction (docs/testing.md rules out GUI test infra), which is why it holds zero logic. Commits b6328fa, 5b76946. Proven on a real target: it is what materializes Zelda's PRG-RAM copy, which the auto recognizer cannot see.

title: Real-ROM value-recovery gap: Bandai FCG / GxROM titles pass bank# via helper/table, so no bank values resolve
description: Found in grm-hdn real-ROM acceptance (goldens dbz2/dbz_datach/dbz_saiyan/dragonpower/shenlong). Block/overlay layout is correct on all, but every detected switch site is unrecoverable: warnings 'call to bank-switch helper FUN_xxxx whose bank argument could not be recovered at this call site' and 'mechanism write with a genuinely undeterminable value'. Result: 0 resolved bank-> comments and 0 cross-bank overlay refs on these titles -- the headline retargeting feature contributes nothing. These games load the bank number from a variable/table rather than an immediate, defeating immediate/mask-algebra recovery. This is a known value-recovery limitation class (helper-arg recovery, gib.2-style context resolution), not a descriptor bug (mappers 16/157/159/66 all layout correctly). Track as the real-ROM motivation for deeper value recovery (table/variable-fed bank args, helper-arg recovery through a stored parameter). Contrast titles where immediates work: Mega Man (UxROM) 1781 refs, wizwarr (AxROM) concrete bank->0/3/7.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANOTHER INSTANCE, ON A TITLE THAT OTHERWISE WORKS (2026-08-06, from the grm-hum megaman trace).
This bead is scoped to Bandai FCG / GxROM titles where NO bank values resolve. megaman is the
opposite case -- it resolves 156 bank comments and 1704 overlay refs -- and still contains this
bead shape in one concentrated place:

  FUN_d846 sends 10 chunks of data to the PPU and sets the PRG bank from a STRIDE-2 TABLE AT
  d81e once per chunk. Ten switch sites in one loop, each taking its bank from a table entry
  rather than an immediate.

Worth recording because it separates two things this bead currently blends: "the title recovers
nothing" and "the value arrives via a table". megaman shows the second without the first. That
makes it a better development subject than the Dragon Ball titles for the table-fed half of the
work -- the surrounding machinery already functions, so a table-read implementation can be
measured against a working baseline instead of against zero.

Also note grm-8iy.4 asked that this bead not be silently widened past Bandai FCG / GxROM without
retitling. Same applies here: this is a data point for the table-fed VALUE problem, not a claim
that megaman belongs to this bead.

title: Shippable optional real-ROM test tier (hash-pinned NES board goldens)
description: Build a reproducible, shippable-but-optional real-ROM regression tier for the NES board descriptors, feeding grm-hdn's acceptance pass. ROM binaries are NOT committed (copyright+size); they are supplied at run time via a ROM library dir. Each pinned title is identified by whole-file SHA-256 so the harness validates against the exact known-good dump and cleanly SKIPs (never falsely FAILs) when a ROM is absent or is a different/bad dump (the library has bad-dump variants with wrong mapper header bytes: Dr Mario [o4]/Tetris [b3]->m65). Deliverables: (1) tools/banktest/RealRomDump.java -- name-agnostic, read-only GhidraScript emitting a bounded/normalized/copyright-safe REALROM golden (block layout, overlay-space + ref counts, bounded samples of bank-> comments / cross-bank overlay refs / warning bookmarks, and the program SHA-256); no ROM bytes or disassembly. (2) tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv pinning id/title/sha256/mapper/board/golden/loader_opts. (3) tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check|bless <romdir...> -- standalone (NOT a run-banktest.sh chunk, NOT in build-and-test.sh 'all'), reuses build/ghidra-home isolation like measure-overlay-scale.sh, hash-indexes the library, imports via NesRomLoader + full analysis + RealRomDump postScript, diffs/bless goldens, second-layer asserts dumped sha256==manifest. (4) docs/testing.md update. Pinned set ~10-12: MMC1 zelda, MMC3 smb3, UxROM contra(+megaman), AxROM wizwarr, NROM smb, plus newly-shipped Bandai FCG (m16 Dragon Ball + 157 Datach + 159) and GxROM (Dragon Power, Shen Long no Nazo).
close_reason: grm-zai: shippable hash-pinned real-ROM test tier landed (33b2c50). grm-hdn: acceptance pass run across 12 real ROMs; per-board results recorded, 3 follow-up findings filed (grm-9oz/m95/y20).

title: Wire 'gradle test' into the acceptance gate as a fast chunk
description: Spike grm-32f.1 left the JUnit test target opt-in (not in buildExtension dependsOn, not run by build-and-test.sh). Once real (non-redundant) unit tests exist, add a 'gradle test' invocation to tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh as a selectable chunk so it gates acceptance alongside the E2E golden suite, while staying fast for the dev loop. Program-fixture tests cost ~1.5s/class (AbstractGenericTest Application bootstrap); pure tests are ~instant -- keep the chunk fast. E2E golden suite REMAINS the out-of-process acceptance authority; gradle test is additive for pure/program-fixture logic.
acceptance_criteria: build-and-test.sh exposes a unit/junit chunk that runs 'gradle test'; documented in the chunk map; full gate green.
notes: grm-32f.4 already did the BLUNT wiring: build-and-test.sh now runs the `test` task (in place of the retired verify* JavaExec tasks) for the all/basic-petscii/basic-dialects/petscii-strings/bit-algebra selections, and the full `all` gate runs it. Remaining scope for 32f.5 is the FAST/selective part: `test` is currently monolithic (runs the whole src/test/java suite wherever invoked), so a partial chunk like nes-banking pays for Ghidra-bootstrap program-fixture tests it doesn't need. Make test selection per-chunk (e.g. gradle test --tests <pattern> mapped from the chunk), and/or add a dedicated fast `unit`/`junit` chunk. The bit-algebra chunk name is now a misnomer (runs whole suite) -- consider renaming as part of this.
close_reason: Gave the JUnit suite its own selectable chunk: renamed the misnamed bit-algebra chunk to `unit` (it already ran the whole suite). `check unit` runs `gradle test` only (no extension build/install); the full `all` gate runs headless + unit. Decoupled headless chunks from JUnit (undoing grm-32f.4's blunt coupling) so a targeted dev loop pays zero JUnit cost. Deliberately skipped finer per-chunk --tests scoping (suite is small/fast; chunk->class map would be fragile). Chunk map/docs updated (build-and-test.sh, CLAUDE.md, testing.md). Full gate green; `check unit` verified standalone. Commit b43101f.

title: Migrate bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers to JUnit @Test in the test source set
description: Spike grm-32f.1 proved the gradle test target works (Ghidra AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder, JUnit4). Migrate the existing verifiers from main()+System.exit+JavaExec into JUnit @Test under src/test/java, retiring the per-verifier source sets/JavaExec tasks: bitAlgebraCheck (pure), gdtBuilder MapCompilerVerify/DescriptorCompositionVerify (pure+gson+snakeyaml), petsciiCheck (main.output+gson). CAVEAT: verifyCharsets deliberately relies on the JavaExec classpath BEING the forked JVM system classpath so Charset.forName exercises real ServiceLoader SPI discovery (build.gradle staged META-INF/services + .map resources); a Test-worker fork must be verified to exercise the same SPI path before charset moves -- flag, don't assume; may stay JavaExec if not. Do incrementally; each verifier can be its own commit. MapCompilerParsingTest (from the spike) is the reference pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Verifiers run as JUnit @Test with per-assertion reporting; old JavaExec verify* tasks removed or reduced; verifyCharsets ServiceLoader path resolved (migrated or documented why it stays); full acceptance gate still green.
close_reason: Migrated all 5 bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers (verifyBitAlgebra/verifyMapCompiler/verifyDescriptorComposition/verifyPetsciiMapper/verifyCharsets) to JUnit4 @Test classes under src/test/java with full coverage preserved. Charset ServiceLoader caveat RESOLVED in favor of migration: Gradle Test-worker fork exercises real SPI discovery (RetroCharsetProviderTest 6/6 green). Retired the 3 check source sets + 5 verify* tasks in build.gradle; wired the  task into build-and-test.sh in their place; deleted the superseded spike MapCompilerParsingTest; refreshed docs. Full acceptance gate green (SUITE OK). Commit a748814.

title: NES/SNES .tbl per-game text tables: parser, loader option, TblStringAnalyzer
description: Split out of grm-1.4 by user decision (2026-07-19): per-game dynamic tables cannot be JVM charsets (SPI enumerates once at launch). Architecture (decided in grm-1.4 planning): (1) retromachines.text.TblTable — pure parser + longest-prefix decoder, zero Ghidra imports; MVP grammar per Nightcrawler Table File Format standard: # comments/blank lines, multi-byte HH...=text entries (longest hex match wins), /HH=[label] end-of-string tokens, [$XX] raw-byte fallback, tolerate legacy *XX= linebreak entries and trailing \n; DEFER $-control params and !/@ table switching. (2) Loader option on NesRomLoader styled after RomFileOption (path + Browse + headless arg + Preferences memory); at import store the RAW .tbl text verbatim + source filename in a dedicated Program options node ('Retro Text Table') so projects stay portable and re-analysis never needs the file. (3) TblStringAnalyzer gated on that property: decodes end-token-terminated runs via longest match; MVP output = PRE comments + bookmarks (C64BasicAnalyzer philosophy); custom dynamic datatype is a possible later phase. Verification: verifyTblParser pure-gradle task + NES fixture with golden.
acceptance_criteria: verifyTblParser passes; NES fixture golden shows decoded .tbl strings as PRE comments/bookmarks; full gate green.

title: C64 screen-code mapping family: screencode.yaml, compiler, data/screencode.map
description: Phase B of the grm-1.4 plan (can trail C-F without blocking). machines/generated/screencode.yaml: permutation rules referencing the PETSCII unicode layer (screen 0x00-0x1F <- petscii 0x40-0x5F, 0x20-0x3F identity, 0x40-0x5F <- 0x60-0x7F, 0x60-0x7F <- 0xA0-0xBF; 0x80-0xFF reverse-video -> glyph of b&0x7F, canonical low byte on encode, reverse-video lossy by design), both variants, provenance. ScreencodeCompiler reusing PetsciiCompiler expansion helpers -> data/screencode.map (unicode_variants 2x256 + encode; NO escaped layer — petcat convention does not apply to screen codes). build.gradle buildScreencodeMap task mirroring buildPetsciiMap, added to buildExtension deps and stageCharsetResources inputs. Extends verifyCharsets screencode assertions (grm-1.4.3 provider already serves these names once the map exists).
acceptance_criteria: verifyCharsets screencode checks pass; x-c64-screencode-* charsets resolve; full gate green.
close_reason: Screen-code family landed: permutation-based screencode.yaml (PRG Appendix B verified, no overrides), ScreencodeCompiler reusing PetsciiCompiler helpers, buildScreencodeMap wired, verifyCharsets full screencode checks 2067 cases, full gate SUITE OK. Reverse-video mechanism comment corrected per user (CHARROM copies, not hardware inversion).

title: gdtbuilder: extract shared harness for Verify* tools (write/check/expectError/temp-dir copied 3x)
description: From /code-review of commit cac2c16. DescriptorCompositionVerify.java's write() and check() are byte-for-byte identical to MapCompilerVerify.java's, and both main() methods share verbatim Files.createTempDirectory / try-finally / Files.walk-reverse-delete boilerplate; tools/petscii/PetsciiMapperVerify.java independently reinvents the same standalone-verify pattern. Extract a small shared VerifyHarness (write/check/expectError hook/temp-dir lifecycle) in the gdtbuilder package so a harness fix (e.g. Windows temp-dir file-lock cleanup, richer failure reporting) lands once; the next Verify* tool reuses it instead of a fourth copy.
acceptance_criteria: One shared harness used by DescriptorCompositionVerify and MapCompilerVerify (PetsciiMapperVerify optional if cross-source-set sharing is awkward); verifyDescriptorComposition, verifyPetsciiMapper, and the full build-and-test.sh check stay green.
close_reason: Extracted gdtbuilder.VerifyHarness holding the shared temp-dir lifecycle (run), write, check, and the throws-and-contains assertion tail (expectThrows). DescriptorCompositionVerify and MapCompilerVerify now delegate to it via VerifyHarness.run + static imports; their expectError/expectCompileError helpers delegate to expectThrows. Removed the duplicated write/check methods and now-unused File/Comparator imports from both. PetsciiMapperVerify left out (separate petsciiCheck source set, default package, no shared classpath, and doesn't use the temp-dir/write/check pattern) per the AC. Both verifiers print 'verification passed'; full build-and-test.sh check green; no golden churn; net -48 lines.

title: Composition validation gaps: duplicate-name guards for regions/symbols/physical; context_register typo is silent
description:
From /code-review of commit cac2c16 (grm-5zg shared fragment composition). Two verified gaps:

1. DUPLICATE-NAME GUARDS ONLY COVER types[]: list-append merge means a board-local list entry can share a name with a fragment entry. grm-5zg added GdtBuilder.validateUniqueTypeNames for types[], but memory.regions[], symbols[] set names, and physical[] names have no uniqueness check in MapCompiler — findRegion (~line 756) is first-match-wins, so a duplicate silently shadows for lookups (e.g. rom_images target/size validation) while BOTH entries are emitted into the compiled .map. A board author who adds a local region named like a fragment's (natural given 'local override' semantics for maps) gets silent wrong output. Fix: extend uniqueness validation to regions/symbols/physical at MapCompiler load, mirroring validateUniqueTypeNames; add DescriptorCompositionVerify cases.

2. TYPO'D context_register HAS ZERO DIAGNOSTIC: cac2c16 removed SCHEMA.md's documented load-time descriptor<->language agreement check ('fails with a clear error') when making context_register optional. Now MapCompiler passes any name through unchecked and BoardBankAnalyzer.stampContextRegister (~1494) silently returns when program.getRegister() is null — a typo like 'c64bnk' disables context stamping with no compile error, no log, no bookmark. Minimal fix: log a warning in stampContextRegister when the option is present but the register is undeclared by the language; better: validate at map compile time once languages are bundled (grm-bk6).
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate region/symbol-set/physical names fail map compile with a clear error (verifier case added); a context_register naming a register the language does not declare produces at least a logged warning at analysis time; full build-and-test.sh check green.
close_reason: Fixed both gaps. (1) MapCompiler now validates uniqueness of memory.regions[] names, physical[] names, and symbols[] set names via a validateUniqueNames helper mirroring GdtBuilder.validateUniqueTypeNames; duplicates fail compile with '<context> <name> is declared twice'. Added 3 MapCompilerVerify cases (dup-region/dup-physical/dup-symbol-set). (2) BoardBankAnalyzer.stampContextRegister now logs a warning via log.appendMsg when context_register is present but names a register the language does not declare (was a silent return); SCHEMA.md updated to document the warning. Compile-time cross-check deferred to grm-bk6. Full build-and-test.sh check green, no golden churn.

title: Declarative-map debt from PRG rework: inert formats section, zero-consumer load_target, hardcoded P6510, derivable PRG_* properties
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727 — confirmed cleanup/altitude items, none user-visible today:

1. INERT formats SECTION: machines/c64.yaml declares formats.prg (extensions [.prg,.p00], 2-byte header, placement, initial_bank_state) and docs/SCHEMA.md (~359) documents formats.prg.placement as selecting the policy, but NO Java reads the formats section — C64PrgLoader hardcodes '.prg' (~207; the declared .p00 is not honored) and the 2-byte header (~267). Either wire the loader to read it or delete the section+docs.

2. ZERO-CONSUMER load_target: this range removed the only YAML use and the only Java reader, but MapCompiler (~216-225) still validates/passes it through and MAP_FORMAT.md (~74) / SCHEMA.md (~349-368) re-document it as 'legacy'. Delete the mechanism (maps are regenerable).

3. HARDCODED P6510: planPrgSlices (~489, also ~360) uses kind.equals("ram") || name.equals("P6510") to widen placement targets — machine geometry in Java. A declarative per-region flag in the descriptor (what load_target could have become) removes the name special case before the next machine (C128 MMU, TED) needs it.

4. DERIVABLE PRG_* PROPERTIES: persistPrgPlacement (~654-658) writes four Program-Info properties where load address, length, and wrapped are all derivable from PRG_SLICES; C64BasicAnalyzer does four Options reads to reassemble them (~111-116, 132). Persist slices only + accessors. Related: load() resolves the entry via the one-arg resolvePrgAddress which re-reads and re-parses the JSON just written (~400) instead of using live locals — and a parse failure silently drops the entry point (caught at ~427).

5. createDirectBlock (~618-634) bypasses MemoryBlockUtils (used by every sibling block path) for non-overlay slices; the raw-Memory path is only needed for slices sharing a pre-created overlay space.
acceptance_criteria: formats section either consumed or removed from yaml+docs; load_target deleted from MapCompiler+docs; P6510 special case replaced by a descriptor flag; single source of truth for PRG placement metadata; build-and-test.sh check green.

title: banktest: c000emutest duplicates emu-recovery harness/fixture and drops two criteria
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. checkC000EmuRecovery (tools/banktest/VerifyBankTest.java ~289-311) copy-pastes checkEmuRecovery's (~180-222) recipe — same EmulationRecovery construction, StopConditions.dirtyWatch+instructionFuel(10_000), IoPolicy.volatileBlocks, recoveredBytes, expected {1..8} — but silently drops the emu-not-suspect and emu-dirty-covers-target criteria the original asserts, so the new golden fixture verifies strictly less without that being visible. Likewise mkprgloadtest.py c000_emu_payload() (~50-63) duplicates mkemutest.py build() byte-for-byte except three operand bytes.

Fix: extract a shared verifyEmuRecovery(idPrefix, entry, payloadAddr) mirroring the existing verifyDecryptRecovery pattern (~340), restore the two dropped criteria to the c000 variant (then bless the expected dump), and parameterize mkemutest.build() by load address so mkprgloadtest imports it.

Minor same-file cleanups to fold in: blockAt() duplicates overlayAddr() resolution with a different missing-space policy (~1364 vs ~1432); the two fileOffset overloads can delegate (~1347/1355); checkPrgPlacement/checkPrgWrap compute describeBlock/bytesAt/fileOffset twice per block (println + criterion).
acceptance_criteria: One shared emu-recovery verifier used by both tests; c000emutest asserts suspect+dirty-coverage criteria; one payload builder parameterized by address; full build-and-test.sh check green (bless expected diffs after review).

title: C64BasicAnalyzer efficiency: per-byte address resolution and full re-work on every added() round
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. Two confirmed efficiency regressions in C64BasicAnalyzer.java:

1. PER-BYTE RESOLUTION (~lines 139, 210-213): the ByteSource lambda and the line-text loop resolve a placed Address per byte (LoadedSlice scan + AddressFactory.getAddressSpace string lookup + Address alloc + Memory.getByte), replacing the previous single bulk Memory.getBytes. ~100K+ round trips for a large PRG per invocation. The lambda also re-implements the file's own placedAddress() helper verbatim (~262-266) instead of calling it — if the fallback policy changes, the walker and annotation pass diverge. Fix: bulk-read each slice once into byte[], serve the walker from arrays; make the lambda call placedAddress().

2. NO EARLY-OUT (~line 163): the AnalyzerRunLog flag only suppresses one log line; every added() invocation still re-runs the full BASIC walk, DescriptorSupport.openGdt() disk I/O, PetsciiMapper.load(), and re-types/re-comments every line — all no-ops after the first run. As a byte-analyzer it re-fires whenever bytes are added (e.g. per DECRYPTED_ overlay). Fix: early-return (or skip the annotation phase) when the run-log/persisted state shows the work is done and inputs unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Walker reads via bulk getBytes per slice; lambda delegates to placedAddress(); repeat added() rounds skip gdt/petscii I/O and re-annotation; banktest BASIC fixtures still pass.

title: C64BasicAnalyzer: SYS argument >65535 wraps into bogus zero-page function
description: From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. renderLine (C64BasicAnalyzer.java ~359-371) accumulates the SYS decimal literal into a long with no bound check then casts to int, and markSysEntry (~285) masks with & 0xFFFF. A SYS literal above 65535 — ILLEGAL QUANTITY on real hardware — silently creates an external entry point, sys_entry label, and function at the wrapped address. Repro: '10 SYS 65600' -> function created in zero page at $0040. Fix: range-check the parsed value (0-65535) and skip/bookmark out-of-range SYS targets instead of masking.
acceptance_criteria: SYS >65535 produces no function/entry; ideally a warning bookmark; existing valid SYS fixtures unchanged.
notes: Fixed by c04ceae: SYS decimal accumulation now rejects values above 65535 before conversion, routes invalid arguments to a Note bookmark, and never wraps through markSysEntry. Dedicated c64basicoverflowtest verifies SYS 65536 yields note=true and functionAt0000=false. Focused basic-dialects suite reverified PASS on 2026-07-18.
close_reason: Fixed by c04ceae; overflow regression passes with no wrapped function and a warning Note

title: Commodore 128 machine descriptor and BASIC 7 import path
description: After PET/BASIC 4 bring-up, add a real C128 consumer for grm-1.6.1. title: Decide c64ref sourcing: git submodule + build-time generation vs committed generated files
description: grm-hnm adds a Python generator (tools/gensymbols/) that converts mist64/c64ref reference data into machines/generated/c64ref-*.yaml symbol files. Decide how c64ref is sourced for the build: (a) CURRENT APPROACH -- generator + COMMITTED generated/*.yaml; c64ref is a manual/dev-time input (cloned ad hoc to D:/git/c64ref), the generated YAMLs are committed static files (matching the existing committed generated/*.yaml pattern), regenerated by manually re-running the generator when c64ref updates; the build does NOT depend on c64ref being present. (b) SUBMODULE -- add mist64/c64ref as a git submodule and run the generator as a Gradle task at build time, so symbols are always regenerated from pinned-upstream source; pros: always in sync, reproducible from source, no stale committed artifacts; cons: couples the build to submodule checkout (network/size), a large reference repo vendored, generator must run every build, licensing/provenance of the vendored data travels with the repo. Trade-off is build reproducibility/freshness vs build simplicity + reviewable committed artifacts. Consider licensing (c64ref is clean-ish but individual source texts have book provenance) and whether upstream churns. Defer until the generator + first generated sets (grm-hnm) land, then choose. User-requested capture 2026-07-13.

title: C64 loader: optionally populate KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN ROM regions from user-supplied ROM files

Keep it optional: absent ROM files -> current behavior (uninitialized ROM regions), no regression. Benefits: (1) ROM routines (KERNAL/BASIC entry points) become disassemblable and callable-into from user code; (2) ENABLES the ROM-sourced dual-home case in grm-1.7.1 -- the canonical CHRGET->$73 fixture needs the BASIC ROM CHRGET source bytes present so a createByteMappedBlock at $0073 can share them. title: grm-1.7.2 tier 2: test emulation-assisted decrypt of a rolling/computed-key loop
description: C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer.apply() already routes a ROLLING/COMPUTED KeyModel (EOR keytab,X etc.) with AUTO confidence to the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness (dirty-watch on the target range, IoPolicy.volatileBlocks) and materializes the read-back bytes via the shared overlay path -- but NO banktest fixture exercises this path, so tier 2 is wired but unverified. Add a rolling-key decrypt .prg fixture (e.g. LDA base,X / EOR keytab,X / STA base,X / DEX / BPL with a JMP into range and a small key table) + a VerifyBankTest branch asserting the emulated recovery produces the correct plaintext overlay and, if the loop reads only initialized RAM, a NOTE (not SUSPECT/WARNING) bookmark. title: C64 memory map: let a PRG load at any RAM address, not just RAM_MAIN ($0800-$9FFF)
description: The c64.yaml descriptor's load_target region RAM_MAIN is only $0800-$9FFF, so C64PrgLoader can only carve a PRG into the base address space when its load address falls in that window. A PRG loading elsewhere in real C64 RAM -- e.g. $C000 (the 4K RAM block), or RAM-under-ROM ($A000-$BFFF BASIC, $E000-$FFFF KERNAL) or RAM-under-IO ($D000-$DFFF) -- conflicts with the base block already mapped there and the loader falls back to placing the PRG in a NEW OVERLAY space instead of base RAM. Consequences: (1) the program's bytes are not where a naive base-space consumer expects them; surfaced concretely by grm-edg's EmulationRecovery fixture, whose $C000-loaded PRG landed in an overlay so EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (which copies each block into ITS space) left base $C000 uninitialized -> immediate decode fault. Worked around by loading the fixture at $2000 (inside RAM_MAIN), but that is a fixture band-aid, not a fix. Rethink the C64 RAM modeling so a PRG can load at ANY RAM address: options to weigh -- (a) model all RAM regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF, and the RAM-under-ROM/IO banks) as load_target-eligible base RAM so createRamMainSplit can carve the PRG wherever it lands; (b) make the loader prefer carving PRG into whichever base RAM region contains the load address rather than only the single load_target region; (c) represent the C64's RAM-vs-ROM/IO banking so RAM-under-ROM loads map correctly. Relates to C64PrgLoader.createRamMainSplit / createPrgBlock and c64.yaml region layout. Discovered during grm-edg (2026-07-12).
design:
Use the existing home-in-base plus alternate-overlay representation, but replace the singleton RAM_MAIN carve with a descriptor-derived, 16-bit PRG routing plan.

1. Treat import as static CPU-address image placement, not KERNAL LOAD emulation. Accept payload lengths 1..65536. Destination of payload byte i is (loadAddr+i)&$FFFF. Reject >65536 before Program mutation because destinations repeat. Split wrapping input into at most two ordered source spans: [loadAddr,$FFFF] from FileBytes offset 2, then [$0000,end] from the following file offset. Preserve file order/source offset in segment metadata.
2. Partition each span at descriptor memory boundaries. Eligible physical targets are direct top-level kind:ram regions, the direct kind:ram occupant of each enumerated bank window, plus the special P6510 region for bytes at $0000/$0001. Nested IO subregions (including COLOR_RAM) are not PRG RAM targets. Reject uncovered or ambiguously covered ranges before mutation.
3. Create FileBytes once. Materialize every slice as a real initialized FileBytes-backed block at the span-derived source offset, with uninitialized prefix/suffix fragments for its target. Always-visible RAM ($0002-$9FFF and $C000-$CFFF) stays in base. RAM beneath BASIC/IO/KERNAL goes into RAM_A000/RAM_D000/RAM_E000 occupant overlay space. Preserve initial BASIC/IO/KERNAL in base and preserve overlay-space names for BoardBankAnalyzer.
4. If the image touches $0000/$0001, initialize those bytes in the P6510 region while preserving IO permissions, volatility, and R6510 typing. Emit a prominent warning/property: this records address-visible register values only; it does not simulate loader chronology, infer bank state from $01/DDR, or change descriptor initial banking. A load starting at either register gets load-start metadata/label but no executable function entry.
5. Eliminate the separate createPrgBlock conflict-fallback path. Use direct Memory creation or assert conflict-free placement; MemoryBlockUtils's initialized helper silently creates an unrelated overlay on conflict, which caused this bug.
6. Persist original load address, payload length, wrapped flag, and ordered slice records (file offset, length, address space, start) in Program Information. Keep PRG as the first slice name when practical, but migrate C64BasicAnalyzer from its single-base-block assumption. Skip BASIC sniff/detokenization for wrapped images because its monotonic interval model is not meaningful there.
7. Place entry label/function at the first slice's real address space: base:$C000 for visible RAM, RAM_A000::$A000 under BASIC, etc. Warn for an entry hidden by initial bank state. The original load address remains the placement origin even when later bytes wrap.
8. Update SCHEMA/MAP_FORMAT: C64 placement is derived from direct physical RAM targets; singleton load_target is a legacy RAM_MAIN implementation detail. formats.prg.placement:load_address remains authoritative.

Reject a single 64K base RAM block: it displaces initial BASIC/IO/KERNAL and regresses references such as JSR $FFD2. Also reject a 64K physical overlay plus byte-mapped CPU views for this bead: Ghidra 12.1.2 byte-mapped blocks report isInitialized=false and EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram skips them; listings/symbols and emulator writes do not share alias identity. Revisit a true physical RAM space only with first-class L4/context-aware resolution.

Acceptance: preserve $0801 behavior; add $C000 EmulationRecovery; $A000/$D000/$E000 placement and home-in-base checks; base/base and base/window boundary slicing; wrap fixtures $FFFE+2 (no wrap), $FFFE+3, and $FFFC+8 (RAM_E000 -> P6510 -> ZEROPAGE) with exact FileBytes offsets; exactly 64KiB accepted; 65537 rejected without partial layout; touching $01 leaves banking.initial_state/home occupants unchanged. Document the rare representation limit for instructions/fallthrough straddling a base/overlay boundary.
notes:
2026-07-15 design investigation completed with three lower-tier read-only reviews (loader/map, architecture/beads, Ghidra block APIs). Consensus: generalized direct carving is the smallest hardware-truthful solution. Related beads considered: grm-edg (originating $C000 acceptance case), grm-1.7.1 (byte-mapped dual-home work; coordinate loader surface), grm-hqa (future snapshot import can reuse RAM routing), grm-wkk/grm-5tl (future L4 architecture, not blockers), grm-rua (default block noise only), grm-54p/grm-mbm (ROM coexistence), and closed grm-5tl.14/grm-1.3 (singleton load_target and home-in-base decisions being refined). No new dependency is required.
2026-07-15 user correction: real PRGs can wrap past $FFFF and place takeover vectors in low RAM (e.g. around $0300). Design revised to support modulo-64K static placement for payloads up to 64KiB instead of rejecting wrap. Wrapped $0000/$0001 bytes are retained as P6510 register values with a warning; full loader/banking chronology remains explicitly out of scope.
close_reason: Implemented descriptor-derived arbitrary C64 PRG placement with FileBytes-backed base/underlay slices, modulo-64K wrap through P6510 and low RAM, persisted placement metadata, overlay-aware BASIC analysis/entries, documentation, and regression fixtures for A/C/D/E placement, wrapped takeover-vector bytes/source offsets, home occupants, and C000 emulation. Full banktest suite passes.

title: Testing strategy: golden-image E2E + unit-level framework + suite partitioning
description:
High-level testing strategy for the extension. CURRENT STATE (assessed 2026-07-12, mostly fine for now): end-to-end golden-image regression via tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless — python generators synthesize test PRGs/ROMs, analyzeHeadless imports with the real loaders, VerifyBankTest.java (~1000 lines) checks criteria and diffs normalized behavior dumps against expected/; build-and-test.sh adds per-worktree isolated extension installs; sibling checkers for petscii and bit algebra. No JUnit anywhere — subagents repeatedly burn time hunting for a framework that does not exist.

THREE QUESTIONS this epic resolves:
(1) UNIT LAYER: would a framework (JUnit via Ghidra's own extension test support — AbstractGenericTest, ProgramBuilder program-fixture classes, gradle test integration) simplify test creation long-term for unit-level testing (MapCompiler parsing, StoredValueScanner bit algebra, strategy dispatch) IN ADDITION TO — not replacing — the E2E golden suite? E2E stays the acceptance authority: it exercises the real loader+analyzer stack headlessly, which unit fixtures cannot.
(2) PARTITIONING/SPEED: split the suite into related chunks (c64-banking / nes-banking / basic+petscii / bit-algebra / per-tool) so that during active development a subset relevant to the current change runs fast and often, while FULL suite passing still gates final acceptance and commits. Needs a selection mechanism (per-chunk driver args or tags) + a documented convention for which chunk covers what.
(3) LEGIBILITY: document the strategy (docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md pointer) so agents and contributors find the harness instead of searching for junit/gradle-test scaffolding that is not there.

Guiding principle: same priority order as everything else — use existing infrastructure first (Ghidra ships JUnit test scaffolding for extensions), mirror how Ghidra's own tree tests analyzers where applicable, roll our own only with recorded justification.
close_reason: All 5 children complete. Testing strategy established: 3 tiers (pure JUnit / AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder / E2E golden image), suite partitioned into selectable chunks (full 'all' gates acceptance), documented in docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointers, all bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers migrated to JUnit @Test, and the JUnit suite exposed as its own fast 'unit' chunk while E2E golden remains the out-of-process acceptance authority.

title: EmulationRecovery harness: bounded PcodeEmulator run + dirty-set capture + descriptor-driven IO policy
description: Shared bounded-emulation core decided by the grm-1.7.4 survey (docs/smc-survey.md par.6): given entry address + stop conditions (breakpoint set / exit-range / dirty-watch / instruction fuel / wall-clock) + IO policy sourced from the board descriptor (IO regions -> readUninitialized + beforeLoad behavior), run the interpreted PcodeEmulator over the current Program image (EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram) and return {dirty address set, recovered bytes, stop reason, provenance log incl. IO-read and uninitialized-RAM warnings}. Callers decide materialization (patch / overlay / byte-mapped block / new Program). Serves grm-1.7.2 tier 2, grm-1.7.3 generic uploader tier, and future banking L4 emulator integration (same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer as vision-board-banking.md par.7.1). NOT JitPcodeEmulator (SMC-unsafe passages).
notes: 2026-07-12 IMPLEMENTED + TESTED. Shipped retromachines.EmulationRecovery + support types (src/main/java/retromachines/): EmulationRecovery (core), StopConditions (fuel/wallclock/exit-range/dirty-watch), StopReason, IoPolicy (interface + volatileBlocks(Program) default deriving IO-ness from descriptor-set block volatility), ProvenanceLog (IO_READ/UNINIT_RAM_READ/WARNING/INFO + suspect()), RecoveryResult (dirty AddressSetView + per-range readback + recoveredBytes(start,len)). Uses interpreted ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator (NOT Jit -- SMC-safe by re-decode). API verified against the actual 12.1.2 install (Emulation-src.zip), NOT the D:/git/ghidra checkout which is 12.2. KEY CORRECTNESS FINDING: the concrete BytesPcodeExecutorStateSpace calls the Address-based dataWritten and the AddressSetView-based readUninitialized (via PcodeEmulationCallbacks.Wrapper injecting thread; null for shared state) -- overriding the other members of each overload pair compiles but silently never fires. Capture is gated by a 'capturing' flag flipped true only after loadProgram+initializeRegisters so setup writes don't pollute the dirty set; register/unique writes filtered by isMemorySpace(). title: End-user docs: README.md 'what it does / how to use it' guide with known-limitation workarounds
description: README.md today is contributor/roadmap-oriented (vision, board status, milestone notes). Add end-user-facing documentation for someone who just wants to USE the extension: (1) what the extension does in plain terms -- descriptor-driven loaders for retro machines (C64 PRG, NES iNES), banked-memory modeling via home blocks + overlays, bank-switch analysis with switch-site comments and cross-bank reference retargeting, bundled data types/symbols per machine, CBM BASIC detokenizing analyzer, PETSCII display strings; (2) install: download release zip (or build via gradle buildExtension), install via File > Install Extensions or unzip into the per-user Extensions dir (%APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC/Extensions/), version-match caveat; (3) usage walkthroughs: import a .nes/.prg, which loader to pick, what the memory map / overlay blocks mean (W8000_M0_B1 naming decoded for humans), where bank-switch comments and warnings appear, how to read them; (4) KNOWN LIMITATIONS + WORKAROUNDS, e.g.: references into non-home (overlay) banks resolve only when the analyzer can prove the bank state -- how to manually retarget a reference into the right overlay when it cannot; helper-based switches with unresolvable arguments produce poison/unknown states -- what the comment says and what to do; analyzeHeadless path constraints (no parentheses, no dot-prefixed project path elements); initial bank state is an assumption (power-on latch undefined) and how to reinterpret when a game differs; one Ghidra version per built zip. Audience is a Ghidra user who has never read the design docs -- keep docs/*.md as the deep dives and link to them. Consider whether README stays single-file or gains docs/USAGE.md if it gets long (README should at least carry the elevator pitch + quickstart).
notes: 2026-07-12 addition from grm-1.7.4 survey: include a worked 'manual SMC recovery' example — Debugger pure-emulation mode (Emulate from listing, step past copier/decryptor, watch Dynamic Listing) + Copy Into Program action — as the documented escape hatch for self-modified code our automation does not recognize (docs/smc-survey.md par.3).

title: SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy: override depositHelperArgument (route via tracked select at call-site in-state)
description: Found during grm-6a7.2: a bare data-write-only MMC3 helper (STA $8001 with arg in A) is classified a helper with argReg='A' and the WHOLE select-data mechanism width, and call-site recovery uses depositHelperArgument's DEFAULT (deposit across full width) because SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy does not override it — misrepresenting the call as writing select+prg_mode+r6+r7 at once. Correct behavior mirrors serial-shift's override, but with a twist: the target depends on the TRACKED SELECT at the call site's in-state, not the switch site's address — the override signature receives the switch site but the deposit must dispatch on the caller's in-state select value (check what recoverCallArgument passes; may need the call-site in-state plumbed into depositHelperArgument — evaluate whether the existing signature suffices [switchSite + argValue + stateMask] or needs an inState parameter added with a default-preserving overload). Select known -> deposit only the targeted field (ownedMask = that field); select unknown -> ownedMask = r6|r7 with nothing known (honest poison); CHR select -> ownedMask=0 no-op. Fixture: extend nesmmc3test2 (H's callers already set up the known/unknown select contexts — add criteria on the recovered annotation values).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 from grm-6a7.2 report item 3. Interacts with grm-6a7.2's requiresOnEntry (a proper override reduces the over-wide effectMask that also feeds modifiedMask). USER ASSESSMENT (2026-07-12): bare data-write-only helpers are probably rare-to-nonexistent in real MMC3 games -- a JSR wrapping a single STA wastes cycles when you're racing the beam, so real helpers almost certainly set select+data together. Still worth implementing for mask-width precision (the over-wide default effectMask pollutes summaries/modifiedMask even for the common two-write helper shape). Treat as precision cleanup, not an expected real-game bug; keep P3.
close_reason: Implemented SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument override with state-routed dispatch. Signature grew a field-local inState param (BankSwitchStrategy interface + default + SerialShift override, which ignores it -- its routing is address-keyed); BoardBankAnalyzer.recoverCallArgument localizes runDataflow's outState into the helper mechanism's field space and passes it down. Override: even switchSite (select-write helper) deposits select+mode fields from the arg byte; odd (data-write helper) dispatches on fieldValueIfFullyKnown(inState, selectField) -- known+tracked routes to that one target field (ownedMask = field alone), known+CHR = verified no-op (ownedMask=0, no comment/no warning), unknown = honest poison of all configured target fields only (never select/prg_mode). Fixture nesmmc3test2 extended with CallerC (CHR no-op) and CallerD (R7 routing); criteria G4-G7 added; G1-G3 unchanged. Golden re-blessed for nesmmc3test2 only: e107 went from the fabricated select=2 to fully-known select=6/r6=2; e128's false select=3 comment gone (wholly-unknown deposit takes warning branch; pre-existing requiresOnEntry warning bookmark stands). RESIDUAL (per-item-6 check): requiresOnEntry/modifiedMask function-summary width is built from each function's own switch sites' effectMask, not CallEffect.ownedMask, so H's own summary stays mechanism-wide -- unaffected by this fix, still the grm-6a7.2 over-approximation. Suite: SUITE OK (check), 12/12, all pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: PETSCII mapping core: data-driven byte->display-string API (unblocks BASIC detokenizer)
description: The subset of grm-1.4 that grm-odt.1 (BASIC detokenizing analyzer) needs — scoped deliberately to unblock it without the NES/SNES tile-table half or Ghidra Charset registration (those stay on the parent). Deliverables per the design inputs recorded on grm-1.4: (1) a Java-callable PETSCII byte->display-string API (e.g. PetsciiMapper), usable outside Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery, for programmatic comment-text building; (2) both charset variants (unshifted/graphics and shifted/lowercase) selectable per call; (3) a STABLE escaped rendering convention for control/graphics bytes ({CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}-style — pick, document, freeze: it lands in golden dumps); (4) mapping data lives in a DATA file (machines/generated/ or data/, following basic-tokens.yaml / c64ref precedent), not hardcoded Java, and is shaped so future Ghidra Charset registration (parent bead) reads the same source; (5) screen codes explicitly OUT of scope here (separate mapping, parent bead). Include a small unit-test-style verification (builder-adjacent or a tiny JUnit if the repo has test infra — check; if none, a verify main() like GdtBuilder's pattern). API should be reachable from analyzer code (src/main/java/retromachines/).
design: BRIEF (scouted 2026-07-11; petcat escape tables archived at scratchpad/petscii-escapes.md). ESCAPE CONVENTION: adopt VICE petcat's SHORT ctrl1[]/ctrl2[] bracket names verbatim ({wht},{down},{rvon},{clr},{F1}..{F8},...) for $00-$1F/$80-$9F, and petcat's {$xx} lowercase-hex fallback for EVERYTHING else non-printable — including the $A0-$FF graphics range (do NOT invent names; do NOT use petcat's cbmkeys[] key-combo names — input-oriented, not glyph-oriented). Interop win: our detokenized comments re-tokenize through petcat. MUST re-pull petcat.c from canonical VICE (vice-emu.sourceforge.io or vice-emu GitHub mirror) to verify ctrl1/ctrl2 verbatim BEFORE freezing — this lands in golden dumps. UNICODE POLICY v1: none — ASCII bracket escapes only (U+1FB00 legacy-computing glyphs deferred as a future optional toDisplayUnicode(); font/rendering nondeterminism is a golden-stability risk). DATA PATH: machines/generated/petscii.yaml (source of truth, both variants, screen codes explicitly excluded) -> NEW small build tool (sibling of MapCompiler — MapCompiler is hard-bound to schema-2 machine descriptors, confirmed trap, do not reuse) -> gitignored data/petscii.map JSON -> runtime Application.findDataFileInAnyModule + gson (DescriptorSupport.loadMap pattern; consider generalizing its private JSON-load helper). Wire buildPetsciiMap into buildExtension deps; add artifact to .gitignore. API: final class PetsciiMapper, flat in retromachines/ (package is flat, no util/), enum Variant {UNSHIFTED_GRAPHICS, SHIFTED_LOWERCASE}, toDisplayEscaped(int,Variant) + toDisplayEscaped(byte[],Variant), cached load(), zero Ghidra-type deps beyond Application/gson. VERIFY: repo has NO JUnit — follow tools/bitalgebra/BitAlgebraEquivalence pattern exactly (standalone main() + own sourceSet + verifyPetsciiMapper gradle task), EXHAUSTIVE 0x00-0xFF x 2 variants (non-null everywhere, petcat-named bytes match frozen table, fallback format exactly {$xx}).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 at user request ('work on grm-1.4, getting it far enough along to unblock odt.1'). Queue: next unit after the in-flight grm-hsv.2 helper fix lands.
close_reason: PETSCII mapping core shipped. petcat convention verified against CANONICAL source (VICE-Team/svn-mirror vice/src/tools/petcat/petcat.c @ dd98b495) — verify-first caught real errors in the scouted table (f1..f8 lowercase, several ctrl1 names the mirror showed blank). machines/generated/petscii.yaml = compact rule-based source (named_controls/literals/identity_ranges/letter_range — only $41-$5A varies by variant); PetsciiCompiler (standalone, MapCompiler untouched) expands to data/petscii.map (gitignored, bundled via new buildPetsciiMap task in buildExtension). PetsciiMapper: flat retromachines/, Variant enum, load() via existing DescriptorSupport.loadMap (already generic — no new helper) + loadFromMapFile(File) verifier seam. ASCII-divergence policy: $5C(£)->backslash, $5E->^, $5F->_ (petcat verbatim); $60-$7F/$A0-$FF uniformly {$xx}. PetsciiMapperVerify (BitAlgebraEquivalence pattern, no Ghidra jars on classpath) PASS 1792 cases; buildExtension green; suite 10/10 byte-identical. grm-odt.1 now UNBLOCKED: call load() once, pick variant explicitly (SHIFTED_LOWERCASE typical for listings), screen codes out of scope.

title: SMC: survey — Ghidra Debugger/p-code emulator leverage for self-modifying code recovery
description: Research bead, feeds all three use-case children: what can Ghidra's Debugger-era machinery (PcodeEmulator, TraceRmi, emulation scripts, 'Emulate' UI) do for us headlessly and programmatically in 12.1+? Questions: (1) can we run a bounded p-code emulation of a copy/decrypt loop over program bytes WITHOUT a live target (pure emulator, no gdb/frida), capture resulting memory, and write it back into the static Program (or a Trace snapshot converted to Program view)? (2) what are the fuel/termination controls (max instructions, memory faults on unmapped IO reads — retro code touches IO registers constantly; need a fault policy: zero-fill vs abort)? (3) is Trace/snapshot the right persistence for 'memory image after boot-init ran', navigable alongside the static view? (4) precedents: existing Ghidra scripts/plugins doing emulation-assisted unpacking (search ghidra repo + community, e.g. malware-unpacking workflows — same problem shape as C64 decrypt-on-the-fly). Deliverable: written findings on the epic + go/no-go per use case (static vs emulated vs manual).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11. Do this survey FIRST when epic work starts — it decides the approach split for all three children.
close_reason: Survey complete: docs/smc-survey.md. Verdicts: 1.7.1 static (byte-mapped blocks), 1.7.2 emulation-assisted pilot on PcodeEmulator, 1.7.3 static-first (.spc + IPL parse; SPC700 sleigh NOT in stock Ghidra). Debugger = manual tier (GUI Copy Into Program); TraceRmi retro connector no-go for now; VICE snapshot import = cheap high-leverage alternative.

title: SMC: SNES SPC700 upload — cross-processor code extraction to a separate Program
description: Use case 3: SNES games upload SPC700 sound-driver code/data through the APU IO ports ($2140-$2143 handshake protocol) into the sound processor's OWN 64K address space and run it there. Different processor (SPC700 vs 65816), different address space — Ghidra Programs are single-language, so the right deliverable is arguably a SEPARATE Program: recognize/parse the upload (boot-ROM IPL handshake protocol blocks: address+length+data records, well documented on fullsnes/nesdev-adjacent references), extract the transferred image, and materialize a new SPC700-language Program in the project (headless: Program creation API; GUI: an action/script), cross-linked to the source Program (bookmarks/comments at the upload site naming the generated Program and vice versa). STRONG GME TIE-IN: this is exactly the AKAO SNES sound-driver code (FF2/FF3/CT dumpspc.pl lineage in game-music-extraction) — the extracted Program is the disassembly target for the music-driver reverse engineering that motivates the whole toolchain. Design questions: one Program per upload session vs per unique image (games re-upload variants); IPL protocol variants vs game-specific upload loops (AKAO games use their own uploader after boot); where the 'separate Program' convention gets documented for other cross-CPU cases (C64 1541 drive code upload is the same shape!).
notes: 2026-07-12 (user direction) DELIVERABLE SHAPE CORRECTION: output is a SINGLE SPC700 Program (one 64K sound-RAM image) alongside the SNES ROM (65816) Program — NOT one Program per uploaded image. A typical game runs the IPL MULTIPLE times to load separate portions of the SAME SPC700 RAM (e.g. one IPL load transfers the SPC700 driver code, another static instrument/sample data, another filter/echo settings). Recovery model = accumulate ALL IPL transfers into the one SPC700 RAM image at their target addresses (same shape as a fully-populated .spc snapshot). Each ROM-side upload site gets a bookmark cross-linking to the target range it populated. One-language-per-Program still puts SPC700 in its own Program (separate from 65816 ROM), but exactly ONE per game, built from N uploads. Updated docs/smc-survey.md par.5 (grm-1.7.3 Deliverable shape bullet) to match.

title: SMC: run-from-elsewhere — ROM->RAM copy recognition and dual-home code mapping
description: Use case 1: code copied from ROM to RAM and executed there (NES games copy hot loops/NMI stubs to RAM; C64 BASIC copies CHRGET to zero page $73 for speed; C64 games copy loaders under ROM shadows). The 'easy' one-to-one case: recognize the copy loop (source range, dest range, length — the same StoredValueScanner/idiom machinery the banking strategies use can find LDA abs,X/STA abs,X bounds), then materialize the destination as an initialized block populated with the source bytes, with provenance comments and cross-space references bridging call sites to the RAM copy (and ideally back-references to the ROM master). Design questions: loader-time (descriptor hints: 'this region is copied to X at boot' as DATA, e.g. CHRGET) vs analyzer-time (detect copy loops generically); relocation/patching during copy = NOT one-to-one — detect and warn rather than mis-map; interaction with banking overlays (source may live in a banked window). Start with descriptor-hinted static case (CHRGET as the canonical fixture), generalize to detected copies after.
notes:
2026-07-24: First increment COMPLETE + pushed (commit abb41da): the automatic copy-loop recognizer (C64CopyLoopAnalyzer) with dual-home byte-mapped overlay materialization, materialize/disassemble decoupling (data vs code), LoopIdioms shared substrate, and TransferSpec neutral core. Full acceptance gate green. Kept in_progress: remaining planned work is now sub-beads grm-1.7.1.1 (manual command front-end) and grm-1.7.1.2 (descriptor copied_to / CHRGET Tier A). Related follow-ups: grm-chu, grm-r6f, grm-1.7.5.
2026-07-25 (grm-chu): materialization was EXTRACTED out of C64CopyLoopAnalyzer into a new front-end-agnostic TransferMaterializer, and the default placement changed from byte-mapped overlay to in-place carve (split x2 -> convertToInitialized -> setBytes) in the base space. The analyzer is now recognition-only and emits TargetKind.SAME_SPACE, letting the materializer choose placement. This matters for the two open children: grm-1.7.1.1 (manual command) and grm-1.7.1.2 (descriptor hint) should both call TransferMaterializer.materialize rather than reimplementing anything -- grm-1.7.1.2 in particular runs from the LOADER, not an analyzer, which is why the extraction was necessary. Decision record: docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md; decision bead grm-7da.
close_reason:
All planned increments done; both children closed. The subsystem now has four front-ends over one materializer, reached through the public RunFromElsewhere facade: the auto recognizer (CopyLoopAnalyzer, machine-neutral), the descriptor copied_from directive, the manual GhidraScript, and the GUI plugin.

Validated on a real target end to end: The Legend of Zelda's 0x1270-byte PRG-RAM routine is materialized IN PLACE at $6C90 in the base space, so the game's 389 JSR / 87 JMP call sites into it resolve natively with no bridging -- which was grm-chu's entire motivation.

The load-bearing lesson, recorded in docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 6: the recognizer materializes ONLY with a jump into the destination proving the payload is code. The permissive rule survived C64 fixtures but produced false positives on 3 of 4 real NES ROMs, snapshotting runtime buffers (including over the stack page). It was affordable to tighten only because the deferred-call case it protected finally has its own front-ends.

Remaining follow-ups are separate beads: grm-r6f (reference retargeting, now narrowed to the overlay path only) and grm-bqs (destination inside a banked window).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 (facade): commit b6328fa adds RunFromElsewhere, the public entry point all four front-ends now go through -- the recognizer, the descriptor directive, the manual script, and the GUI plugin. TransferSpec/TransferMaterializer stay package-private deliberately: the record has grown a field per front-end (now 12 components) and publishing it would make every future field a source-breaking change. Callers build a fluent Request instead.

Two things the facade adds that the analyzer never needed, because two of the four front-ends take their input from a human or a YAML file rather than from real instruction operands:
- VALIDATION. Bad length, out-of-space range, entry point outside the copy -> a SKIPPED Result carrying the reason, plus a log line. Never a silent overlay in the wrong place.
- Result.alreadyPresent. The materializer returns SKIPPED for both 'already done' and 'failed', and telling them apart matters because re-running after supplying a ROM IS the documented recovery path.

Also landed in b6328fa: originLabel parameterizes the provenance text (three front-ends, only one has a loop, so 'copy loop -> COPY_xxxx' could not stay hard-coded); a null provenanceSite is now legal and logs instead of bookmarking, which is docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md section 6's 'log note only' rule; TransferPlacement.NEW_BLOCK for a wholly unmapped destination (grm-1.7.6 item 3); and the C64CopyLoopAnalyzer -> CopyLoopAnalyzer rename + language-based gating.

Full acceptance gate green with ZERO golden churn -- the widened analyzer gate fired no false positives on any existing NES/PET/C128 fixture.

title: CBM BASIC dialect expansion: BASIC 4 (PET) + BASIC 7 (C128) token lists and analyzer parameterization
description: Add the per-dialect extension lists to the shared token data file (BASIC 4: $CC+ disk keywords CONCAT/DOPEN/DCLOSE/RECORD/HEADER/COLLECT/BACKUP/COPY/APPEND/DSAVE/DLOAD/CATALOG/RENAME/SCRATCH/DIRECTORY; BASIC 7: $CC+ single-byte additions PLUS $CE/$FE two-byte prefixed tokens as per-prefix lists building BASIC_V7_TOKEN_CE/_FE enums) and the types: entries in future pet.yaml / c128.yaml machine descriptors. Analyzer side: the line-walker consumes dialect config from the descriptor (which enums, which prefix pages) — per grm-odt.1's (bytes consumed, name) token-lookup interface. GATED ON: pet/c128 machine descriptors existing (separate machine-bringup work, not this bead).
notes:
Filed 2026-07-11 as part of the grm-1.6 epic promotion. Do not start until a second CBM machine descriptor exists.
2026-07-18 user authorized prerequisite order: PET first (grm-1.8), then C128 (grm-1.9), then this dialect-expansion bead. grm-1.9 depends on grm-1.8; this bead now depends on grm-1.9.
Implementation design: preserve C64BasicAnalyzer class identity but select dialect from compiled formats.prg.basic metadata via Retro Machine Map. Metadata names primary GDT token enum, optional ordered CE/FE prefix enums, and PETSCII variant. PET uses BASIC_V4_TOKEN; C128 uses BASIC_V7_TOKEN plus per-prefix enums; C64 explicitly selects BASIC_V2_TOKEN. Generic lookup returns bytes-consumed and preserves invalid/truncated prefix pairs raw. Authoritative VICE petcat behavior also corrects DATA rendering: raw until an unquoted colon, then normal token scanning resumes.
Implemented descriptor-driven CBM BASIC dialect analysis. title: CBM BASIC program support: token data, detokenizing analyzer, dialects 2/4/7
description: Umbrella for making Ghidra genuinely understand tokenized CBM BASIC programs across the dialect family: BASIC 2 (C64/VIC-20), BASIC 4 (PET), BASIC 7 (C128). Pillars: (1) dialect-layered token DATA shipped as .gdt enums (shared $80-$CB base = single transcription; per-dialect extension lists fork above $CB with conflicting values; BASIC 7 adds $CE/$FE two-byte prefixed tokens -> per-prefix enums); (2) a line-walking detokenizing ANALYZER (line-link/line-number structure, token typing outside quoted/REM contexts, detokenized line comments, SYS-entry detection replacing the loader's wrong entry-function-at-load-address wart); (3) DIALECT parameterization — which enum(s)/walker rules apply comes from the machine descriptor, so PET/C128 support = data + descriptor, not new Java; (4) PETSCII rendering (grm-1.4's C64 half) as the string-literal/REM display layer inside detokenized comments. The BASIC analyzer is a primary design-driving CONSUMER of grm-1.4: it needs a Java-callable byte->display-string PETSCII mapping (shifted/unshifted), not just Ghidra charset registration for string search.

title: C64: BASIC line-walking analyzer — detokenized comments, token typing, SYS entry fix
description: Phase 2 of grm-odt (scouted 2026-07-11): new C64BasicAnalyzer extends AbstractAnalyzer (NOT BoardBankAnalyzer — that base is banking-flow specific), gated on C64PrgLoader.NAME + program entry == the descriptor load_target region start (derive 'is BASIC-start PRG' from c64.yaml, do NOT hardcode $0801). Walk classic line structure from load address: 2-byte next-line link, 2-byte line number, tokenized bytes to $00 terminator; program ends at $0000 link. Per line: apply BASIC_V2_TOKEN (phase-1 enum, looked up from the .gdt by name and enumerated into a value->name map — no parallel Java token table, single source of truth) to token bytes OUTSIDE quoted strings; type link+linenum words; EOL/pre comment with the detokenized line text. GOTCHAS from scouting: quote-tracking state machine (PETSCII control/graphics bytes >= $80 inside quotes are NOT tokens); REM lines store the REM token then RAW untokenized text to EOL (must not token-decode); embedded control chars. ALSO FIX pre-existing loader wart: C64PrgLoader marks a function at the raw load address even for BASIC PRGs (line-link bytes, not code) — suppress for BASIC-start PRGs and instead parse a SYS <addr> line if present, marking THAT as the real ML entry (scope SYS parsing explicitly: simple decimal literal only). TEST: tools/banktest-pattern fixture — hand-tokenized 3-4 line .prg (FOR/PRINT/NEXT/SYS 2064) via mkbasictest.py, VerifyBasicTest checks token annotation, line structure, comment text, $0000 terminator, SYS entry; golden dump.
notes: Split from grm-odt 2026-07-11 per scout plan. Depends on phase-1 enum landing (consumes BASIC_V2_TOKEN from the .gdt). Est 1-2 days; medium risk (quote/REM state machine). DIALECT NOTE (2026-07-11): the analyzer must be dialect-parameterized from the start — which token enum(s) it consumes should come from the machine descriptor (c64.yaml -> BASIC_V2_TOKEN; future pet.yaml -> BASIC_V4_TOKEN, c128 -> BASIC_V7_TOKEN + two-byte prefix handling), not hardcoded. BASIC 7 two-byte tokens will need the walker to consume prefix+byte pairs — design the token-lookup interface around (bytes consumed, name) rather than byte->name.
close_reason: C64BasicAnalyzer shipped: line-link walker (shared C64BasicWalker, also used by the loader's BASIC-start sniff), petcat-compatible detokenized PRE comments via PetsciiMapper, link/linenum typed as words, token bytes left undefined (comment carries meaning). Tokens consumed from the .gdt archive DTM (BasicV2TokenLookup; dialect-agnostic (bytesConsumed,name) interface, BASIC-7-prefix-ready). Loader wart fixed: BASIC-start PRGs no longer get a function at the load address; the analyzer marks the SYS <decimal> target instead. TWO CORRECTIONS vs the brief: (1) DATA text IS tokenized in real BASIC 2 (the DATA GOTO gotcha) — no DATA protection branch, verified against petcat/ROM behavior; (2) naive BASIC-start detection false-positived on pure-ML fixtures (stray $00 made one bogus line) — caught by the suite, fixed by requiring the FIRST line to parse cleanly. c64basictest = 11th fixture (B1-B5: exact line renders incl. {clr}/{$a0}/{lgrn}, REM not decoded, SYS entry at 0x842, no function at 0x801); 10 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. Deferred to grm-1.6.1: dialect lists, two-byte prefixes, SYS expressions, variant override (documented in docs/basic-analyzer.md).

title: MMC1: nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring + end-to-end fixture

title: MMC1: findIdioms hook + serial-shift strategy + fixtures
description: Design A + B on parent grm-hsv. (1) New optional BankSwitchStrategy hook findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty; BoardBankAnalyzer runs it per function like findHelpers and folds matches into the switchResults-shaped map (containment property: merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation unchanged). PROTOTYPE THE HOOK SHAPE FIRST — if it doesn't fold into switchResults it ripples back. (2) SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy: bit-7-set write anywhere $8000-$FFFF = reset (prg_mode->3 known, ORs control with $0C); fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR chain walked statically (writes 1-4 null, write 5 full BankState; target from write-5 addr bits 14:13, value reassembled); canonical STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop via findIdioms (sole loop-body write to range + shift of same reg + trip-count 5 or 4+preloop; seed from ONE backward scan of pre-loop load; commit on loop EXIT edge). Params: multi-field-per-target deposit — targets {0:{fields:[{mirroring,shift 0,bits 2},{prg_mode,shift 2,bits 2}]}, 3:{fields:[{prg_bank,shift 0,bits 5}]}} — strategy-opaque, no compiler change. Source loop matcher shapes from REAL commercial MMC1 disassemblies (Metroid/Zelda), not wiki-invented. Fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable (WARNING), CHR-write recognized-but-discarded. Bit-7 partially-known must NOT silently assume reset (explicit fixture).
notes:
Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 3; sub-bead 2 mode-register-class skipped — MMC1 needs none per Design B, MMC3's is co-emitted in select-data).

REAL-GAME IDIOM SURVEY (2026-07-11, scratchpad/mmc1-idioms.md; Zelda1/FF1/Metroid disassemblies verified mapper 1): (1) ALL THREE games use the FULLY UNROLLED 5xSTA/4xLSR chain — NONE use the counted STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop the design treated as canonical. PRIORITY INVERSION: the static unrolled-chain walker is the PRIMARY pattern (covers all surveyed titles); the findIdioms loop matcher is SECONDARY (keep — synthetic fixture + unsurveyed titles — but do not gate acceptance on it). (2) FF1 writes to NON-CANONICAL addresses inside each register's 8K window ($9FFF/$BFFF/$DFFF/$FFF9) — design's 'target from write-5 addr bits 14:13' already handles this; make the fixture cover a non-canonical address. (3) Zelda's reset = ORA #$FF then STA to ALL FOUR register addresses (four consecutive reset writes — each is an independent bit-7 reset, must not confuse the chain walker). (4) FF1 reaches the unrolled helper through a JMP trampoline (JSR SwapPRG_L -> JMP SwapPRG) — check findHelpers/Ghidra thunk handling follows it. (5) Value provenance: Zelda = immediates (easy); FF1 = value computed via ROL/AND/ORA well before the JSR (backward scan may fail -> honest WARNING); Metroid = DEFERRED mailbox (call sites write a pending var; a per-frame dispatcher does the real writes with AND/ORA-composed value -> unresolvable -> WARNING, expected degrade; the dispatcher itself is the switch site, call sites are not). A pure peephole matcher misses real call sites in 2 of 3 games — acceptance expectations for hsv.2 should reflect that (fixed windows + reset-dance prg_mode=3 still give most of the value).
close_reason: SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy landed with ZERO engine changes — the planned findIdioms hook proved unnecessary: runDataflow probes computeSwitch on every instruction, so the strategy claims the counted loop's closing BNE as the switch site and the commit flows through the existing switchResults fold (strictly better containment than the hook). Primary recognizer = survey-informed unrolled 5xSTA/LSR bidirectional chain walk (breaks on non-chain instr, control-flow join into any link, X/Y store, RMW); write-5 target from ITS OWN addr bits 14:13 (FF1 $FFF9 non-canonical fixture-proven); quad-resets classified independently before chain logic. Key empirical fix: StoredValueScanner treats shifts as opaque, so preceded-by-LSR-A stores get bit 7 known-clear STRUCTURALLY. Loop matcher: trip-5 STA/LSR/DEX|DEY/BNE, poison suppression by delegating body-membership to the same branch matcher (recognizers cannot disagree). Synthetic board nes-serialtest.yaml on mapper 222 (101 is NOT safe — NESdev duplicate-assignment, not reserved); 4-value prg_mode layouts; 32K modes mapped PRG[0] pending evalExpr shift/divide (grm-hsv.2 flag). nesserialtest = 9th fixture, 16 criteria incl. honest WARNING paths (table seed, partial bit-7 not misread as reset). SUITE OK, 8 pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: MMC3: select-data strategy (select+prg_mode co-emission, even/odd-over-range), fixture
description: Design A + Design B resolution (a) on parent grm-6a7: new SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy. Even-address store in $8000-$9FFE range = bank select: resolve byte via existing scanner, deposit bits 0-2 into 'select' field AND bit 6 into 'prg_mode' (co-emission from the same recovered byte; keeps first-match-wins engine loop unchanged). Odd-address store = data: if inState select fully known and targeted field tracked (6->r6, 7->r7) overwrite only that field; select unknown -> poison r6 AND r7; select known 0-5 (CHR) -> leave r6/r7 UNTOUCHED (per-frame CHR swaps must not poison PRG — THE easy-to-get-wrong case, fixture it); data unrecoverable with known select -> only targeted field unknown. notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11. Parent grm-6a7 design sub-beads 2+3 folded together per design.

title: Release-build strategy on GitHub (Actions matrix across supported Ghidra versions)
description: Set up automated release builds for ghidra-retro-machines on GitHub. Reference sketch = kylewlacy/GhidraNes (.github/workflows/): a reusable _build.yml (on: workflow_call) building with a matrix of ~19 Ghidra versions (10.3 through 12.1) via the antoniovazquezblanco/setup-ghidra@v2.1.0 action (installs Ghidra + exports GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var), temurin Java 21, gradle -PGHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=..., then renames dist/*.zip to ghidra_<ver>_<sha>_<date>_<name>.zip and uploads as artifacts; release.yml triggers on tag push v*, calls _build, downloads merged artifacts, and creates a DRAFT release with gh release create --generate-notes + gh release upload; ci.yml reuses the same _build on ordinary pushes. Adaptations needed for GRM: (1) our build.gradle checks the GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var FIRST, which is exactly what setup-ghidra sets — so CI works naturally, no -P needed; (2) matrix should start narrow (12.1.x we actually support) and grow deliberately — sleigh compile + GDT JavaExec tasks may not be version-portable as far back as GhidraNes goes; (3) consider running tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh (analyzeHeadless, works on ubuntu) as a CI quality gate before release assets are published. TRIGGER MECHANISM IS OPEN: user finds tag pushing clunky as a downstream fork — evaluate alternatives: workflow_dispatch with a version input (workflow tags + drafts the release itself, one button in the UI), 'release: published' trigger (draft the release in the UI first, action builds+attaches assets), or push-to-release-branch. Pick whichever makes cutting a release a single low-ceremony step.
design: TRIGGER DECIDED (user, 2026-07-12): workflow_dispatch to start. release.yml takes a version input (e.g. '0.3.0'), runs the _build matrix, then tags and creates the DRAFT release itself (gh release create --generate-notes + upload assets) -- one button in the Actions UI, no local tag push. Tag creation happens IN the workflow from the dispatched ref, so the fork's local clone never needs to push tags. Keep the trigger swappable: structure release.yml so switching to 'release: published' later is just changing the on: block + reading the version from the release tag instead of the input. ci.yml on ordinary pushes reuses the same workflow_call _build.
notes:
Requested by user 2026-07-11. GhidraNes workflow files fetched and verified 2026-07-11 (repo kylewlacy/GhidraNes, default branch main). setup-ghidra action needs auth_token: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid API rate limits when downloading Ghidra releases.

VERSION-SUPPORT POLICY (user, 2026-07-11): Ghidra will install/keep using an extension built against a different version — it does NOT proactively check compatibility, so a mismatched build may work or break depending on API drift. For the extensions we care about (mostly loaders), the biggest breakage so far is the 11->12 breaking change to the Loader load() method signature. HARD FLOOR = Ghidra 12.0: we will NOT support the <=11 load() API — working around it is a pain (see how GhidraNes contorts to span both). So the matrix may be a small subset, possibly even one build serving several versions. PROCEDURE: check back-support starting at 12.0 and work FORWARD, running the banktest suite against each release to find the true minimum version that works (compat = suite passes, not just compiles). If we find critical dependencies on behavior introduced post-12.0 (candidates to check: ImporterSettings record shape, CommentType enum, SleighCompile invocation, MemoryBlockUtils signatures), DISCUSS each with the user before deciding to work around it vs. raising the floor — do not silently add compat shims.

title: Reconstruct testing procedure for safe parallelization (isolated trees/Ghidra infra, efficient rebuilds)
description: Today the build/test loop is serialized through shared mutable infrastructure, which makes parallel subagent work (now the standing preference) risky: (1) the built extension is installed by delete+unzip into the single per-user Extensions dir (%APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/Extensions/) — two agents installing different builds clobber each other, and an open Ghidra GUI locks the jar; (2) tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh uses shared work/project dirs under one tree; (3) a single working tree means concurrent code edits collide. Rework so N agents can build+test independently: git worktrees (or EnterWorktree) per agent; per-agent Ghidra 'installation' or at least per-agent extension install + headless project dirs — investigate whether analyzeHeadless can point at an alternate extensions dir (e.g. ghidra.user.settings.dir / -vmargs user-dir override) so one shared read-only Ghidra install serves many isolated setting dirs, which is far cheaper than duplicating the 1GB+ install; per-agent scratch/work dirs keyed by worktree. Constraint: keep the rebuild loop reasonably fast — full gradle buildExtension per iteration is already the dominant cost, so prefer solutions that share gradle caches across worktrees and avoid re-unzipping more than needed. Deliverable: updated run-banktest.sh / helper script(s) + documented procedure agents can follow without stepping on each other.
notes: Requested by user 2026-07-11. Motivated by the new user-level 'use subagents whenever it makes sense' policy — current single-install test flow is the main thing forcing serialization. Remember headless gotcha: project path must contain no dot-prefixed path element.
close_reason: Landed: tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh (one-command build -> per-worktree isolated extension install under build/ghidra-home via -Dapplication.settingsdir/-Dapplication.cachedir + GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS -> suite), run-banktest.sh BANKTEST_SETTINGS_BASE hook, CLAUDE.md Build & Test procedure. Verified: main-tree SUITE OK, stamp-skip on second run, isolated settings dir demonstrably used (pass/fail tracked isolated zip while shared %APPDATA% copy present), two worktrees ran concurrently both SUITE OK. Bonus fixes the worktree smoke test flushed out: settings.gradle pins rootProject.name (worktree dir name broke loader discovery via jar name); build.gradle buildExtension now depends on buildPetsciiMap (fresh checkouts shipped a zip missing data/petscii.map -> silently broken C64 BASIC detokenizer; was masked by stale artifact in main tree).

title: C64 BASIC tokens as a Ghidra enum (or similar data type)
description: Idea parked for later: represent the C64 BASIC V2 token set ($80 END ... $CB GO, plus the two-byte extensions if we ever cover BASIC 7/other dialects) as a data type the extension ships — most likely an enum in the generated .gdt (via the YAML types: mechanism / headless GDT builder), so tokenized BASIC program text in a PRG/disk image can be annotated readably in the listing. Open questions: plain enum vs. a typedef'd byte with an analyzer that walks BASIC line links (line-link/line-number/token-stream structure) and comments/detokenizes; where it hooks in (C64PrgLoader for BASIC-start PRGs?); whether symbols/types in machines/c64.yaml is the right home. No urgency — capture only.
design: PLAN (scouted 2026-07-11, read-only exploration). PHASE 1 = THIS BEAD: (1) GdtBuilder (tools/gdtbuilder/src/main/java/gdtbuilder/GdtBuilder.java) supports only kind: struct|flags; add third kind 'enum' — new branch in buildTypes() + buildEnum() mirroring buildFlags() but reading values: [{value,name,comment}] with EnumDataType(name,size) + add(name,value,comment); no bit-shift logic; topo-sort/archive plumbing untouched. (2) machines/c64.yaml types: add BASIC_V2_TOKEN, kind: enum, size: 1 — 76 contiguous tokens $80 END .. $CB GO, hand-transcribed with provenance comment (C64 Programmer's Reference Guide / c64-wiki token table; same 'inline seed' pattern as the KERNAL symbols). No gaps, no 2-byte extensions in stock V2 (BASIC 7 dialects out of scope). (3) docs/SCHEMA.md: document enum kind alongside flags (bitmask vs sequential distinction); check MAP_FORMAT.md types: section.
